# FF8 Accessibility Mod — Changelog

Newest on top. Each entry begins with a `## vMAJOR.MINOR.BUILD` heading followed by a blank line and the commit message body. The push utility (`Utilities/push_to_github.ps1`) reads the top heading to determine the version being pushed and uses everything between that heading and the next `## v` heading as the commit message body.

The version in the top heading **must** match `FF8OPC_VERSION` in `src/ff8_accessibility.h`. The push utility refuses to push if they don't.

Older entries (pre-v0.15.12.0) are preserved in `CHANGELOG_HISTORY.md`.

## v0.131.8

**THE LADDER AND AUTO-DRIVE WORK IS DONE; THIS BUILD TAKES OUT THE SCAFFOLDING IT WAS BUILT ON.** No behaviour change is intended. Every removal below is a symbol nothing in the shipped mod reads any more, or a diagnostic that has already given up its answer. **THE MODE-WATCH TRACE IS GONE.** v0.126.0 and v0.127.0 carried two tables on the engine's own step path -- a first-sighting bitmask over every movement mode a ladder step was played in, and a table of every non-climb mode transition. They existed to answer one question: what movement mode does crroof1's descent set? v0.128.0 answered it by reading the script instead. **None** -- the descent runs no ladder opcode at all, animates in place and teleports, which is why nothing the trace could ever have seen would have named it. The finding is written into ladder_cue_model.inl where the reasoning lives; the code that found it is deleted, along with `LadderTransitions`, `LadderTransitionIsNew`, `LADDER_TRANSITION_CAP`, `LadderModeFirstSighting`, `s_ladderEngineModes`, `s_ladderTransitions`, `s_ladderLastMode` and their two `Log::Field` sites. A diagnostic that has stopped diagnosing is just noise on a hot path. **THE MODE-SWAP CONSTANTS GO WITH THE FIX THEY BELONGED TO.** v0.126.0 sounded the descent by presenting the player's movement mode byte as 3 for the length of the call; v0.131.0 withdrew that, because it meant writing the entity from AccessibilityThread and the game caught it half-written and stranded Aaron on the ascent's two-triangle landing. `LADDER_MODE_OFFSET`, `LADDER_MODE_SOUNDS_AS` and `LadderModeSoundsAsLadder` were that fix's vocabulary and nothing has called them since. The v0.126.0 comment block stays but now says, at the top, that its fix was withdrawn and where to read why -- a block that describes a reverted approach as if it were current is worse than no comment. **THE OPCODE TABLE BECOMES EVIDENCE INSTEAD OF CODE.** `LADDER_OPCODE_FIRST/LAST/COUNT`, `LadderOpcodeIsMove` and `LadderOpcodeMode` encoded the four ladder opcodes and the movement modes their handlers set. That table is how the silent roof ladder was found and it is still true -- but since v0.130.0 the cue is driven by the script's own PREQEW wait and by the mode the handler leaves behind, so nothing asks which opcode ran. It is written down in full in the file's header comment, where it cannot rot into a second source of truth that some later build starts dispatching on again. **THE MOD NO LONGER PRETENDS IT MIGHT CALL THE ENGINE'S STEP ROUTINE.** `s_ladderStepSound`, `LadderStepSound()` and `s_ladderStepChecked` stored a function pointer to sub_00520260 that has not been called through since v0.131.0 moved the cue onto the leaf sound player sub_0046B2A0. `s_ladderSelfCall` guarded re-entrancy on a path that can no longer exist -- the mod cannot land back in its own hook when it never calls the hooked routine. `LadderStepFoot` computed an alternating foot argument for a routine the mod does not call; sub_0046B2A0 has no feet, it takes a sound id. `s_ladderModeSwapped` was a bool held at false so a log line could read it, and the log line went in v0.131.0. **What stays is `LADDER_STEP_ADDR`, `LADDER_STEP_SIG` and `LadderStepSigMatches`**, because the prologue must still be verified before MinHook overwrites it -- the read-only measurement hook is how the 469 ms cadence gets learned from the game. `InstallLadderStepHook` now checks the signature directly and says what a failure actually costs: the cadence measurement, not the cue. **AND THE v0.131.7 EXIT FILTER SAID ITS PIECE FOUR TIMES A SECOND.** The 23:20 log has seven `JSM exit ... dropped` lines repeated four times within seconds, because `InjectMapExits` had no once-per-field gate. It could not borrow `s_scanTraced`: `RefreshCatalog` sets that true at the end of its entity scan and calls `InjectMapExits` afterwards, so the injector has never once seen it false. It gets its own flag, `s_mapExitTraced`, reset on the same field load. The verdict is a property of the field's script -- identical on every rebuild -- so saying it once is saying it completely, and a reader looking for why an exit is missing finds one line instead of a wall. **TESTING.** tests/ladder_cue_test.cpp drops its assertions on the removed opcode table and mode-swap helpers and replaces them with the property those helpers used to serve: the mod sounds mode 2 even though the engine's own branch will not, which is the whole of why the descent is audible. A mutant that narrowed `LadderModeIsClimb` back to the engine's 3-and-4 would silence the way down and previously passed. tests/ladder_cue_compile.cpp keeps its real low-mapped entity block and its "the movement mode byte is untouched" assertion -- that one is the guard against the stranding bug and it matters more now that the swap's vocabulary is gone. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** nothing new. This is a cleanup build, so the useful test is that the last one still holds -- crroof1's roof ladder should sound in both directions, and the lift on crsphi1 and crtower1 should still drive in a couple of seconds.

## v0.131.7

v0.131.7 (#centra). **THE LIFT WORKS, AND READING THE LOG END TO END TURNED UP THE NEXT ONE.** v0.131.6 in the 22:16 run: `cat0 ent3 model=6 type=NPC name='Lift'`, then `goal tri 131 from the entity's own placement, not a coordinate search`, `A*+funnel path: 10 waypoints from tri 71 to 131`, `stopped: Arrived.` -- three seconds, first attempt, on crsphi1. And again on crtower1 at 22:17:32, goal tri 128, `Arrived.` Both the naming and the goal-triangle fix hold. **BUT crtower2 LISTS ONE DOORWAY FOUR TIMES, AND THE FOURTH REFUSES TO MOVE.** The 22:17:00 catalog: `cat5 JSM ent9 'Exit to Centra Ruins 8' pos=(1451,-383)`, `cat6 JSM ent11` same name same position, `cat7 JSM ent12` same again, `cat8 JSM ent17` same name and **pos=(0,0)** -- and Aaron pressed drive on that fourth one four times: `[drive] REFUSED -- target validation failed: catIdx=8/11 entityIdx=-317`. **THE FIRST THREE ARE PARTY MEMBERS.** crtower2's MAPJUMP to field 283 lives in every character's own script -- squall, zell, irvine, rinoa, selphie and quistis each carry an identical copy at (1451,-383), because that is the code that moves whichever of them is walking. The three in the active party are already filtered as party members; the three who are NOT in the party are not, so a character who is not even in the game contributed an exit to the catalog. A character's script is not a doorway, whether or not that character happens to be along. **THE FOURTH HAS NO POSITION.** director0's MAPJUMP is real code and it is nowhere -- no coordinates, no walkmesh triangle. The drive refuses it, correctly. Listing it offers the player something that cannot work, and for a blind player an entry that refuses is worse than one that is absent, because the only way to discover it is broken is to try it. **NEITHER RULE CAN HIDE A REAL EXIT:** a doorway the player can walk to has a position, and it is not stored inside a playable character. Disc-wide the two rules touch 214 party-member exit entities across 124 fields and 465 position-less ones across 361 -- crtower2 is not a special case, it is the one he happened to be standing in. **ALSO:** `[drive] stopped: (null)` at 22:16:53. StopAutoDrive(nullptr) is deliberate -- it means "release the keys and say nothing", used on a field change -- and the announce was correctly guarded, so nothing was ever spoken. Only the log printed `(null)`, which is a trap for whoever reads it next; it now says what actually happened. **TESTING.** The four-entry fixture is asserted as a whole -- of crtower2's four listings for one doorway, exactly one survives -- and each rule separately. The placement test is bounded on the side that matters: (0,0) is a legal coordinate, so a field whose origin is walkable keeps its exit as long as it has a triangle, and coordinates without a triangle are a placement too. The real doorway at (1451,-383) on triangle 37 is asserted to survive first, because an exit the player cannot see is worse than a duplicate. tests/catalog_harness.cpp gained the same party-sym list it does not otherwise include; its 60-fixture golden is unchanged. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** crtower2 -- Centra Ruins 9. The exit to Centra Ruins 8 should appear once, and driving to it should work rather than refusing.

## v0.131.6

v0.131.6 (#centra). **THE LIFT, AND WHY THE DRIVE COULD NOT REACH IT.** Aaron: "I had to do the drive twice for it to actually complete. There was also an earlier field where you have to walk onto an automated lift, but the lift was identified as an NPC and auto-drive wouldn't actually trigger it." Read end to end rather than grepped, the 21:01 log shows those are one event, on crsphi1 -- Centra Ruins 7 -- and it is the only drive in the whole session that failed. `21:01:06 GPS Started: NPC dist=1003`, `21:01:08 drive started toward ent3`, `21:01:14 stopped: Cancelled`, `21:01:16 GPS Started: NPC dist=400` -- **and no drive line at all after the second target**. He walked onto the lift himself at 21:01:25. My previous summary counted that session as "10 drives started, 9 arrivals, 0 give-ups" and never noticed which one it was, because I read greps instead of the log. **THE LIFT IS FOUR TRIANGLES.** crsphi1 has five walkmesh islands and four of them share a single XY footprint at different heights: tri 131 at z 942, tri 149 at 1561, tri 122 at 2231, tri 140 at 2949. That is the lift platform drawn once per stop it makes. The drive's goal-triangle search runs over the target's COORDINATES, so it could return any of the four -- and it returned **122, two thousand units up, on an island the player has no way to reach**: `startTri 71 and goalTri 122 are on disconnected walkmesh islands; straight-line fallback`, then `A* No path from tri 64 to tri 122`, then a straight-line approach that parked him four hundred units short of an entity whose talk radius is 128. tri 131 is on the player's own island and was walkable the whole time -- BFS over the field's own mesh confirms 71 to 131 connected, 71 to 122 not. **THE MOD ALREADY HAD THE RIGHT ANSWER AND THREW IT AWAY.** The catalog reads every entity's live walkmesh triangle each refresh and logged this one in the same second the drive failed: `[dedup] ent3 tri=131`. So an entity target now supplies its own goal triangle and no search is done. The engine's statement of where a thing is standing beats any lookup over its coordinates, and it costs a read rather than a scan of the mesh. Gateways, trigger lines and JSM sentinels keep the coordinate search -- they have no entity placement to ask, which is precisely why v0.119.0 gave them a Z to search with and left entity targets on the 2D one. Same family as that build; the half of it that was missed. **AND IT IS CALLED "LIFT" NOW, NOT "NPC".** `stone` is catalogued as an interactive entity on exactly two fields disc-wide -- crsphi1 and crtower1, the lift's two stops, both classified Map Exit by the scanner -- and is a Background everywhere else it appears (crtower3, eccway12, gnroad1, tvglen2), which the catalog never surfaces. Checked against all 900 fields rather than inferred from the word, which is the bar this project sets before trusting a SYM. **TESTING.** The rule is asserted against the real fixture: ent3 on tri 131 supplies 131, and the three non-entity sentinel ranges supply nothing. Triangle 0 is refused because that is the engine's "not on the mesh" value -- pathing to it during a transition would send the drive somewhere arbitrary -- and an id at or past the mesh size is refused rather than indexed, in both the boundary case and a wild one. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** Centra Ruins 7, target the Lift. It should be announced as "Lift", and the drive should path to it on your own island and arrive rather than stopping short.

## v0.131.5

v0.131.5 (#centra). **THE CLOCK FIX WORKED AND THE REMAINING FAILURE IS NOW ONE DRIVE, ONE MECHANISM.** The 20:47 run against v0.131.4: pins fell from 49 to 12, failed sweeps from 20 to 2, nine of the twelve pins cleared at the first probe angle, both ladder climbs sounded, and the drives to the ladder up and the ladder down both arrived cleanly. What is left is a single drive -- 20:50:20, crroof1's ramp, from the foot of the ladder to the field exit -- which ran forty-one seconds, six recoveries, and gave up 511 units short. **AND IT IS NOT A STEERING PROBLEM.** The drive-vec lines say what happens: `t=30 pp=(1178,-513) wpRaw=(1343,-58)` -- first waypoint, north -- `t=60 pp=(1357,-96) wpRaw=(1459,-19)` -- second, further north -- `t=90 pp=(1232,-373) wpRaw=(1334,-672)`, which is **the final target**. Four waypoints, and between two log lines it went from following the second to having none left, so from then on it steered straight at the exit across ground the walkmesh does not connect: jammed at tri 19, re-pathed, ran back north, and did the whole thing again. The oscillation verdicts on that drive read "1072 units walked, 27 units gained" and "1248 walked, 35 gained" -- a five-hundred-unit lap, not a shuffle. **THE CHAIN-ADVANCE IS SOUND; THE OVERSHOOT RULE BESIDE IT RUNS AWAY.** Advancing through waypoints stops at the first one not reached. But the overshoot rule -- "we got close and are now moving away, so count it as reached" -- `continue`s, and can therefore consume the rest of the list in one tick. **crroof1's ramp is a switchback**, and on a path that doubles back, moving away from the waypoint behind you is precisely what walking the next leg looks like, so every remaining waypoint reads as overshot at once. **A WAYPOINT GENUINELY REACHED STILL CHAINS**, because arriving at several in a row is real and common on a tight funnel. An overshoot is an inference, and one inference per tick is enough: the next tick makes the same call again if it is still true, and the drive will have moved in between. **TESTING.** The rule is asserted directly -- first overshoot of a tick advances, second does not -- and then against the shape of the failure: a four-waypoint list cannot be crossed off by one tick's inference, which is exactly what the log recorded. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** the ramp drive from the ladder foot to the exit, the one that gave up. The line to watch is `wpRaw` in the drive-vec entries -- it should walk down the waypoint list rather than jumping to the target -- and the drive should either arrive or give up on the pathing rather than after forty seconds of laps.

## v0.131.4

v0.131.4 (#centra). **THE MONITOR WAS READING THE WRONG CLOCK, AND THE LOG CONTRADICTS ITSELF IN ADJACENT LINES.** At 20:14:58 it declared `pinned -- 0 units walked in the last 32 ticks`, while the drive's own diagnostic thirty ticks either side of it has the player covering ninety-nine units: `t=60 pp=(4468,-91)` then `t=90 pp=(4456,8)`. Both cannot be true of the same second, and the drive-vec line is the one reading the player's position directly. **A DRIVE TICK IS NOT A GAME FRAME.** UpdateAutoDrive runs on AccessibilityThread, which polls faster than the game renders, so a run of consecutive ticks routinely sees the same position -- not because the player is stuck but because the engine has not stepped him yet. Thirty-two of those ticks can be a fraction of a second of game time, and a fraction of a second of standing still is what every walking character does between frames. **THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE 20:13 RUN'S BEHAVIOUR:** forty-nine pins, twenty of them sweeping every heading and finding nothing, seventeen oscillation verdicts, two give-ups. Most of those were never pins. The verdicts were right about the numbers they were handed and the numbers covered no time. **SO THE WINDOW IS SAMPLED ON THE CLOCK NOW** -- one sample per 50 ms, thirty-two of them, a fixed 1.6 seconds however fast the mod happens to be polling -- and the thresholds describe that second and a half rather than an unknown number of frames: twelve units walked is unambiguously stuck, and three hundred walked for sixty gained is unambiguously a loop, where a character moving at even a third of normal pace covers several hundred. **v0.131.3's FIX STANDS AND IS CONFIRMED BY THIS RUN:** zero `180 degrees` escapes in the whole log, against the previous run's turn-around-and-give-up. The escape now only claims success when it makes ground toward the target; this build stops it being ASKED to escape from things that were not pins. **TESTING.** The sampling rule is pinned as a pure function of two timestamps -- first sample always due, same millisecond never, one tick short never, the interval itself yes -- so a whole window can be exercised without a clock. The window is asserted to cover at least a second of real time (or "between frames" reads as "stuck" again) and no more than three (or a genuine pin is endured too long), and the thresholds are asserted against the window rather than restated: the stall bar under twenty units, and an oscillation required to walk at least five times what it gains. The crroof1 two-cycle and the crtower3 wall fixtures still answer as each other's negative. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** the same routes. The number to watch is the count of `pinned` lines -- it should drop from forty-nine to a handful, and the ones that remain should be real.

## v0.131.3

v0.131.3 (#centra). **"UNPINNED AT 180 DEGREES." v0.131.1 AND .2 MADE ONE DRIVE WORSE, AND THIS IS THE LINE THAT SAYS SO.** The 20:04:09 drive -- crroof1's ramp, from the foot of the ladder back to the field exit -- thrashed for forty-one seconds and gave up 512 units short. The log shows the escape succeeding over and over while getting nowhere: `20:04:12 pinned, sweeping from 30 / unpinned at -30`, `20:04:12 pinned, sweeping from 60 / unpinned at -60`, `20:04:13 pinned, sweeping from 90 / unpinned at 90`, `20:04:13 pinned, sweeping from -90 / unpinned at -135`, `20:04:15 oscillating -- 496 units walked, 25 units gained`, and at 20:04:45, **`unpinned at 180 degrees`**. **THE ESCAPE'S SUCCESS TEST WAS "HAS HE MOVED 45 UNITS", AND WALKING BACKWARDS PASSES IT.** So the sweep turned him around, declared victory, held the reversal for three quarters of a second, and pinned again facing the wall -- with the oscillation detector then firing on the resulting shuffle and switching off the trigger-line avoidance. Three mechanisms, each doing exactly what it was told, adding up to forty-one seconds of nothing. That is my regression, introduced in v0.131.1 and made more persistent by v0.131.2's hold. **AN ESCAPE IS ONLY AN ESCAPE IF IT MAKES GROUND TOWARD WHERE THE DRIVE WAS TRYING TO GO.** The movement is now measured against the direction the drive actually wanted -- the un-rotated steer, which is that direction by construction -- and a probe that moves him somewhere useless keeps sweeping instead of claiming success. Sliding along a wall at 30 or 60 degrees passes; a right-angle squeeze that gains nothing does not; a reversal never does. **AND 135 AND 180 ARE GONE FROM THE SWEEP ENTIRELY.** Walking backwards to reach a goal in front of you is the pathfinder's job, not the steering's. The sweep is now the six headings that can actually help -- 30, -30, 60, -60, 90, -90 -- and one that exhausts them hands back to the recovery ladder to re-path, which is the correct escalation and was always what should have happened instead of turning around. **TESTING.** The success test is asserted against the real geometry of the failure: straight at the target and both 45-degree wall-slides are useful; a right-angle squeeze, a 135-degree back-off and the literal 180 that the 20:04:45 line recorded are not. Movement has to be real as well as useful -- five units toward the target is not an escape, and the threshold itself is not past it -- so the drive cannot claim a win from the drift of leaning on a wall. Every probe angle is asserted to be at most a right angle, which is the shape of the fix rather than a restatement of the list. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **NOT FIXED, AND NOT NEW:** crroof1's ramp is a genuine pathing problem that predates all of this -- the same stretch ping-ponged at 16:52:49-16:53:04 under v0.126.0, before any progress monitor existed. This build stops the escape machinery from making that worse and hands the ramp back to recovery instead of walking away from the target; it does not make the ramp itself route better. That is the next one worth taking on its own. **TO TEST:** the ramp drive from the ladder foot to the exit. It may still need recoveries, but the log should no longer contain a `180 degrees` escape, and a give-up should come from the pathing rather than after forty seconds of turning around.

## v0.131.2

v0.131.2 (#centra). **THE RUN WORKED -- AND SHOWED THE SWEEP DOING THE SAME WORK SEVEN TIMES.** The 19:46-19:47 log is what v0.131.1 was for: six fields driven end to end, **one** recovery in the whole session, zero cancellations, zero give-ups, arrival at the roof ladder at t=0.99, and both climbs sounding (19 steps up, 9 down). The oscillation verdict fired twice and cleared it; the pin verdict fired seven times and cleared every one in under a second. But look at what it cleared: `19:46:27 pinned, sweeping from 30` / `19:46:27 unpinned at 30` / `19:46:28 pinned, sweeping from 30` / `19:46:28 unpinned at -30` / `19:46:29 pinned, sweeping from 30`. Seven pins in ninety seconds, every sweep restarting from the top. **v0.131.1's OWN ENTRY CLAIMED THIS WAS ALREADY FIXED** -- "the moment the player actually moves it stops and KEEPS the angle that worked, so he slides along the wall instead of turning straight back into it" -- and the code did the other thing: it dropped the rotation the instant he moved, so the next frame steered back into the wall and he re-pinned half a second later. The claim described the right behaviour. This build is the code catching up to it. **THE WINNING ANGLE IS NOW HELD** for three quarters of a second after the unpin -- long enough to clear the corner rather than just the contact. **AND A PIN THAT LANDS INSIDE THAT HOLD IS THE SAME WALL,** so the sweep resumes at the NEXT angle instead of re-trying the one that just bought half a second; a pin that arrives later is a new obstacle and starts from the top. Each attempt begins with more information than the last, which is the whole difference between a search and a loop. **TESTING.** The resume rule is asserted from every starting point, including wrapping off the end of the sweep and the no-previous-winner case, plus a termination check -- a resume rule that could cycle forever would turn the search back into the loop it exists to replace. The hold is bounded on both sides: longer than a single probe, so it cannot expire into an immediate re-pin, and under a second, so the drive is never walking at an angle to its waypoint for a stretch the player would feel. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** the same route. The drives should still complete; the difference to look for in the log is fewer `pinned` lines, and the ones that remain sweeping from something other than 30 degrees.

## v0.131.1

v0.131.1 (#centra). **THE LADDER IS DONE. THE TWO STUCK DRIVES IN THE SAME LOG ARE NOT THE SAME FAILURE, AND THE RECOVERY LADDER TREATED THEM IDENTICALLY -- WHICH IS WHY NEITHER GOT BETTER.** Aaron: "that worked! Only issue now is the auto-drive getting stuck when headed to that ladder... there was another part where I got stuck as well when headed to Ruins 7. See if you can make object avoidance / getting out of being stuck more intelligent." The 19:15 log has one of each, with opposite signatures. **crroof1, 19:15:26-19:15:36, tri 34 -- AN OSCILLATION.** The player alternates between exactly two positions thirty units apart, forever: `pp=(1476,-187) trigRedir=1 finalDelta=(16.9,7.3) kb=DR` then `pp=(1498,-167) trigRedir=1 finalDelta=(-8.9,-3.9) kb=UL`. He is moving the whole time. The trigger-line avoidance projects the steer PARALLEL to a line it does not want him to cross, and the tangential component flips sign each time he crosses back -- a textbook two-cycle. Five recoveries, every one of them nudging perpendicular to a corridor edge, which is orthogonal to the thing actually going wrong, and then he cancelled. **crtower3, 19:15:07-19:15:14, tri 89 -- A HARD PIN.** `pp=(-1305,-34) trigRedir=0 moveDist=0 lX=989` for seven seconds. He is not moving at all; the commanded direction is into geometry, and the four-mode perpendicular escape guesses at which way is clear rather than finding out. **SO: ONE MONITOR, TWO VERDICTS, EACH WITH THE REMEDY THAT MATCHES IT.** Path length and net displacement over a half-second window separate them completely -- oscillating is a long path with no net distance, pinned is no path at all -- and both are read from the player's own position history, which costs nothing and cannot be wrong about whether he is getting anywhere. **OSCILLATING: SUSPEND THE THING DOING IT.** The trigger-line avoidance goes off for three seconds and the drive steers straight at its waypoint. Suspended, not deleted -- three seconds is enough to break a two-cycle and the avoidance is still wanted for the rest of the drive. **PINNED: SWEEP THE HEADING, DO NOT GUESS AT IT.** Against a wall the mod knows one thing for certain: the direction it is asking for does not work. So it stops asking for that one and tries the rest -- 30, -30, 60, -60, 90, -90, 135, -135, 180 -- nearest first, alternating sides so a wall on either hand is found in two probes rather than four, twelve ticks each, whole sweep under two seconds. The moment the player actually moves it stops and KEEPS the angle that worked, so he slides along the wall instead of turning straight back into it. A sweep that finds nothing hands back to the recovery ladder and says so in the log, because a heading that works nowhere is a pathing problem and not a steering one. **TESTING.** tests/drive_progress_test.cpp replays both episodes tick by tick from the positions the drive actually recorded: the crroof1 two-cycle asserted oscillating and explicitly NOT pinned, the crtower3 wall asserted pinned and explicitly NOT oscillating -- each other's negative, which is the whole distinction. A straight run across a field and a slow two-units-a-tick final approach to a ladder trip neither, so the remedy cannot fire on a drive that is simply working or about to arrive. A window one sample short answers no to both questions and the sample that fills it answers yes, so the first half-second of every drive is not read as a stall. The sweep is asserted to widen, to pair each angle with its mirror, to rotate nothing for an index outside it, and to preserve magnitude and perpendicularity against the real crtower3 heading. **SIZE.** field_nav_autodrive.inl went over the 80 KB gate again; the 1.3 KB [drive-vec] format key moved to field_nav_autodrive_helpers.inl, leaving 1231 bytes free rather than the 36 the change alone would have left. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** drive to the roof ladder from the field entry, the run that ping-ponged at tri 34, and to Ruins 7 through the crtower3 corner that pinned. `grep drive logs/ff8_field.log` will name which verdict fired and what it did.

## v0.131.0

v0.131.0 (#centra). **THE MOD STRANDED HIM, AND IT DID IT BY WRITING ENGINE STATE FROM ITS OWN THREAD.** Aaron: "heard sound climbing down but once I climbed down I couldn't move." The descent finally sounds -- v0.130.0's PREQEW mechanism worked exactly as designed, 9 steps, armed and released by the script's own wait -- and then he could not walk. The log says precisely where he was: `zone-filter active: player tri=1, 2/80 triangles reachable`, at (637,-684). **Tris 0 and 1 are a two-triangle island at z 19296, and crroof1's party method 4 -- the ASCENT -- is `LADDER MOVE 0x026 -> (661,-622,19296)`.** He finished a DESCENT standing on the ascent's mid-ladder landing, an island with no walkable connection to anything on the field. That is not a story event and it is not the game's doing. **v0.126.0 PUT HIM THERE.** To make the engine's step wrapper take its ladder branch, that build wrote the player's movement mode byte at +0x23C to 3 for the length of the call and put it back afterwards -- written as though the two happened between one engine frame and the next. They do not. FieldNavigation::Update() runs on **AccessibilityThread**, the mod's own thread (src/dinput8.cpp), while the game updates its entities on its own. Sample that byte inside the window -- nine to nineteen times per climb, every 469 ms -- and the engine sees a player on a ladder and moves him toward the ladder destination still sitting in +0x1B4/+0x1B8/+0x1BC from the last ladder move. On this field that is (661,-622,19296), and that is where he was standing. **SO THE CUE STOPS TOUCHING THE ENTITY.** sub_00520260 is only a wrapper: it decides which sound a footfall should make and hands it to the sound player. The mod already knows the answer for a ladder -- sound id **0x3F**, read out of the branch itself at 0x005203BB -- so it now calls the player directly and skips the wrapper entirely: `sub_0046B2A0(0x3F, 0x400000, pan, volume)`, cdecl, four arguments, exactly as 0x005203BB pushes them. That routine is pure audio -- it maps the selector to a channel, stores the id, calls the mixer -- with **no entity pointer, no movement mode, no bone lookup and no projection**, and therefore nothing the game thread can catch half-written. Volume is 0x77, the loudest the engine's own distance attenuation can ever produce (0x7F minus its minimum term of 8), so the cue can never be louder than a real footstep; pan is the centre value all four engine call sites pass. Twelve bytes of the player's prologue are checked before the mod calls through the address, as the step routine's fifteen already were. **THE READ-ONLY HOOK STAYS.** sub_00520260 is still hooked to measure the engine's real cadence -- that hook runs on the GAME's thread, writes nothing, and is how 469 ms was measured in the first place. The distinction this build is built on is not "hook versus call", it is **read versus write**. **TESTING.** The probe drives the descent against a real low-mapped entity block and asserts the movement mode byte is byte-for-byte unchanged across a step, that the sound player is handed the ladder id and selector and never an entity, and that an ascent goes down the identical path -- a mutant that reintroduced the swap "only for modes that do not already sound as a ladder" fails the descent and the ascent assertions together. The volume constant is pinned against the engine's own ceiling rather than to a number. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** the roof ladder, both directions. Both should sound, and you should be able to walk afterwards. **IF YOU ARE STILL STANDING ON THAT ISLAND IN A SAVE**, reload -- tris 0 and 1 have no walkable exit, so the only way off is the script that put you there, and this build removes the thing that did.

## v0.130.0

v0.130.0 (#centra). **TWO ROOT CAUSES, BOTH PINNED FROM THE EXE AND THE FIELD FILES, NEITHER OF THEM WHAT THE LAST FOUR BUILDS ASSUMED.** Aaron: "this is getting excessive to do so many BATs over such a small thing. Go back to the game files and exe. Pin down exactly what is going on." Fair. Here is what they say. **(1) THE CLIMB SOUND: ASK THE SCRIPT, NOT THE SYMPTOMS.** v0.129.0 armed the cue on the button the ladder line waits on, and the 18:15-18:21 run armed three times with no climb behind any of them -- `grep -c "engine movement mode"` over that whole log returns 0. The drive had parked the player at t=1.02 and t=1.03, fractionally past the line's end, so the press did nothing; the mod then played sixteen ladder steps over eight seconds while NAV-OBSERVE recorded him walking around with the arrow keys. A cue that fires when nothing happened is worse than one that stays silent. The control-lock byte was wrong too, and the same log says so: every one of those events ended "control free". **THE FIELD SCRIPT STATES THE MOVE EXACTLY**, once decoded correctly -- and this project had the JSM word format backwards, which is the root of the whole four-build detour: the opcode is the HIGH byte and the parameter is the low 24 bits sign-extended, exactly as src/field_archive_jsm_decode.inl has said since v0.12, while the ad-hoc dumps used to chase this bug read `w & 0xFF` and turned every instruction into a different one. Decoded properly: `lad0` (Ladder Up) method 5 is BTNTEST 0xC0 -> **PREQEW(party, method 4)**; `lad1` (Ladder Down) method 5 is BTNTEST 0xC0 -> **PREQEW(party, method 5)**. Party method 4 runs the ladder opcode 0x026 and sets movement mode 3. Party method 5 sets animation 3, runs it, sets animation 7, waits 15 and 32 frames, and SET3s the character to (923,-896,18403). No ladder opcode, so no movement mode, so **the original game is silent going down too**. **PREQEW IS OPCODE 0x019, HANDLER 0x0051D530, AND IT IS A WAIT:** it returns 3 while the requested method is still running -- which makes the interpreter re-execute the same instruction next frame -- and returns 1 only once that method has finished (0x0051D6E2). Its first argument is the CALLING entity, the line itself. That is a per-frame heartbeat for exactly as long as the move lasts, from the frame it starts to the frame it ends, emitted by the game's own interpreter. A press that does not register never reaches it. No button, no control byte, no teleport threshold, no backstop, no guessed duration -- every one of those was this project inferring from outside something the script says out loud. A new offline/jsmdis.py disassembles field scripts correctly, with argument pushes folded into the consuming opcode, so the next question of this kind is answered from the disc instead of from a BAT. **(2) THE DRIVE: A SIDE-FLIP IS NOT AN ARRIVAL, AND THE PARAMETER ALONE CANNOT SAY IT IS.** Aaron: "auto-drive is unreliable and doesn't always take me to the ladder." At 17:58:25 the drive announced "Ladder Down. Press X to use it" while the player stood at (175,-329) -- **321 units** from crroof1's Ladder Down segment, verified against the field's own walkmesh. The arrival came from the CROSSING path, where the player's side of the line's INFINITE extension flips, and v0.18.3.304 bounded that with the projection parameter alone. The parameter was perfectly inside the segment, because it says WHERE ALONG a line the foot falls and nothing whatever about how far off to the side the player is: walking parallel to a line three hundred units away sweeps it from 0 to 1 without ever approaching. **That path now measures the perpendicular distance to the SEGMENT**, which it never did. And the proximity path now requires the foot INSIDE the segment rather than within 15% of an end -- 18:15:04 and 18:21:22 both announced at t=1.02 and t=1.03 and both presses did nothing. The margin exists so a drive that is nearly there is not told to walk forever; it was never a statement about where the engine accepts the button. Being too strict is the safe failure: the aim point is the clamped point ON the segment, so a drive not yet inside simply keeps walking and arrives a moment later. **TESTING.** tests/btn_line_arrival_test.cpp is built entirely from Aaron's own log fixtures and crroof1's real captured lines: the 17:58 position asserted alongside AND 321 units away AND not an arrival; every t from 1.01 to 1.05 past the ladder's end rejected while every t from 0 to 1 on it is accepted; the arrivals that did work (t=0.99, t=0.33) still working; and a sweep proving the failure in one sentence -- 300 units to the side reads as "alongside" at every t and arrives at none of them, 50 units arrives, 70 does not. field_nav_autodrive.inl went over the 80 KB gate with the change, so the arrival test moved into field_nav_autodrive_helpers.inl (81589 bytes now, 331 free). tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** target the Ladder Up on the Centra roof and let the drive take you. It should stop ON the ladder, not beside it or past it, and X should work first time. Then climb up, and climb back down -- both directions should now step. **NOT IN THIS BUILD:** "easy to inadvertently walk back to the previous field". The geometry is now measured -- crroof1's exit gateway sits on tris 38-41 at z 17998-18134, 474 units from the ladder at tri 69, and the route between them is the ramp that climbs 370 units of Z -- but a proximity warning is new machinery with its own noise budget and does not belong in the build whose point is the ladder. It is next.

## v0.129.0

v0.129.0 (#centra). **v0.128.0's GATE COULD NOT HAVE PASSED ONCE, ON ANY LADDER, EVER.** It asked whether the trigger line the player was standing on was called a ladder by reading `s_capturedLines[].name`. That field is written exactly once in the whole codebase -- in the SETLINE hook, where it is set to `'\0'` under a comment saying "Name resolved later in RefreshCatalog" -- and RefreshCatalog resolves names into the CATALOG and never writes them back. So the question was always asked about an empty string, and an empty string is not a ladder. The diagnosis in v0.128.0 stands; the code that acted on it never ran. **THE 17:58 LOG PROVES THE DESCENT HAPPENED AND THE MOD SAW NOTHING:** the drive announced "Ladder Down. Press X to use it" at 17:58:25, NAV-OBSERVE recorded the player moving 654 units in 27 ticks at 17:58:33 -- which is not walking, it is the SET3 teleport at the end of the move -- and between those two lines the mod wrote not one [LADDER] line. **THE NAMES COME FROM THE CATALOG NOW,** which is the same data the mod already speaks out loud: a trigger-line entry carries entityIdx = -200 - lineSlot, which is how the refresh dump prints "cat1 TRIGGER line1 center=(474,-447) name='Ladder Down'". The geometry still comes from the captured line that slot points at, measured to the segment rather than to its nearest end. **AND THE CUE NOW HAS TWO WAYS IN, BECAUSE ONE OF THEM IS STILL A THEORY.** The control-lock byte at 0x01CE4903 is read straight out of the 0x04E/0x04D handlers and it *should* be set for the length of the scripted move -- but it has never actually been observed set, because the name gate meant the mod never got as far as looking. So this build does not bet the fix on it. The descent has a second signal that needs no engine state at all: the player presses the button the line is waiting on. crroof1's `lad1` runs BTNTEST 0xC0 -- Cross or Square -- and the mod already announces "Press X to use it", so the press is the game's own start signal and the mod's own announcement in one. Either edge arms the cue and **the log names which fired**, so if the control lock is the wrong byte the next run says so instead of the next build guessing again. **IT ENDS ON WHICHEVER COMES FIRST, AND SAYS WHICH.** The engine's own ladder move finishing outranks everything -- the ascent arms this cue too, since it is the same button, and there the movement mode is the authority; without that rule, pressing X at the foot of crroof1's ladder would leave the cue running for the backstop's full eight seconds after the climb had ended. Then control coming back, then a single-frame move of 200 units or more (the teleport -- the 17:58 descent's was 654), then an eight-second backstop so a press over a ladder that does nothing costs a few seconds of stepping rather than a stuck cue. **TESTING.** The catalog sentinel mapping is pinned both ways, including that a slot past the captured-line count is refused rather than indexed. Both arming signals are asserted on the edge and not the level, both refused off a ladder line, and the release of the button asserted not to arm. Every end condition is asserted in priority order, with the 654-unit jump from the real log as the teleport fixture and an ordinary 40-unit walking frame as the negative. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** crroof1's roof ladder, down. **AND WHATEVER HAPPENS, THE LOG NOW ANSWERS IT** -- `grep LADDER logs/ff8_field.log` will show the arm line with the line name, the distance and which signal fired, and the end line with the reason. If it is still silent, that grep says whether the cue armed and did not sound, or never armed at all.

## v0.128.0

v0.128.0 (#centra). **THE WAY DOWN IS NOT A LADDER MOVE. IT NEVER WAS.** Aaron, three builds running: "the sounds work going up but not down on that top ladder." Every fix so far assumed the descent was a ladder move the mod was mishandling -- v0.126.0 presented mode 2 as mode 3, v0.127.0 added a transition trace to catch a mode nobody had catalogued. Both were looking for a movement mode that **is never set**, and the reason took a corrected JSM disassembler to see: this project had the field-script word format backwards. The opcode is the HIGH byte and the parameter is the low 24 bits sign-extended -- src/field_archive_jsm_decode.inl has said so since v0.12 and the ad-hoc dumps used to chase this bug were reading `w & 0xFF`, which turns every instruction into a different one. Decoded correctly, crroof1 says it plainly: **`lad0` (Ladder Up) runs PREQEW(party, method 4); `lad1` (Ladder Down) runs PREQEW(party, method 5)**, and the two methods are not the same shape. **Method 4 (UP):** anim 3, run anim, anim 4, **ladder move 0x026** to (661,-622,19296), SET3 (456,-418,19496). **Method 5 (DOWN):** anim 3, run anim, anim 7, WAIT 15, WAIT 32, **SET3 (923,-896,18403)** -- and that is the whole of it. Square played the climbing animation in place, waited a fixed number of frames, and teleported the character to the bottom. No ladder opcode, so no movement mode, so no engine step -- **the original game is silent going down too** -- and the mod, which watches that mode, was silent for exactly the same reason. **v0.127.0's TRACE EARNED ITS KEEP BY SAYING SO.** The descent at 17:32:36-43 produced no MODE-WATCH line at all, while the catalog either side of it shows the player moving from the 9-triangle top zone to the 65-triangle bottom one. A descent that happened and logged nothing is the finding; a first-sighting mask would have looked identical to a descent that never happened. **SO THE MOD WATCHES THE CONTROL LOCK INSTEAD.** Opcodes 0x04E and 0x04D bracket both party ladder methods and they are the engine's player-control pair -- 0x04E (handler 0x0051DE90) writes 1 to **0x01CE4903**, 0x04D (0x0051DDA0) writes 0. One global byte, no hook, true for exactly as long as the scripted move runs and false the frame it ends. That is a better end condition than any duration this project could have guessed at, and guessing at durations is what produced the 260 ms in v0.124.0. **IT IS GATED ON THE LADDER LINE,** because control is locked for every cutscene and every door in the game. The cue arms only when control goes down WHILE the player is standing on a captured trigger line this field calls a ladder -- which costs nothing new, since the catalog already resolved those names to say "Ladder Down. Press X to use it" out loud. Distance is measured to the SEGMENT, not to its nearest end: crroof1's ladder lines are ~130 units long and the player stands anywhere along them. And it arms on the EDGE, not the level, so it cannot re-arm across the teleport that ends the descent. **TWO WAYS IN, ONE STATE.** LadderIsClimbing() is the movement mode OR the scripted cue, so crtower3 -- which sets mode 2 AND locks control -- cannot cue the same step twice. **TESTING.** The name gate is asserted against the field's real catalog strings, ladders and non-ladders both, including a null name. The geometry gate runs against crroof1's actual captured line, (444,-509)->(505,-385) with centre (474,-447), the position the catalog announced it at: the middle, both ends and 140 units perpendicular are underfoot; 160 is not; the OTHER ladder in the same field is not; 200 units past an end is not, which is the v0.122.0 lesson about infinite extensions applied to the same field that taught it. The probe drives the descent end to end against a real entity block -- mode 0 silent without the cue, stepping with it, mode 0 presented as 3 so the engine picks the ladder sound, the byte restored, and the cue stopping the frame control comes back with nothing played after the landing. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** crroof1's roof ladder, down. It should now sound the same as going up. The tower ladders should be unchanged. **STILL OPEN:** the drive pinned on crtower3 in triangle 87 for eighteen recoveries at 16:50:52 in the previous run; that is the next thing worth a build.

## v0.127.0

v0.127.0 (#centra). **THE MEAN WALKED TO 970 MS BECAUSE A SKIPPED STRIDE WAS BEING TREATED AS A SLOWER LADDER.** The 16:39-16:54 run measured nineteen gaps on crtower3 and the cadence went 469 -> 783 -> 970 before settling at 586 -- which is the number crroof1's silent roof ladder then played at, a quarter slower than the ladder it exists to imitate. **FOUR GAPS DID IT: 953, 1359, 1344 and 672 ms.** The first three are 2x and 3x the real 468-469 ms interval v0.126.0 measured. They are the engine's zero crossing missing a stride, not the animation changing speed, and averaging them in is arithmetic that cannot be right: a skipped step carries no information about the pace except that it was a whole number of steps. **SO A GAP IS FOLDED BEFORE IT IS BELIEVED.** Divide by 1, 2 or 3 and keep the quotient closest to the pace already held, provided it lands inside 80-125% of it. 953/2 = 476 and 1359/3 = 453 both survive and both are the truth. **THE BAND IS NOT ARBITRARY EITHER.** A gap near 1.5x the pace reads equally well as one slow stride or two fast ones and nothing in the data says which, so the band is set so BOTH readings fall outside it: 672 against a 452 ms belief is too slow at 672 and too fast at 336, and is dropped rather than dragged in. At +/-35% that halving squeaks in -- a fold that finds some quotient in range for every gap is a licence to believe anything. **REPLAYED AGAINST THE RUN'S OWN NINETEEN GAPS the cadence now stays between 426 and 469 ms throughout** and never exceeds the value it started from; the roof ladder would have sounded at ~430 rather than 586. That replay is a test, not a note: the nineteen numbers are in tests/ladder_cue_test.cpp in order, asserted never to reach 586 again. v0.125.0's "the first real sample is taken outright" rule is gone with them -- it existed to stop a 700 ms guess contaminating a measurement, and since v0.126.0 the starting value IS a measurement. **AND THE MOD STOPS FILLING HOLES IN THE ENGINE'S OWN RHYTHM.** The suppression slack goes from two intervals to four. At two, that 1359 ms hole at 16:51:22 was long enough for the mod to cut in, and the log duly reads "2 mod steps, engine sounded it itself" on a ladder the mod was supposed to leave alone. Four intervals is ~1.9 s, past the longest hole the engine has ever been observed to leave, so a genuine dropout is still covered and the game's own pacing is not interrupted. **THE PROBE WAS NOT BUILDING, AND THAT IS THE REAL FINDING IN THIS ENTRY.** v0.126.0 wrapped the mode swap in __try/__finally. The winshim maps __try to try and __except to catch(...); no macro can fake __finally, so tests/ladder_cue_compile.cpp -- the probe that exists precisely because this code cannot be checked any other way -- stopped compiling, and the gate that should have refused the push was not clean. The swap is now three guarded steps instead, which say the same thing, restore the byte on the fault path as well, and can be driven on the host. **AND THE PROBE WAS PASSING A NUMBER WHERE AN ENTITY SHOULD BE.** It handed 0x1234 to the cue as the player's block -- fine while nothing dereferenced it, useless the moment v0.126.0 started writing +0x23C, and a segfault once it actually ran. It now maps a real block low enough that the engine's `int entityPtr` round-trips on a 64-bit host, watches the mode byte FROM INSIDE the stand-in routine, and asserts what v0.126.0 shipped untested: a descent is presented as mode 3, an ascent is left alone, and the byte is put back either way. **AND ONE DIAGNOSTIC, BECAUSE THE DOWN LADDER HAS NEVER ACTUALLY BEEN TESTED.** v0.126.0 answered "why is the way down silent" with mode 2 and fixed it by presenting mode 3 for the length of the call, and nothing has exercised that path since: the 16:36-16:55 run went UP crroof1's roof ladder at 16:54:29, arrived at the Ladder Down line at 16:54:52, and the log ends there. So MODE-WATCH now records TRANSITIONS rather than first sightings. A first-sighting bitmask cannot distinguish the two ways a descent can still fail -- a movement mode nobody has catalogued, and no new mode at all because the descent is a plain scripted move -- since modes 0 and 1 are seen within seconds of any field loading, and a descent that walks the character down through them logs nothing and looks exactly like a descent that never happened. Walking is 0->1 and 1->0 and nothing else; anything a ladder does leaves its own pair. One line per distinct pair, capped at 24 so a per-frame table cannot overrun. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** the Centra ladders again, both directions. The tower ladders should sound as the game sounds them with nothing added -- the log should say "0 mod steps, engine sounded it itself" -- and the roof ladder should hold the same pace rather than slowing across the climb. **ALSO IN THE LOG, NOT FIXED HERE:** at 16:50:52-16:51:11 the drive pinned on crtower3 in triangle 87, ran eighteen recoveries in nineteen seconds and was cancelled. Tri 87 is a dead-end sliver whose only neighbour is 86; the player sat at (-1767,-468) with the stick at -68 degrees and moveDist=0 while the first waypoint, 106 units away, was inside tri 86 across the shared edge. The crroof1 ramp ping-ponged the same way at 16:52:49-16:53:04. That is the next thing worth a build.

## v0.126.0

v0.126.0 (#centra). **469 MS, AND THE DOWN LADDER IS SILENT BECAUSE NOBODY HAS EVER LOOKED AT WHAT MODE DESCENDING SETS.** v0.125.0 stopped guessing the climb cadence and hooked the engine to measure it, and the 13:06 run on crtower timed fourteen consecutive gaps: 468, 407, 468, 453, 469, 469, 469, 468, 469, 469, 469, 453, 469, 468. Eleven of the fourteen are 468-469 ms; 453 is one frame short at 64 Hz and 407 is three, which is the poll quantising rather than the animation changing speed. The running mean reached 465 ms by the time Aaron climbed crroof1's silent ladder, and he called it "the normal pace". **THAT PACE IS NOW THE DEFAULT.** LADDER_STEP_MS_DEFAULT goes 700 -> 469, so a silent ladder sounds right on the FIRST climb rather than needing an engine-sounded ladder ahead of it to teach the mod the rhythm -- which is the whole of what "repurpose this for other silent ladders" requires, since crroof1 only sounded correctly because crtower happened to come first on that route. The learning still runs and still refines; it simply has nothing left to rescue. **AND THE DESCENT GETS MEASURED THE SAME WAY IT GOT FIXED.** Aaron heard the climb up and nothing on the way down. LadderModeIsClimb() names modes 2, 3 and 4 because those are the three this project has actually watched the game set -- mode 4 on crtower, mode 3 on crroof1, both of them ascents. Descending is a separate animation and plausibly a separate mode, and widening the test to catch it would be a guess of exactly the kind the 260 ms was. So this build does not widen it. Two bitmasks log one line the first time each movement mode is ever seen, and one line per mode the engine is caught playing a ladder step in -- the second logged BEFORE the climb-mode gate, because a step the engine plays in a mode this file does not call a climb is precisely the evidence that is missing. One descent of a crtower ladder with this build and the log names the number.

## v0.125.0

v0.125.0 (#centra). **"THE CLIMBING SOUNDS WERE VERY FAST COMPARED TO THE WAY THEY USUALLY SOUND ON A LADDER" -- AND THE 260 MS THAT MADE THEM FAST WAS A GUESS.** v0.124.0 spent its whole entry arguing that the mod should stop assuming and go read the engine, and then, three lines from the end, wrote `LADDER_STEP_MS = 260` because a quarter of a second felt about right. Aaron's log times it exactly: `climb started` at 12:28:09, eighteen steps, `climb ended` at 12:28:14. Five seconds, eighteen rungs, and a listener who knows what the other ladders sound like. **THE ENGINE KNOWS THE CADENCE AND THE MOD NOW ASKS IT.** sub_00520260 does not fire on a timer -- it fires on a **zero crossing**. At 0x004783A2 the previous foot offset in `si` is compared against the new one in `bx` and a step plays when their signs differ, once per foot, twice per animation cycle. So the true interval is a property of the climbing animation's playback speed: not a number anyone can read out of the exe, and not one worth guessing at a second time. This build hooks the routine, times the gaps between the game's own steps on the ladders that already sound, and replays that measured interval on the ones that do not. One engine-sounded ladder anywhere teaches it, and on the only route up the Centra Ruins the tower ladders come before the roof one. **AND THE SAME HOOK CLOSES A BUG AARON HAS NOT HIT YET.** v0.124.0 polls the movement mode and steps on **every** ladder -- including crtower3's `ladup0` and crtower1's `p0_ladup0`, which the engine is already sounding. That is a second set of steps laid over the game's own. The Centra run that produced the log climbed only the silent roof ladder, so the doubling never reached his ears; the hook that measures the cadence is also what hears the engine working and holds the mod's cue back. Two intervals of engine silence hand the ladder back, so a skipped crossing does not let the mod cut in for one step in the middle of the game's rhythm. **EACH CLIMB IS JUDGED ON ITSELF.** The engine-activity memory is cleared the frame the movement mode turns into a ladder mode, because steps the game played on the previous ladder must not silence the next, silent one -- which is exactly the roof ladder's position in the route. And the first mod step now waits out a 400 ms grace period, which covers the mount animation and gives a sounded ladder time to declare itself before the mod puts a step on top of its opening one. **THE MEASUREMENT IS FILTERED, NOT SWALLOWED.** A gap under 300 ms is the two feet crossing on the same frame and a gap over 1400 ms spans a pause or two different ladders; neither is a stride, and learning from the first would drive the cue straight back to the rattle being fixed. Real samples are a running mean weighted two-to-one toward what is already believed, except the first, which is taken outright -- averaging a guess into a measurement only contaminates the measurement. Until anything is measured the default is 700 ms, and the log says which of the two it is using on every climb. **THE MOD'S OWN CALL IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR THE ENGINE'S.** The mod calls the MinHook trampoline rather than the patched entry point, and carries a re-entrancy flag anyway, because if MH_CreateHook ever fails the mod is calling the hooked address and would otherwise record its own step, decide the engine is busy, and silence itself one step in. The prologue signature is checked **before** the hook goes in, since MinHook overwrites the very bytes the check reads. **TESTING.** The five-second climb is now a scenario rather than a constant: the probe runs the schedule across 5000 ms of frames and asserts the result is no longer anything like eighteen steps, and still audibly a climb. The interval is a parameter, so a mutant that quietly kept using a constant fails a test where a slower learned cadence must actually space the steps further apart. The engine path is driven end to end -- first step with no gap to measure, second one measured, an 8 ms double-crossing discarded, the mod silent while the engine works, the ladder handed back after two intervals of silence, and a fresh climb sounded at the cadence learned from the ladders before it. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** climb the Centra Ruins ladders in the order the route takes them. The tower ladders should sound exactly as the game has always sounded them -- one set of steps, not two -- and the roof ladder should now sound at the same pace rather than the rattle. The log records the measured gaps, so if the pace is still off, `grep LADDER logs/ff8_field.log` will say by how much.

## v0.124.0

v0.124.0 (#centra). **"WHY CAN'T WE UTILIZE THE SAME CLIMBING SOUND AS THE REST OF THE LADDERS IN THE GAME?" WE CAN, AND v0.123.0 SHOULD NOT HAVE CLAIMED OTHERWISE.** That build synthesised three knocks and justified it -- "chasing the engine's SE would tie an accessibility cue to an internal audio path" -- which sounded like a finding and was an **assumption I never tested**. Aaron asked the obvious question and the answer took twenty minutes of disassembly. **THE ENGINE'S STEP ROUTINE IS ONE CALL:** `sub_00520260(entityPtr, foot, volume, pan)`, cdecl, four arguments, four call sites in the exe (0x004783D6, 0x00478420, 0x0052A31C, 0x0052A35C), each cleaning with `add esp, 0x10` and passing volume 0x7F or 0x40 with pan 0x80 for centre. **AND IT PICKS THE SOUND ITSELF** from the entity's movement mode at +0x23C: `cmp dl,3 / je` and `cmp dl,4 / je` both land on 0x005203BB, which pushes sound id **0x3F** -- the ladder step -- while every other mode falls through to the terrain footstep table at 0x01CE4BFC. So the mod hardcodes no sound id, no volume and no waveform. It asks the engine for the noise this character on this surface would make, and on a ladder that is the ladder sound the other ladders play. **AND THAT REVEALS THE REAL DIAGNOSIS.** Mode 3 -- crroof1's roof ladder -- reaches the ladder branch **exactly as mode 4 does**. v0.123.0's story, that the sound belongs to the mode and the roof ladder drew the silent one, was wrong. The routine is driven by footstep event frames in the climbing animation, and crroof1's `lad0` runs animation 3 where crtower3's runs animation 6: one has the frames, one does not. **The roof ladder was never missing the sound. It was missing the call.** **SO THE MOD MAKES THE CALL, AND POLLS RATHER THAN HOOKS.** v0.123.0 hooked the four ladder opcodes and needed a 900 ms debounce to survive one climb firing several of them. The movement mode is the engine's own statement that a climb is in progress, so a per-frame read of one byte needs no debounce and no guess at how long a climb lasts: steps play every 260 ms while the mode says climbing and stop the frame it clears. Four opcode hooks and an address-table lookup deleted. **CALLING A HARDCODED ADDRESS IS GUARDED TWICE.** Fifteen bytes of the routine's prologue are compared before the mod ever calls through it -- a repacked or patched exe fails and the cue stays silent, which is the only safe answer when the alternative is jumping into the middle of something else -- and the call itself is SEH-wrapped, because a fault must not take the game down over a sound. **TESTING.** The probe exists because this code lives in field_navigation.cpp's include chain, which cannot be syntax-checked on the host; the sound was split into its own unit so it could be. It drives the signature check against the real prologue and against copies corrupted in the first byte and the last, the spacing across the interval boundary, the alternating feet, the reset when a climb ends (so the next one steps on its first frame rather than waiting out an interval that began minutes ago), and the unresolved-routine path playing nothing and faulting on nothing. The model test pins that mode 3 IS sounded -- a mutant that sounded only the modes the engine already calls for would leave the one ladder this build exists for exactly as quiet. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **NOTE:** tests/winshim/mmsystem.h was added in v0.123.0 for the synthesised waveform and nothing needs it now. It stays because it closes a real winshim gap -- src/world_map.cpp still cannot be host-checked, and PlaySound was one of the two reasons.

## v0.123.0

v0.123.0 (#centra). **THE GAME IS NOT WITHHOLDING A SOUND -- IT IS RUNNING A DIFFERENT OPCODE.** Aaron: "that particular ladder on the roof for some reason does not have the ladder climbing sound that is normally played... It is useful for a blind player to confirm they are actually climbing." Field scripts move a character along a ladder with **four interchangeable opcodes**, and all four write the entity's movement mode at +0x23C: `0x024`->2 (handler 0x00525740), `0x025`->3 (0x00525900), `0x026`->3 (0x00525A30), `0x027`->4 (0x00525B60). The Centra Ruins uses three of them. crtower3's `laddw0` runs 0x024 and crtower1's `p0_ladup0` runs 0x027 -- the two Aaron says make the noise. crroof1's `lad0`, the roof ladder, is **the only one in the ruins that runs 0x026, and the only one that is silent.** The sound belongs to the movement mode, the mode belongs to the opcode, and the opcode is a 1999 script author's choice in a file this mod does not patch. **SO THE FIX IS NOT TO CHASE THEIR SOUND.** Firing the engine's own SE would leave every other 0x025/0x026 ladder in the game just as quiet and would tie an accessibility cue to an internal audio path. The mod cues **every** ladder move itself, on all four opcodes, so "am I climbing?" has one answer everywhere. Three short damped knocks at 196 Hz -- the shape of a foot finding three rungs, low enough to sit under the music rather than compete with speech -- synthesised once into a WAV in memory and played with PlaySound/SND_ASYNC, the same mechanism the Garden-battle block tone has used since v0.20.111 for exactly this reason: it never stalls the game thread and never takes the floor from a spoken line. Hooked on the four opcode handlers pulled from the engine's own dispatch table, gated to the player's entity block so an NPC on a ladder is silent, and debounced at 900 ms because one climb runs several of these opcodes -- crtower3's `ladup0` fires 0x027 and then 0x024 inside a single script. **NO DIRECTION IN THE CUE, AND THAT IS A DECISION.** The obvious guess is that the opcodes pair up/down -- an older comment in this project even names 0x025 LADDERUP and 0x026 LADDERDOWN. The disc says otherwise: crtower3's `ladup0` (up) runs 0x027 while its `laddw0` (down) runs 0x024, and crroof1's `lad0` -- which v0.116.0 established travels UP -- runs the one supposedly called LADDERDOWN. The opcode does not encode direction, so the cue does not claim to. **THE PROBE EARNED ITS KEEP IN THE FIRST MINUTE.** The cue lives in field_navigation.cpp's include chain, which cannot be syntax-checked on the host -- it pulls in DirectInput and inline assembly, the same standing limitation src/world_map.cpp has carried for years. So the cue was split into its own includable unit with one dependency the hook keeps to itself (which entity is the player), and a host probe builds the rest against a new winshim mmsystem.h. It immediately failed an assertion: the debounce used `lastMs == 0` to mean "never cued", the shim's clock reads 0, every cue stamped 0, and the debounce never engaged. On Windows the tick is never 0 after boot, **so that would have shipped and stayed invisible**. "Never cued" is now its own flag. **TESTING.** The opcode->mode table is pinned as the evidence it is, including that the silent 0x026 IS cued -- the mutant that only cues the opcodes the engine already sounds would leave the one ladder this build exists for exactly as quiet. The probe reads the synthesised waveform back: the four RIFF tags, both sizes agreeing with the sample count, the buffer fitting, an audible peak, silence between the knocks, and each knock decaying rather than droning -- a cue that is silent, clipped or a flat second of tone is a bug no compiler sees and nobody hears until a BAT. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** climb the roof ladder in the Centra Ruins. It should now knock three times, the same as the tower ladders -- and so should every other ladder, since the cue is the mod's and not the engine's.

## v0.122.0

v0.122.0 (#centra). **NEAR AN END IS NOT ON THE LINE, AND THE LOG SHOWS EXACTLY WHAT THAT COSTS.** The 2026-08-28 20:33-20:35 run is six clean arrivals, zero cancellations, zero give-ups, and the 22-hop roof ramp that ate 25 seconds in v0.119.0 now completes -- but on crroof1 the drive arrived at the ladder **four times in two minutes and he never once got up it**. The zone filter says so without ambiguity: tri 20, tri 65, tri 48, tri 34, every one in the 65-triangle main zone, never the 9-triangle platform above. **HE WAS NEVER BESIDE THE LADDER.** At 20:34:53 he is at (1050,-753) against a line running (862,-952) to (971,-839). That is 117 units from the near endpoint -- inside v0.121.0's 60 after two more seconds of walking -- and, projected onto the line, **t = 1.74**: three quarters of the segment's own length PAST its far end. He was up the ramp from the ladder, not on it. The engine's touch zone is the segment, so X did nothing, four times, in silence. **v0.120.0 CLAMPED THE AIM POINT AND FORGOT TO CLAMP THE ARRIVAL.** Aiming at the nearest point on the segment was right; treating "60 units from that point" as "on the ladder" was not, because when the player is past an end the nearest point IS the end and the distance says nothing about which side of it he is standing. **THE PROJECTION PARAMETER ALREADY KNOWS**, and this project already fixed this exact geometry once: v0.18.3.304 bounds the crossing test to a foot inside the segment with a 15% end margin, after a nearly-Y-parallel line's infinite extension announced an arrival 960 units early. Same test, same margin, reused rather than re-invented -- and decided ONCE, at the top of the block, so the crossing check and the proximity check cannot disagree about it. **BEING TOO STRICT HERE IS THE SAFE FAILURE.** A drive not yet alongside simply keeps going: the aim point is the endpoint, so walking to it brings t back to 1.0 and inside the margin. Too strict costs a drive that runs its clock out and says so; too loose costs what he just spent two minutes on, which is silence. The arrival log now carries the t it arrived at, so the next run can be checked rather than assumed. **TESTING.** The fixture is the log's own numbers -- crroof1's ladder line and the position the drive kept stopping at -- asserted to be past the end and NOT alongside. Both endpoints, the middle, and both margins are asserted inclusive and bounded. A point 80 units off the midpoint at right angles is asserted still alongside, which kills a mutant that measures distance instead of the parameter, and a zero-length line is alongside by definition because it has no end to be past. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **ALSO CONFIRMED:** the crtower1 ladder still works -- arrival at 20:31:59, field change to crtower2 ten seconds later, no drive involved, which is a player pressing X and climbing.

## v0.121.0

v0.121.0 (#centra). **v0.120.0 WORKS, IN HIS OWN KEY.** The 2026-08-28 20:16 log: `[drive] target line0 waits on BTNTEST 0x00C0 ('Left Ladder Up') -- arriving on it, not through it` then `arrived at a BTNTEST line 0x00C0 -- "Left Ladder Up. Press X to use it."`. **X**, not "Cross" -- the engine keymap resolver gave his actual binding. He climbed. Across the whole run the drive failure count is **one**, against a dozen two builds ago, and the two `stopped:` lines with an empty reason are both `transition COMPLETE ... reached`, which is how a successful exit has always ended. Two things the log says to fix. **ONE: IT ANNOUNCED A LADDER HE DID NOT ASK FOR.** On crtower2 he selected "Left Ladder Down", which is up on the landing, so the island-bridge search sent him to "Left Ladder Up" -- correct, that is the only route -- and the mod then said "Left Ladder Up. Press X to use it." with no hint of why. **Being walked somewhere you did not ask for and told so in a confident voice is how a blind player stops trusting the catalog.** One clause fixes it: "...That is the way to Left Ladder Down." It goes on only when the bridge is something OTHER than the target, and only onto a sentence that exists -- a bare "That is the way to X" with no action in front of it is not a thing to say. **TWO: THIRTY UNITS WAS ONE UNIT TOO TIGHT.** At 20:16:12 the drive sat at **dist=31** against the ladder base with `moveDist=0` and burned `recovery 1` through `recovery 4` -- five seconds, two nudges, one of them `escapeMode=1 pinned=1` -- trying to close a single unit the player had already stopped being able to close. The arrival radius is now **60**, which is not a new guess: it is the figure this codebase already uses for "close enough to interact" (the talk-radius floor in this same function, and the direction-drive default), and the same log has him climbing the ladder from 42 units away. **TESTING.** The new clause is killed against a mutant that appends unconditionally ("Ladder Up ... that is the way to Ladder Up"), against an empty leads-to, and against appending to nothing; it is checked after the pad-name fallback as well as after a resolved key, and a buffer too small for the tail keeps the instruction rather than half a tail. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **STILL OPEN, AND NOW DIAGNOSED:** the drive to crroof1's ladder ping-pongs around triangles 34/35 and he cancelled after 25 seconds. That route is not wrong -- the roof is a **22-hop zig-zag ramp** (tri 38 -> 37 -> 36 -> 35 -> 34 -> 33 -> 32 -> 31 -> 68 -> 25 ... -> 69, climbing z 18134 to 18403 and doubling back on itself) -- so the waypoints heading north-east away from a target to the south-west are correct, and the failure is the drive not holding a narrow ramp, not the path. Unrelated to the button work; needs the corridor-steering pass.

## v0.120.0

v0.120.0 (#centra). **A LADDER IS NOT A DOORWAY, AND THE DRIVE HAD ONLY EVER BEEN TAUGHT DOORWAYS.** The 2026-08-28 log at 19:36:54: parked FIFTEEN UNITS from the ladder it had correctly walked to, still steering at a point 300 units past it, `no-progress stuck`, `Cancelled`. The push is deliberate and right for an exit -- v0.15.9.2.14 added it because "stopping 300 units short of an exit means the player has to walk through manually" -- and completely wrong for a ladder, where there is no walkmesh beyond the line to walk onto. **BTNTEST IS OPCODE 0x6D**, read out of FF8_EN.exe rather than guessed: handler 0x0051DA50 pops a mask, ANDs it with the live pad word at [0x01CE48B0] and leaves 1 or 0 in the script's local 0 -- which is exactly what the `PSHL 0; PSHN_L 1; OPER ==` that always follows it reads back. A Centra ladder's `touch` opens `PSHN_L 192; BTNTEST; ...` and does nothing at all until a button is held. **AND THE DISC CONFIRMS THE BUTTON ORDER A SECOND TIME.** v0.67.3 derived `0=L2 ... 4=Triangle 5=Circle 6=Cross 7=Square ... 12=Up 13=Right 14=Down 15=Left` from the 0x05 icon codes. Every BTNTEST mask in the game reads as a sentence under it -- **0x00C0 Cross|Square x142** (the action pair), 0x0080 Square x103, 0x0010 Triangle x76 (the menu button), the four D-pad singles, 0xFFFF x16 (skip the cutscene), Select, Start. Under the raw PlayStation pad order the commonest mask in the game would be "Left or L2", which no script would ever wait on. Two derivations, two decades apart, same answer. **THE SCANNER NOW RECORDS IT.** `touchButtonMask` per entity, taken from the top of the push run at the BTNTEST -- the same by-construction argument read every other consumer here relies on -- and the init method excluded, because a BTNTEST there is not the thing the player has to press on arrival. 201 entities disc-wide carry one; **112 of them are LINES, 101 of those 0x00C0**, and that is exactly the set that used to swallow a drive. The scanner golden gains a `btn=` column. **WHAT CHANGES ON ARRIVAL.** For a line with an actionable mask the drive (a) aims at the NEAREST POINT ON THE SEGMENT instead of pushing 300 units through the midpoint -- which is also where the engine's own touch test wants the player standing -- (b) tightens the arrival radius from the 300-unit non-entity default to 30, and (c) stops and says what to press. **IN THE PLAYER'S OWN KEY, NOT THE PAD'S.** "Press Cross" is useless to someone on a keyboard, and this mod already knew better: the 0x05 icon codes have spoken real keys since v0.67.3 by resolving through the engine's keymap at 0x01CD0208. That resolver was buried behind an action-index lookup a BTNTEST mask has no use for, so its second half is now `FF8TextDecode::ButtonKeyName(button)` and both paths share it. The mask names two buttons because the game takes either; the first one the engine can put a key to wins, and the pad name is the fallback only when it can put a key to none of them. So: **"Left Ladder Up. Press Enter to use it."** **THE EVERYTHING-MASK IS NOT AN INSTRUCTION.** 0xFFFF appears sixteen times and every one is a skip-the-cutscene test; announcing "press L2" there would be arbitrary and wrong, so an actionable mask is one that is neither empty nor everything. **TESTING.** The bit order is pinned against the masks that prove it. The sentence is killed against a mutant preferring the pad name over the key, against an empty key counting as a key, and on both fragments (a label with nothing to press, something to press with no label). `BtnMaskIsActionable` is killed against `mask != 0`, which would announce the cutscene skips. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **TO TEST:** drive to either ladder on the Centra tower ground floor, or to the down-ladder on the floor with the statue. Expect to be walked ONTO it and told the key -- not parked short of it in silence.

## v0.119.0

v0.119.0 (#centra). **THE FIELD WALKMESH IS 3D AND THE LOOKUP WAS NOT. THAT IS THE WHOLE FAMILY OF DRIVE FAILURES.** The 2026-08-28 log, on crtower1, driving to a ladder the player had just picked out of the catalog: `target on different walkmesh island (start tri 52, goal tri 21) -- searching for bridge trigger` / `no reachable trigger line found, using direct steering` / six recoveries / `moveDist=0` / `Cancelled`. **THE LADDER WAS NOT ON A DIFFERENT ISLAND.** crtower1's walkmesh is 137 triangles in 14 connected components: one floor of 111, and thirteen two-triangle pockets. Read their centres out of the .id and they name themselves -- island 9 at z=11413, island 10 at 11813, island 11 at 12213, island 12 at 11013, island 13 at 10613, **all at the same X and Y** -- five rungs of one LADDER, stacked 400 units apart above the floor, which the game teleports the party onto one at a time as the climb plays. Two more sets of five do the other ladder and the stone. FindNearestTriangle scored on X and Y alone, so asked where the ladder's trigger line at (1617,-444) is it answered **tri 21, a rung a thousand units in the air** (22 units away in plan view) instead of tri 88, the floor directly under it at 52 units and z=10378. The line's own Z is 10385. The drive then compared the player's floor triangle against a rung, correctly found them unconnected, and spent twelve seconds hunting a bridge to a place it was already standing beside. **AND IT EXPLAINS v0.118.0 TOO.** crtower2's exit to crtower3 resolves 2D to tri 73 on the right-ladder platform (island 12) and 3D to tri 91 on the main floor (island 0) -- **the player's own island**. There was never an island to cross there; ordinary A* walks it, and the bridge machinery .118 fixed was treating a symptom. It is the same shape as the Deep Sea Research Center hatch bug open since v0.112.0, where the drive "reaches the goal triangle then steers at the captured line's raw midpoint, which is off the walkable floor". **THE FIX NEEDS NO TUNING CONSTANT**, which is why it is done this way and not with a Z tolerance: field X, Y and Z are the same int16 world units, so plain 3D Euclidean distance separates the cases by two orders of magnitude -- the rung scores 22^2 + 1028^2 = 1,057,268 and the floor 52^2 + 7^2 = 2,753. Nothing to pick, nothing to re-tune per field. **ONLY A CALLER THAT HAS A HEIGHT MAY USE IT.** Exactly two kinds do: SETLINE trigger lines, which have carried z1/z2 since v05.58, and INF gateways, whose lineZ1/lineZ2 v0.18.3.298 stopped throwing away. The drive's goal triangle, the bridge search's candidates, the chosen bridge and the recovery re-paths all take the 3D form; **the player's own position, GPS and every diagnostic keep the 2D function unchanged**, because they have no height to offer and a wrong Z is worse than none. WalkmeshTriangle gains the centerZ the loader has always had the vertices for and always discarded. **TESTING.** The fixture is crtower1 itself -- the five rung centres and the floor beneath them, read out of the .id -- and the test asserts BOTH halves: that the 2D form picks a rung (the bug, pinned so it cannot be quietly reintroduced) and that the 3D form picks the floor. Every rung is checked, not just the nearest, killing a mutant that compares only the first candidate. And the 2D form is pinned unchanged: same metric, same lowest-index tie rule, and on a flat mesh the two forms are asserted to give the identical answer, so no field without stacking can move. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. **ALSO CONFIRMED IN THIS RUN:** the roof statue read "Code:7 4 4 4 2" out loud, the panel took it, "Correct."; and crtower1's console showed as "Control Panel, not active" before the power was on. **STILL OPEN:** a ladder needs a BUTTON PRESS, and the drive aims 300 units PAST a trigger line to force a walk-through crossing -- which is right for a doorway and wrong for a ladder, where there is no walkmesh beyond it. The 19:36:54 stall is exactly that: parked 15 units from the ladder, still pushing at a point 300 units through it. Arriving ON a button-press line and saying which key to press is next.

## v0.118.0

v0.118.0 (#centra). **v0.117.0 CONFIRMED, AND THE LOG HANDED OVER THE NEXT ONE.** The roof statue now reads out: `[VAR-EXPAND] 5 insert(s) -> "Code:7 4 4 4 2"` followed by `[AMESW] win[0] Speaking: "Code:7 4 4 4 2"` -- the same five digits the C key gave him ten seconds later. No rejections anywhere in the run. **THE NEW ONE: THE ISLAND-BRIDGE REDIRECT FOUND THE RIGHT ANSWER AND THREW IT AWAY.** On crtower2, driving to the exit up to crtower3: `target on different walkmesh island (start tri 37, goal tri 73) -- searching for bridge trigger` / `redirecting to trigger line 1 center=(1406,-384) tri=37 dist=74`. That is exactly right -- the exit is on the far island, the only way across is the left ladder, and the ladder was **74 units from the player**. Then: `tick=120 dist=1708 player=(1432,-404) steer=(693,-1284)`, six recoveries, `moveDist=0` on every one, `A* failed from tri 36` three times, `Cancelled`. Twelve seconds going nowhere. **WHY: v06.01 WROTE THE BRIDGE INTO A LOCAL.** The redirect assigns `_tx`/`_tz` in HandleKeys.
