WHY IT WAS SLOT 2 AT ALL: the chase and train prompts use slot 2 and their header comment says "slots 0 and 1 are reserved for the engine's main dialog flow". That is true of THEIR fields. It is not a property of the engine, and I copied the number instead of the reasoning. **A slot is only free if the field's own script does not use it, and that is a question with a checkable answer** -- one scan of the field's message opcodes, which is how the table above was built. SO THE PROMPT IS NO LONGER AN ENGINE DIALOG. It is a spoken line and two keys: **G to be guided, S to skip.** No window slot is touched, so there is nothing to leave behind and nothing to collide with; the keys are not directional, so answering can never be what starts an encounter; and it REPEATS -- three times, nine seconds apart -- because a sentence leaves nothing on screen to come back to, where a box did. No answer after the third leaves the mod guiding, the mode that changes nothing about the game. AND WHILE IT IS ASKING, THE MOD HOLDS THE LIGHT OFF, writing the same pair the corridor's own Hojo safe pockets write, so a player standing still listening to a question the mod asked cannot be caught by a pulse nobody told them about. TWO MORE THINGS THE LOG SETTLED. "Clear. The light cannot reach you here." is now "Safe stretch. Keep walking to the light." -- Aaron read the old line as "puzzle cleared", stopped walking, and stood in front of the stuck box waiting; the test now fails if the word "Clear" comes back. And the frame rate is no longer an assumption: the armed phase measured **5,297 ms against 158 script frames** and the safe windows **1,703 and 1,734 ms against 35 to 60**, so the field script ticks at 30 Hz and the safe window really is the 1.2 to 2.0 seconds the model claimed. Also confirmed live: `pCurrentFieldId = 846` alongside `pCurrentFieldName = 'sdcore1'` -- the `name='sdisle1'` in v0.99.0's entry log was the documented name-buffer lag caught mid-flight, and the module keys on the id, which is why it worked anyway. TESTING. Seven mutants, seven kills, including both-keys-down resolving to a mode, an unbounded repeat, a hold-safe that keeps writing after the field is left, and the old "Clear" wording. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. NOT SAVED, SO NOTHING IS STUCK: the menu log shows no save after the puzzle, so loading the last save clears the window and the scene can be replayed from the corridor.

## v0.99.0

JUMBO CACTUAR PUT THE PARTY IN EDEA'S HOUSE, AND THE MOD DID IT. Aaron: "I won the battle, but afterward the game seemed to glitch. I heard it say a field name like I was at Edea's House, but I could hear the world map music. The catalog would not populate, and even though I could hear world map music it would not let me save when I opened the menu, and you can save anywhere on the world map." He was right that it was ours. The 2026-08-25 log has the whole thing in five lines: `22:42:13 [VICTORY-THREAD] Mode: 2 -> 3` -- the WORLD MAP into a battle; `23:31:51 [NAME-BYPASS] New GF detected (idx=13), bypass armed`; `23:31:51 [NAME-BYPASS] Patched 0x00470AB9: 0B -> 01`; `23:32:08 Mode: 4 -> 1`; `23:32:08 [fieldload] id=505 name='ehenter2'`. WHAT v0.13.46 DID, AND WHY IT WAS ONLY EVER HALF RIGHT. A GF drawn in battle opens the naming screen as mode 11, straight from the battle system rather than through the MENUNAME field opcode, and a glyph grid is not something a blind player can navigate. So the mod rewrites the immediate in the one instruction that writes mode 11 -- `0x00470AB2 mov word ptr [0x1cd8fc6], 0xb` -- and v0.13.46 wrote a CONSTANT 1, MODE_FIELD. Out of a field battle that is correct: the party goes back to the room it was standing in, which is every GF the game hands you in a dungeon, which is why this has been quiet since v0.13.46. **Jumbo Cactuar is fought on the world map.** The engine went into field mode holding whatever field id was still in the slot -- 505, Edea's House 2, left there by an earlier visit -- and every symptom is downstream of that one byte: the world map music kept playing because the world map was never left or re-entered properly, the catalog stayed empty because WorldMap::Update correctly saw the game was not on the world map, and Save was refused because in a field you may only save at a save point. THE ENGINE ALREADY KNEW THE ANSWER AND SO DID WE. Disassembled, the block the patch sits in reads `cmp word [0x1ce0758], 1 ; mov word [0x1ce0758], 3 ; mov word [0x1cd8fc6], 0xb ; jne ...` and then writes **1 or 2** into 0x1cd2ed4 -- a word read in exactly one place in the whole executable, the naming screen's exit at 0x00470C47, which restores the game mode from it. So the engine decides before it opens the naming screen which mode to come back to, and it decides with `[0x1ce0758] == 1`: equal is the field, anything else is the world map. The same test appears again at 0x00470C8D choosing between mode 1 and mode 2. Two independent sites, one rule. AND THE PATCH REPRODUCES THE POST-NAMING STATE EXACTLY: the naming path sets `[0x1ce0758] = 3` and its exit never touches it again, so a player who completes the naming screen reaches the world map with 0x1ce0758 == 3 -- precisely where the patched instruction leaves it. The only bytes skipped, 0x1cd2ed4 and 0x1cd2eec, are read only by the exit path we no longer take. **BUT THE OBSERVED MODE IS WHAT THE MOD ACTS ON, NOT THAT TEST.** The victory thread has polled the game mode at 30 Hz since v0.13.24 and logs every change; `Mode: 2 -> 3` at 22:42:13 IS the world map, written down, forty-nine minutes before the bypass wrote 1 over it. A direct measurement of where the party was standing cannot be wrong about the thing it measures, and a reading of one branch can. So the sampled mode decides, the engine's test is the fallback for a battle already in progress when the mod loaded, and both are logged side by side on every bypass with a SOURCES DISAGREE line if they ever differ -- which is the only way we would find out that this changelog is wrong about 0x1ce0758. AND IF THERE IS NEITHER, THE MOD DOES NOT PATCH. A naming screen Aaron has to navigate is a bad outcome. A save file that believes the party is in a room it has never entered is a worse one, and guessing is how you get the second. The existing mode-11 path already announces "Naming screen appeared." ONE MORE LINE THAT HAD GONE DEAD: the bypass deactivation tested `mode == 1`, so on a world-map return it would never have fired at all. It now tests 1 or 2. A SPLIT, FOR THE 80 KB CAP: battle_tts_victory.inl reached 83,442 bytes with the fix in it. The naming bypass -- its state, its arm/deactivate logic and the code patch -- moves verbatim into src/battle_tts_naming_bypass.inl behind three functions the victory thread calls, and victory.inl drops to 72 KB. TESTING. tests/naming_bypass_test.cpp compiles the pure model in the same global scope battle_tts.cpp includes it in; nine mutants, nine kills, including the one that reinstates a constant, the one that lets the engine test outrank the observation, and the one that guesses MODE_FIELD instead of refusing -- which is v0.13.46's bug written out as a mutant. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. THIS BUILD ALSO CARRIES v0.98.0, the Deep Sea Research Center light puzzle, which is unrelated and was already delivered but not yet built. NOTHING HERE TOUCHES THE SAVE FILE: the 23:32 menu poll shows the save screen opened and backed out three times with Block 6 still Empty, so no save was written in the bad state -- but the Cactuar GF went with the unsaved session and Jumbo Cactuar has to be fought again.

## v0.98.0

THE BLUE LIGHT IS ONE BYTE, AND THE GAME KEEPS IT WHERE THE MOD CAN READ IT. Aaron: "Starting with getting Bahamut at the Deep Sea Research Center. There is a mini-game / puzzle where you must walk toward the glowing blue light... The trick is that the light pulsates, and you are supposed to walk only when the light has pulsated off." FINDING THE FIELD. field.fs is 294 MB, so a selective extractor pulled the sixteen DSRC fields (ddruins1-6, ddsteam1, ddtower1-6, sdcore1, sdcore2, sdisle1) and their .msd text was decoded looking for Bahamut. It is in **sdcore1, field 846**: messages 17-27 are his -- "The blue light leads all to death.  Turn back...", "You have perceived the resonance...", "Damned imbeciles.  Why do you wish to fight?" -- and its .sym names the whole scene (`Bahamu::bahamu0..bahamu4`, `BossBattle`, and a `core` entity whose two methods are the light going up and coming down). sdcore2 was the near-miss: it HAS a `light` entity with `tukeru`/`kesu` (turn on / put out) methods, but its Director opens with `var[84] == 846` -- the game asking "did the party arrive from sdcore1?" -- so it is the room AFTER Bahamut and its light is scenery. Which also means **846 is not a derived field id: it is the number the game's own script compares against**, so the module can key on the id (immediate) instead of the name (which lags by seconds). THE PUZZLE, DISASSEMBLED. `Director::default` is a `while (true)` of ninety-nine dwords and one iteration reads: RANDOM picks one of three pulse tails; play the wind-up sound; REQ `core::speed` (the light brightens); WAIT 18; **if var[1028] == 0 then var[1024] = 1**; WAIT 110; REQ `core::down` (the light fades); WAIT 48; **var[1024] = 0**; WAIT 12; WAIT 30 / 20 / 5. Two entities do nothing but watch that byte -- `battlekun1::default` and `battlekun4::default`, identical but for one button mask: `while (true) if var[1024] == 1 and BTNTEST(mask) then BATTLE(318 | 319 | 320)`. So the penalty is a random encounter, it fires only while the byte is 1 and a direction is held, and nothing else in the field reads it. The mod does not need to see the screen, count frames or find the light's model. `var[1024]` is at 0x01CFEDB8 and it is exact. AND THE SKIP IS THE GAME'S OWN, NOT A FORGERY. Three trigger lines -- `Hojo::touch`, `HojoHojo1::touch`, `HojoHojo2::touch` -- are seven dwords each and all three are `var[1028] = 1 ; var[1024] = 0`. They are the safe pockets along the corridor, and while var[1028] is set the Director's `if var[1028] == 0` fails and the light NEVER arms. So Skip writes exactly the pair the corridor's own safe pockets write. It HOLDS them, every tick, because `Koe::touch` -- the mid-corridor Bahamut voice line -- clears var[1028] and re-arms var[1024] behind itself, and a skip that stops working halfway is worse than one that was never offered. Everything downstream is untouched: `BossBattle::touch` reads neither byte and opens by clearing var[1024] itself, so the dialogue, the AASK, the battle and the GF all play exactly as they do on merit. THE PROMPT, AS ASKED FOR. On arrival, an engine-rendered ASK on slot 2: "Guide me: I will say Go and Stop as the light pulses" (the default) or "Skip it: the light stops mattering, walk straight in". It opens once the puzzle proves itself live -- var[1024] observed at 1 -- with a settle-delay fallback for a player who walks into a safe pocket before the first pulse, and both paths are gated so the arrival cutscene is never interrupted: var[614] == 1 is the Director's own gate on that scene. It re-arms on every re-entry to sdcore1. THE CUE IS AN EDGE, AND A LATE CUE IS DROPPED RATHER THAN QUEUED. The script's own numbers say why. Armed is 110 + 48 = 158 frames, always. Safe is 18 (the light is brightening but the byte is still 0) + 12 + tail = 60, 50 or 35. **The light is dangerous for more than twice as long as it is safe, and the safe window is the short one** -- which is the whole difficulty of the puzzle. The mod cannot lengthen that window so it must not waste any of it: the cue fires on the instant the byte moves, never on a timer, and a cue that cannot be spoken promptly is DROPPED with a log line instead of queued, because a queued "Go" arrives after the window it describes has closed and the next edge is seconds away. The one thing worth interrupting is our own previous cue; Bahamut's voice coming down the corridor is not. NO PREDICTIVE CUE YET, DELIBERATELY. The armed phase is a constant 158 frames, so a "ready" a beat before the light clears is buildable -- but only on measured milliseconds, not on a guessed script frame rate. This build logs both phase durations at every edge. One BAT hands back the numbers. TOOLING, AND A CORRECTION TO IT. `offline/jsm.py`'s opcode table decoded 0x02 as JMP and 0x46 as MES, which cannot be right in a format that carries opcodes up to 0x155; the real encoding was already written down in `src/field_archive_jsm_decode.inl`, read out of the exe at 0x00530760 -- a word whose HIGH BYTE IS ZERO is a bare opcode, and that is how every opcode above 0xFF is encoded. `offline/jsmdis.py` is the disassembler built on that, and it labels methods by walking the group table (count = w & 0x7F, start = w >> 7) against the .sym's declaration order. One thing worth recording for next time: **REQ's entity index is the .sym's BARE-NAME order, not the declaration order the group table reproduces** -- `REQ 9` in sdcore1 is Bahamu, whose declaration position is 10. Confirmed by five separate REQs landing on his five script ids. TESTING. tests/bahamut_light_test.cpp compiles the pure model standalone; twelve mutants, twelve kills, including the two that matter most -- checking the light byte before the safe byte (the corridor really does reach a contradictory (armed, safe) pair, because Koe::touch leaves var[1024] at 1 behind it) and dropping the cutscene term from the prompt gate. `src/bahamut_light_overlay.cpp` joins field_archive.cpp and field_overlay.cpp in the gate's winshim syntax check, so this module gets a host compile rather than meeting a compiler for the first time on Aaron's machine. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.97.0

A CLEAN GLOBAL TOUR -- NINE FLIGHTS, EVERY ONE ARRIVED, ZERO STALLS -- AND TWO THINGS AARON NOTICED THAT THE LOG COULD NOT HAVE TOLD ME. First the tour, because it is the first fully clean run: Esthar City 367 against a 369 radius, Fisherman's Horizon twice at 492 and 367, the Deep Sea Research Center 213, Shumi Village 240, Edea's House 248, Deling City 217, Galbadia Station 402, Dollet 303; every landing announcement correct, every follow-on walk arrived, and not one [RAG] BLOCKED, "not moving" or "Stuck" in 28,458 lines. The v0.95.0 invariant and the v0.96.0 repairs are holding. ONE. "A FEW TIMES WHEN THE MOD TOLD ME TO LAND I WAS NOT ON A SPOT WHERE THE GAME WOULD LET ME LAND, AND I HAD TO MANUALLY MOVE FORWARD OR BACKWARD TO LAND NEARBY." The reason is arithmetic, and it is the MARGIN rather than the walk. The arrival radius is floored at 288 -- just over the airship's 0x100 move step -- and v0.83.0 set it to clearance minus 96. So a row whose ground reaches only 320 units got a 288 radius with THIRTY-TWO UNITS TO SPARE. The ship is allowed to stop ANYWHERE inside the radius, so what has to be landable is the radius PLUS room for whatever the game wants around the ship, and thirty-two units of that was plainly not enough. TWENTY-NINE OF THE FORTY ROWS HAD UNDER 256 UNITS OF MARGIN. AND v0.83.0 COULD NOT HAVE SEEN IT, because the 256-unit cell grid it chose points on cannot tell 320 units of room from 544. Its bar was met on paper and missed in the game. The grid now only picks a shortlist of the nearest two dozen candidates and the POLYGON measurement decides, so a walk row is the nearest cell with at least 544 units of real ground -- 288 of radius plus a full move step of margin. Every WALK row now has 256 units of margin where the worst had 32. A PAD keeps the old 96: its coordinate is the game's own, cannot be moved to find more room -- the Deep Sea pad simply IS 384 units across -- and all three have landed correctly in every BAT since v0.83.0. THE COST IS WALKING, AND IT IS SMALL: the median walk goes from 641 units to 999, and the longest walk row from 2,346 to 2,404, still inside the 2.5 km the landing test has always held it to. AND THE MARGIN IS NOW A PROPERTY CI HOLDS. The measured clearance ships in the row rather than sitting in a generator comment, so tests/rag_arrival_test.cpp can assert what v0.83.0 had no way to check: every walk row keeps a move step of margin, every pad keeps 96, and no row's radius reaches past its own ground. A mutant that widens one radius back into its margin is killed by name. TWO. "'UNITS' DOESN'T REALLY MEAN ANYTHING TO A PLAYER." He is right, and the codebase already half agreed with him: the catalog has said "Esthar City. 25 kilometers away." from the beginning, and v0.20.88 made the Garden switch to kilometres past five of them for exactly this reason -- its changelog says "one hundred and twenty-two hundred units" is not a distance anyone can hold in their head. What it never did was finish the job. BELOW five kilometres, FIVE SEPARATE ANNOUNCERS went on saying "9 hundred units", which is the same complaint at a smaller scale. All five now go through one formatter in src/wm_distance_pure.inl: 1000 units to the kilometre, one decimal, and the catalog's own spelling. One decimal because whole kilometres are WORSE than the units they replace at exactly the range a walk lives in -- "1 kilometer" for anything from 500 to 1499 units says less than "9 hundred units" did. Below a tenth of a kilometre there is no number worth saying, so it says so. A DEAD GUARD REMOVED RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING: the formatter clamped negative distances to zero, and the mutant that removed the clamp could not be killed -- the "less than a tenth" floor already catches every negative. A second guard for a case the first covers, and an untested one. Deleted, with the reason recorded. TESTING. Three mutants on the formatter, three kills; one on the margin invariant. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.96.0

FOUR FLIGHTS ARRIVED CLEANLY AND THE FIFTH WAS PARKED ON A LANDING PAD THE WHOLE TIME. The good half first, because v0.95.0's invariant did its job: Esthar City arrived at 244 against a 369 radius, the Deep Sea Research Center at 258 against 288, Fisherman's Horizon at 395 against 512, and every one logged "[PLAN] Ragnarok mode -- skipping planner ... flying=1", which is the guard that had never once fired before this build. The Lunatic Pandora detour fired too, on the Deep Sea leg, exactly where it should. Then Deling City stalled twice. THE SCREENSHOT SETTLES IT IN ONE LOOK: the Ragnarok is SITTING ON THE FISHERMAN'S HORIZON PAD, on the circular platform, bridge either side, ocean all round. He had landed. And the take-off check let a grounded drive start anyway: "[RAG] height check: shipZ=-200 groundH=0 gap=200 -> AIRBORNE". A HEIGHT TEST NEEDS A HEIGHT, AND 0 IS THE ENGINE SAYING THERE ISN'T ONE. The FH pad is a man-made platform over water, not ordinary terrain, so the engine has no ground height for it. The gap was measured against a ground that is not there, came out at exactly 200, and landed on the AIRBORNE side of a boundary it had no business being compared against by a single unit. The rule itself has been right everywhere it had a ground to read -- -544 against -544 on open terrain, 900 to 3,400 on every real flight -- and this is its one weak spot. The mod's own reader has a triangle where the engine has none, and it is validated to within 14 units of the engine across 3,852 ground-truth samples, so it is now the fallback: with the pad's real height the same reading becomes shipZ -200 against ground -91, a gap of 109, ON THE GROUND, and the drive is refused with "Take off first." AND THE DETECTOR THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT HAS BEEN DEAD FOR SIX BUILDS. v0.88.0 added the BLOCKED rule -- commanded forward and did not move, two strikes, six seconds, say something actionable -- and it is keyed on a counter that increments "if (s_ragFlying && wantUp)". v0.90.0 then split the airship's throttle off the car's welded pedal, moved it to s_flyCmdFwd, and set `wantUp = wantDown = false` for flight outright. THE COUNTER HAS READ ZERO ON EVERY FLIGHT SINCE. That is why the 19:38 stall took eighteen seconds to reach "Stuck. Cannot reach destination." instead of six to say something he could use. This is the same shape as v0.95.0's planner guard: a correct rule wired to a signal that had moved out from under it, invisible because the failure mode is silence. The lint now fails the build if that counter ever stops reading the flag flight actually sets. AND THE ADVICE DEPENDS ON WHY THE SHIP IS NOT MOVING, BECAUSE THE TWO CAUSES NEED OPPOSITE ACTIONS. Against a structure means climb; sitting on the ground means take off. v0.88.0 said "gain altitude" for both, which would have been precisely the wrong instruction here. It now reads the gap -- through the same repaired ground -- and says "The Ragnarok is on the ground. Take off first" or "blocked by something ahead. Gain altitude", and with no ground reading at all it says both rather than confidently picking one of two opposites. TESTING. Four mutants, four kills on the ground rules -- zero as a real height (which is v0.95.0 exactly), our reader overriding an engine that has an answer, grounded and blocked inverted, and guessing with no reading -- plus one on the lint. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.95.0

THE NEW AIM DIAGNOSTIC NAMED THE CULPRIT ON ITS FIRST LINE, AND THE CULPRIT WAS MY OWN GUARD SITTING IN THE WRONG PLACE. Every [RAGSTEER] line in the 18:58 log reads "<-- AIM OVERRIDDEN", with the aim hopping between fine-grid cells a couple of hundred units ahead of a ship twenty-eight kilometres from its destination: steer(81984,11712), steer(81600,11328), steer(81472,11200) against tgt(54791,5650). Those are walking-path waypoints. And above them in the log: "[PLAN] A* wall-clock bail at 151552 expansions" and "[PLAN] GRID planner ok: ... -> 302 fine cells". THE PLANNER RAN AGAIN -- the same ten seconds of frozen game and the same 302-cell walking route v0.87.0 was written to prevent. WHY THE v0.87.0 BAIL HAD NEVER RUN ONCE. It is in PlanDrivePath and it is correct and it was THIRTY-FIVE LINES DOWN -- below `if (RouteNetPlan(...)) return true;` and `if (PlanPathGrid(...)) return true;`. For every destination the grid planner could serve, the function returned before the guard was reached. A GUARD THAT RUNS AFTER THE THING IT GUARDS IS NOT A GUARD. It is now the first statement of the function, and tests/lint_rag_guard.py fails the build if either planner call ever precedes it again. AND AARON IS RIGHT ABOUT THE SHAPE OF ALL THIS. "Let's make sure to separate the machinery for each of our vehicles... any adjustments to one cannot negatively impact the other. Make sure all the ground-based avoidance machinery and whatnot is excluded from the Ragnarok's auto-drive code." The evidence is five builds long and every one of them was found by a separate BAT: v0.80.0 the forward-collision guard steering the ship sideways down a coast; v0.84.0 thirteen reverse un-wedge bursts fired at a ship that cannot wedge; v0.87.0 the planner handing it a walking route; v0.94.0 the firing-area escape swinging the aim round Sorceress Memorial while the ship pointed dead at Esthar; and now v0.95.0, which is v0.87.0's guard having never fired. Five subsystems, all written for vehicles that touch the ground, all reached through one shared executor. SO THIS BUILD STOPS ADDING GUARDS ONE AT A TIME. src/world_rag_drive.inl asserts ONE INVARIANT, once, after every override has had its turn: WHEN THE AIRSHIP IS FLYING, THE AIM IS THE DESTINATION. Whatever moved it -- the escape, a path, a bridge, an LOS clamp, a corner cap, a sweep, or something nobody has found yet -- is undone before the executor sees it, and a flying drive's path length is forced to zero because the airship has nothing to route around and a non-empty path can only be a walking route that leaked in. THE ONE AIM IT KEEPS IS ITS OWN: the Lunatic Pandora detour, because that is the only thing on the map that cannot be answered by climbing over it. A subsystem nobody has found yet is now covered by the same line as the four that have been. WHAT THIS BUILD DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, AND WHY. The Garden has a genuinely separate executor -- "when it owns the drive the foot/car one is not ticked at all" -- and that is the right end state for the airship too, along with the same treatment for the Chocobo, which nothing has addressed yet. It is not done here for two reasons, both about risk rather than effort: world_map.cpp cannot be syntax-checked against the winshim, so a new executor reaches MSVC for the first time on Aaron's machine with no host test behind it; and it would land in the same build as a fix for a live stall, leaving a regression with two suspects. world_rag_drive.inl is where that executor goes, and the invariant above is what it will be built out of. TESTING. Six mutants on the invariant, six kills -- not clamping the aim (which is v0.94.0 exactly), keeping the leaked path, and four on the Pandora exception. Two of those six only killed on the second attempt: the first Pandora assertion checked that the aim was "outside the radius", which a destination forty kilometres away satisfies whether the detour fires or not, so it passed for the wrong reason. It now checks the aim is at the RIM. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.94.0

THE BOARDING FIX WORKED, AND UNDERNEATH IT WAS THE FOURTH PIECE OF CAR MACHINERY STEERING THE AIRSHIP. v0.93.0 did its job exactly: [18:42:36] the vehicle changed mid-drive -- stopping the drive ... Aboard the Ragnarok. Auto-drive stopped. Cycle the catalog to choose where to go, followed by "Catalog built (36 entries)". No hand-cancel, no stale latches. Then the Esthar flight crawled anyway, and the reason was somewhere else entirely. THE SIX LINES THAT SETTLED IT: [18:43:01] hdg=3200 off=573 err=-573 keys=A^-- and [18:43:02] hdg=3317 off=656 err=+656 keys=-^-R. The true bearing from (82048,11532) to the Esthar landing is 3210 of 4096. THE SHIP WAS POINTING AT 3200 -- DEAD ON -- AND WAS TOLD TO TURN AWAY. One second later the aim had swung a hundred and eighteen degrees the other way, while the ship had moved a hundred and seventy-six units across a twenty-eight kilometre leg, which cannot move a bearing by more than a hair. Something was moving the AIM, not the error. IT WAS THE FIRING-AREA ESCAPE. That machinery exists so a walker or a car does not blunder into a world-map entry trigger's firing area on the way past and load a field it did not want. AN AIRSHIP CANNOT TRIP AN ENTRY TRIGGER AT ALL, and the game's own evaluator says so every tick of every flight: "[TRIGEVAL] ... vehId=50 ... NO PROGRAM IS EVALUATED". Aaron boarded the Ragnarok where it was parked -- beside Sorceress Memorial, INSIDE ITS FIRING AREA -- so the escape armed on the spot, and EscapeSteerAround spent the next minute swinging the aim round the Sorceress Memorial box while the drive chased it. The position trace is that argument written out: ten seconds frozen, then hops of 950 and 2,150 units separated by crawling and backtracking east. Same shape as the forward-collision guard (v0.80.0), the reverse un-wedge bursts (v0.84.0) and the planner (v0.87.0): MACHINERY WRITTEN FOR A VEHICLE THAT TOUCHES THE GROUND, APPLIED TO ONE THAT DOES NOT. Four of them now, found one at a time, each by a BAT. The escape no longer arms in flight, and the site that MOVES THE AIM refuses in flight too -- arming is not the only way that latch can be set, and a leftover from a drive begun on foot would move the aim just the same. tests/lint_rag_guard.py fails the build if either loses its guard, alongside the collision guard, the two un-wedge sites, the planner resolution and the flight key mapping. AND THE REASON THIS TOOK HAND-COMPUTED BEARINGS TO FIND. [RAGSTEER] recorded the error without recording WHAT THE ERROR WAS MEASURED AGAINST, and the one line that would have named the culprit -- [ESCAPE] routing around Sorceress Memorial -- is gated behind DRIVE_STEER_DIAG, which is false in shipping builds because it costs 50 ms of synchronous file I/O per drive. So the diagnostic that exists to explain flights explained everything except the thing that was wrong. It now logs the aim beside the target and marks the line "<-- AIM OVERRIDDEN" when they differ. One glance, not an afternoon of trigonometry. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: the throttle rule. "Aim first, then go" costs about four seconds of turning in place at the start of a drive, and with the aim finally holding still that is a single sweep rather than the minute of oscillation in this log. One change at a time, and the evidence points at the aim. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.93.0

AARON'S DIAGNOSIS WAS EXACTLY RIGHT AND THE LOG SHOWS IT TWICE IN ONE SESSION. "It seems like the first destination I try to go to glitches, then subsequent destinations work fine. I think there is a problem where the mod is not identifying when the player boards/disembarks the Ragnarok." Here is the 18:18 sequence, and the 18:20 one is identical: [18:18:21] DRIVE Start -> Ragnarok at (82117,11779), dist=528 / [18:18:22] VEHID engine vehicleId=50 -> steering as VEHICLE from drive start / [18:18:28] DRIVE Stopped: CANCELLED / [18:18:28] VEHID ... rebuilding (embark/disembark). He auto-drove ON FOOT to the parked ship and pressed X when he got there. THE ENGINE VEHICLE ID READ 50 WITHIN A SECOND -- and the watcher was forbidden to look at it. The drive carried on flying the airship toward the coordinate where the airship used to be parked, with s_ragFlying still FALSE from a start made on foot, until Aaron cancelled it by hand. Only the cancel let the catalog rebuild. Every subsequent destination worked because by then the catalog and the latches finally matched what he was sitting in. WHY THE WATCHER WAS BLIND: IT WAS GUARDING THE WRONG THING. v0.82.0 added CheckVehicleIdChange and gated it on "not while a drive is active", on the grounds that auto-drive injects arrow keys and cycles every vehicle byte the engine owns. That is true, v0.14.94 established it -- AND IT IS TRUE OF THE LOCOMOTION BYTE, WHICH THIS WATCHER DOES NOT READ. It reads the engine vehicle id, which arrow injection does not perturb, and not perturbing it was the entire reason v0.82.0 chose the id over the byte. The guard was copied from the byte's world into a place where its justification did not apply, and it cost exactly the case it was standing in front of. THE FIX IS AARON'S SPEC, LINE BY LINE. Boarding or stepping off is now detected mid-drive; the drive STOPS rather than continuing on stale latches; the catalog is invalidated so the next tick rebuilds it for the vehicle he is actually in; and he is told what he is in and that the choice is his again -- "Aboard the Ragnarok. Auto-drive stopped. Cycle the catalog to choose where to go." There is nothing worth salvaging from the old drive: the flying flag, the landing row, the arrival radius and WHICH KEY SET THE EXECUTOR PRESSES are all latched at StartAutoDrive and all now describe the wrong vehicle. StopAutoDrive is forward-declared rather than moving files: the include order in world_map.cpp is load-bearing and documented line by line, and shuffling it to borrow one function is how that gets quietly broken. AND THE HARNESS CAUGHT ONE OF ITS OWN. The new boarding test failed on its first run for a reason that had nothing to do with this change: catalog_story_test stubbed GetVehicleType and GetBfsRuleClass as functions returning CONSTANTS -- always FOOT, always class 0. A stub that always says FOOT cannot tell a boarding from a steady state, so every catalog test that has ever run against them was asserting less than it looked. Both now mirror world_map_geometry.inl for real, which is the same principle the berth table and the locomotion verdict are included verbatim for: a probe that invents its inputs agrees with itself and proves nothing. TESTING. Four mutants, four kills -- never invalidating (which is v0.92.0 exactly), invalidating with no drive running, invalidating on every tick, and restoring the guard in the watcher itself, that last one caught end to end by the harness rather than by a predicate. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.92.0

THE SETTLE FROM v0.91.0 IS GONE, AND SO IS THE DESCENT FROM v0.89.0, BECAUSE THE PREMISE UNDER BOTH WAS WRONG. Aaron: "You do not have to descend in order to land. Pressing X to land/disembark descends the ship automatically." v0.89.0 built a descent for the final approach and v0.91.0 built a vertical settle on top of it, and both rested on the same unexamined assumption: that the ship had to be LOW to be set down. It does not. X flies the whole descent itself, from whatever height the ship is at, SO EVERY UNIT OF ALTITUDE THE DRIVE GAVE AWAY ON THE APPROACH BOUGHT NOTHING -- and cost the one thing that has ever mattered here, because flying the last stretch low is exactly what put the ship into the Fisherman's Horizon towers at 15:15, and the cruise climb was added to stop precisely that. THE POLICY IS NOW AARON'S ORIGINAL REQUEST AND NOTHING ELSE: "make sure the airship ascends to max altitude when doing auto-drive so it doesn't get stuck against things on land." Climb, arrive high, let X do the rest. RagAltitudeWant takes one argument now and returns one answer. RAG_ALT_DESCEND survives as a value nothing returns, so the axis stays expressible if a reason for it is ever found -- but a rule that starts returning it should be a deliberate act, and the test asserts that nothing does. WHAT THE SETTLE COST WHILE IT EXISTED: up to twelve seconds of holding the arrival announcement back and pressing DOWN, over a ship that could have landed the moment it got there. It was one build old and never flown, which is the only good news in that sentence. AND THE 200 CONSTANT IS PUT BACK IN ITS PLACE. 0x54B860's |shipZ - groundH| >= 200 was read as "too high to land" and it is not that. It keeps the ONE job it has actually earned: telling GROUNDED from AIRBORNE at drive start, where on the ground the altitude IS the ground -- measured at -544 against a ground height of -544 -- and every genuine flight has read 900 to 3,400. It has never once misread in that job. It was never a ceiling on landing and should not have been described as one. THE KEY IS NAMED NOW, BECAUSE IT IS KNOWN. At v0.79.0 Aaron said "I think you use the same key to land Ragnarok that you do to disembark the mobile Garden" -- a guess, so the wording deliberately stayed vague: "Land the Ragnarok to go in." He has since confirmed it outright ("You embark/disembark using X"), so every arrival now names it: "Over the Fisherman's Horizon landing pad. Press X to land and go in." A prompt that names the key is worth more to someone who cannot see the ship than one that describes the intention. THE LESSON, WHICH IS THE SAME ONE AS TWO BUILDS AGO. v0.90.0 recorded that two readings which each explain the evidence usually mean the evidence is not fine-grained enough. This is the neighbouring mistake: a constant found in the disassembly was given a meaning that FIT every observation without anything ever testing it, and then two builds of machinery were erected on that meaning. The gap really was 2,472 units and the engine really does refuse at 200 -- what was never checked is whether that refusal had anything to do with the key the player presses. TESTING: the altitude test now pins climb-always and asserts that nothing returns DESCEND; the arrival wording tests pin the named key, and a mutant that drops it from the pad line is killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.91.0

BOTH PADS REACHED, THE FISHERMAN'S HORIZON BLOCK GONE -- AND THE SHIP ARRIVED TWO AND A HALF THOUSAND UNITS UP, WHERE IT CANNOT LAND. First the good half, because it is real: the v0.90.0 cruise climb works. The Deep Sea Research Center arrived at 221 units against a 288 radius over 97 km; Fisherman's Horizon at 438 against 512 over 151 km, and the tower block that stopped the ship dead at 15:15 DID NOT RECUR. Steady 17,000-unit windows the whole way, heading deltas of 155 to 293 -- the ship flew straight, high, and fast, which is what separating the throttle from the climb was for. Now the half that matters. The two arrival lines: "over Deep Sea Research Center ... 221 from the target ... shipZ=-2840, |shipZ-groundH|=2472 vs the engine's own 200 set-down gate" and "over Fisherman's Horizon ... 438 ... |shipZ-groundH|=2654". 0x54B860 REFUSES TO SET THE SHIP DOWN AT ANYTHING FROM 200, so the drive announced "Land the Ragnarok to go in" at a height where landing is impossible. It got him to the right place and left him unable to use it. THE DESCENT WAS COMMANDED. RAG_BRAKE_DIST is 4,000 and the approach has pressed DOWN inside it since v0.89.0. The ship crosses 4,000 units in ABOUT SEVEN TENTHS OF A SECOND at 17,000 per three-second window; there is no descent of two and a half thousand units that fits in that. And the obvious cure is the wrong one: starting the descent earlier means flying the last stretch LOW, which is exactly what put the ship into the Fisherman's Horizon towers at 15:15 and what the cruise climb exists to prevent. SO IT COMES DOWN WHERE NOTHING CAN BE IN THE WAY: STRAIGHT DOWN, ON THE SPOT. Fly high the whole way, stop over the landing point, and descend vertically -- which is how a helicopter arrives, and the Ragnarok has been a helicopter since Aaron established at v0.86.0 that it can stop in midair and turn on the spot. The arrival is HELD, not announced, while the ship is over the landing point and still too high: throttle shut, DOWN held rather than pulsed, and the turn abandoned so it does not drift off the spot it spent 151 km getting to. The announcement fires when the gap is under 200 -- when he can actually do what it asks. THE HOLD IS BOUNDED, AND THE BOUND IS NOT DECORATION. Over water the engine's live ground height reads 0 and the gap can never close, so an unbounded settle is a drive that hangs forever pressing DOWN. Twelve seconds, then it announces anyway and says in the log why it gave up. An UNREADABLE altitude does not hold the arrival open at all -- with no measurement there is no way to know it would ever close, and v0.80.0 spent an entire build on the lesson that a drive which will not end is worse than one that ends honestly. TESTING. Five mutants, five kills, including the one that reproduces v0.90.0 exactly -- never settling -- killed by the Deep Sea arrival's own number. The bound, the unreadable case, and the not-yet-settling sentinel each have their own. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. WHAT IS STILL UNPROVEN: nobody has yet landed at a pad from auto-drive. Every arrival so far has either been too high to set down or has been reached by hand. This build is the first that should end with the ship low enough for X to work.

## v0.90.0

ONE FLAG WAS DOING TWO JOBS, WHICH IS WHY THE LAST TWO BUILDS EACH GOT HALF THE ANSWER. Aaron gave the whole scheme: "you go forward and backward using A and W just like the Garden does. You ascend and descend using the up/down arrow keys. You embark/disembark using X. You turn left/right using the left and right arrow keys." Read SetDriveKeys against that and the confusion of the last two builds dissolves. Its `up` parameter presses THE UP ARROW **AND** THE A KEY -- one flag, deliberately, because for a car those are the same pedal (v0.14.102, in its own words: "gas pedal mirrors UP arrow"). For the airship they are two different controls on two different axes: A IS THE THROTTLE AND THE UP ARROW IS THE CLIMB. The drive has never once been able to say "go forward" without also saying "go up", or "climb" without also saying "go forward". SO BOTH DIAGNOSES WERE HALF RIGHT AND NEITHER WAS RIGHT. v0.88.0 read the 15:15 log -- UP held, ship frozen -- and concluded UP was the throttle. True: A was going down with it. v0.89.0 read Aaron's "you ascend and descend using the up and down arrow keys" and concluded UP was the altitude. Also true: the arrow was going down with it. The evidence could not distinguish them BECAUSE THE FLAG WAS DOING BOTH THINGS, and neither build looked at what SetDriveKeys actually sends. That is the lesson worth keeping: two readings that each explain the evidence usually mean the evidence is not fine-grained enough, and the place to look is one layer down. ONE. FLIGHT GETS A SETTER WITH ONE FLAG PER CONTROL. SetFlightKeys drives all six: A forward, W back, UP climb, DOWN descend, LEFT and RIGHT turn. The car keeps SetDriveKeys and its welded pedal, untouched -- nothing in this build changes a key that foot, car or Garden has ever been driven with. The two are never called on the same tick: they share the A key and the arrows, and s_ragFlying is latched for the whole drive, so there is no tick on which the mode changes underneath the dispatch. The airship's keys are released at StopAutoDrive BEFORE s_ragFlying goes false, because the executor only reaches SetFlightKeys while flying and nothing else would ever let go. W is wired and unused: the airship has no reason to back up, and v0.84.0 established it can never be wedged. It is there so the axis exists rather than being rediscovered later. TWO. WHICH FINALLY LETS IT CLIMB AND FLY AT THE SAME TIME. That is what Aaron asked for two builds ago -- "make sure the airship ascends to max altitude when doing auto-drive so it doesn't get stuck against things on land" -- and it has not been expressible until now. The cruise holds A and the up arrow together. The approach releases the climb and presses DOWN until the gap is under the engine's own 200-unit set-down gate at 0x54B860, which three arrivals have now measured as the ship's natural resting altitude. THREE. AND THE THROTTLE ONLY OPENS WHEN THE SHIP IS AIMED. With the axes separated this becomes sayable for the first time: do not fly and turn at once. Turning under power is what a wide arc is made of, and an arc is exactly what put the ship in orbit at v0.85.0. Stop, turn, go -- which rotation being free and instant makes the cheap option. TESTING. Three mutants on the new throttle rule, three kills, and the lint now fails the build if SetFlightKeys loses any of its five keys or if the executor falls back to SetDriveKeys for flight -- which would weld the throttle to the climb again and lose everything above. It joins the collision guard, the two un-wedge sites and the planner resolution it already protects. The v0.89.0 no-fly cylinder round the Lunatic Pandora and its eight mutants are unchanged. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.89.0

UP WAS NEVER A THROTTLE, AND THAT ONE FACT EXPLAINS EVERY OBSERVATION OF THE LAST FOUR BUILDS. Aaron: "You ascend and descend using the up and down arrow keys." So every wantUp this drive has spent since v0.85.0 was an ALTITUDE command, and the "braked approach" was not braking anything -- it was intermittently pressing the CLIMB key and calling it gas. The 15:15 log settles the rest without any interpretation. Sixteen samples with UP held and dist frozen at 1806; then, with NOTHING PRESSED AT ALL: dist=1806 keys=U--- / dist=1471 keys=---- / dist=1037 keys=----. FOUR HUNDRED UNITS A SECOND ON NO KEYS. The Ragnarok flies forward by itself. LEFT and RIGHT point it, UP and DOWN take it up and down, and there is nothing to throttle. AND HERE IS WHY IT ALL FITS. Outside RAG_BRAKE_DIST the ordinary steering branch holds wantUp continuously -- so on every long haul the ship CLIMBED the entire way, which is exactly why 151 km crossings sailed over everything and arrived. Inside the brake distance the pulse took UP away, the ship settled back toward its natural low altitude, AND IT FLEW INTO THE FISHERMAN'S HORIZON TOWERS 1,806 units short of the pad. The braked approach was an uncommanded descent, and the cruise was doing the right thing entirely by accident. Three separate arrivals have measured |shipZ - groundH| at exactly 200 -- the ship's natural altitude IS the engine's own set-down gate at 0x54B860. ONE. FLIGHT GETS ITS OWN STEERING BRANCH, FOR ALL DISTANCES, AND THE TWO AXES ARE SEPARATE. LEFT/RIGHT aim, with the tight 8.4-degree cone on the approach because rotation is free. UP/DOWN do altitude and nothing else. The throttle pulse, the overshoot cut-off and their state are deleted rather than left standing next to a corrected explanation. TWO. IT CLIMBS THE WHOLE CRUISE, WHICH IS WHAT AARON ASKED FOR OUTRIGHT: "make sure the airship ascends to max altitude when doing auto-drive so it doesn't get stuck against things on land." It comes down only inside the approach, and only until the gap is under 200, because below that is the ground and pressing DOWN into it is not an improvement. An unreadable altitude commands neither -- with no measurement the honest move is to leave the axis alone. THREE. THE LUNATIC PANDORA, WHICH IS THE ONE OBSTRUCTION ALTITUDE CANNOT ANSWER. Aaron: "The Pandora is directly above Tears Point and reaches up into the sky higher than Ragnarok can go." Everything else on this map is cleared by climbing; this has to be flown AROUND. One no-fly cylinder centred on the CATALOG'S OWN Tears' Point marker -- looked up by name, so the two coordinates cannot drift apart -- and an aim point on the rim, on the side the route already favours, so a ship a little north of it goes north rather than being sent across its face. The route is treated as a SEGMENT: a cylinder astern or beyond the destination is not in the way. And flying TO Tears' Point still works, because a destination inside the cylinder is not something to steer around -- there would be nowhere to arrive. THE RADIUS IS A FIRST GUESS AND SAYS SO IN THE LOG. Nobody has measured the Pandora; what is known is that FH stopped the ship 1,806 units from a point inside it and the Pandora is larger. 3,000 units is deliberately generous, because too wide costs a slightly longer flight past Tears' Point and too narrow costs the failure this exists to prevent. Every application logs the numbers so the next BAT can tighten it. TESTING. Eight mutants, eight kills across the two files, including the two that reproduce v0.88.0 exactly -- no climb on the cruise, and never diverting round the Pandora. The no-fly geometry is held to the four cases that would quietly ruin it: an infinite line instead of a segment, aiming at the rim instead of past it, always diverting to the same side, and diverting a flight whose destination IS the thing in the way. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.88.0

For this hull that can mean exactly one thing. 0x53E6B0 falls through to `return 1` for vehicle 0x32, so NO POLYGON IS CLOSED TO IT -- which means whatever stopped it IS NOT IN THE POLYGON MASK AT ALL. It is a structure standing up off the ground, and Fisherman's Horizon is the largest structure on the map. Aaron cleared it by gaining altitude, which is the same fact from the pilot's seat. THE DIAGNOSTIC v0.86.0 ADDED FOR EXACTLY THIS PURPOSE PAID FOR ITSELF ON ITS FIRST OUTING: every previous diagnosis in this run of builds was reconstructed from position lines a second apart, and this one was legible at a glance. ## v0.87.0

FOUR DESTINATIONS REACHED, INCLUDING BOTH UNPROVEN PADS AND A FULL WALK-IN -- AND THE ONE THAT HUNG WAS A TEN-SECOND A* THAT SHOULD NEVER HAVE RUN. The braked approach works. The Deep Sea Research Center pad arrived at 266 units against a 288 radius, groundH engine=-368 row=-368, "agree -- the ship is over the landing point", and he landed on it; Fisherman's Horizon at 505 against 512; Esthar City ended "Arrived at Esthar City" through the game's own mode watcher, which means landing at the Airstation loaded the field directly; and Balamb Town -- a WALK row, the kind v0.83.0 moved for having only 64 units of room -- arrived at 273 against 288, landed, and the follow-on foot drive ended "Arrived at Balamb Town." End to end, for the first time. Also confirmed by three separate arrivals: |shipZ - groundH| = 200 at every one of them. THE RAGNAROK CRUISES AT EXACTLY THE ENGINE'S SET-DOWN GATE, which is why 200 was the right boundary for the take-off test and why it has never misread. THE ONE THAT HUNG. Aaron: "The first time I tried to get to Esthar City it seemed to get hung up, but once I went to other destinations I was able to get to Esthar City fine." The log says why in four lines: [13:41:11] DRIVE Start -> Esthar City, dist=28005 / [13:41:11] TRIGAVOID plan avoids 2 learned trigger circles / [13:41:21] PLAN A* wall-clock bail at 157696 expansions / [13:41:21] PLAN GRID planner ok: ... -> 302 fine cells. TEN SECONDS OF FROZEN GAME, and then a THREE-HUNDRED-AND-TWO-CELL WALKING ROUTE handed to an airship, which it then crawled and pivoted along at a tenth of flying speed -- 88, 390, 177, 490, 175 units per window against the 17,257 the same ship managed twenty minutes later. AND PlanDrivePath HAS REFUSED TO PLAN FOR THE RAGNAROK SINCE v0.78.0. The code is right there: `if (veh == VEH_RAGNAROK) ... return false`. It never fired, because `veh` came from s_lastVehicle -- the LOCOMOTION BYTE's committed verdict -- and that byte has never once seen the Ragnarok in any BAT yet recorded. Every [PLAN] line in the log reads `veh=0`: ON FOOT, THE WHOLE TIME HE WAS FLYING. THIS IS v0.82.0's BUG IN THE SECOND PLACE NOBODY CHECKED. That build found the CATALOG was built for the wrong vehicle because nothing watched the engine vehicle id, and fixed it -- in the catalog. It did not go looking for anything else keyed on s_lastVehicle. The planner was, and the fix is the same fix. AND WHY THE OTHER DESTINATIONS WORKED, which is the part Aaron's observation pins down exactly: from the Deep Sea Research Center the start and the target are on opposite sides of an ocean, so the foot A* found nothing and returned a three-cell stub in seven expansions -- useless, harmless, and the ship flew straight. From Sorceress Memorial both ends are on the Esthar landmass and FOOT-CONNECTED, so the A* had a real walking route to find, and found it. The bug was never about Esthar; it was about whether a walker could have made the trip. THE FIX. ## v0.86.0

AARON CORRECTED THE MODEL, AND THE MODEL WAS THE PART THAT MATTERED. v0.85.0 explained the 12:59 orbit as a TURNING CIRCLE -- "at 2,500 units per second the airship's turning circle is a thousand units and more across" -- and built a braked approach on top of that. Aaron, who flies it: "you can literally stop in midair and turn the ship in any direction you want. You do not have to turn in a wide circle." THE FIX WAS ROUGHLY RIGHT AND THE REASON WAS ENTIRELY WRONG, which is the most expensive kind of comment to leave standing, because the next person builds on it. It is corrected in the file rather than quietly amended, exactly as the v0.73.0 changelog corrected the v0.72.0 Propagator diagnosis. WHAT ACTUALLY CAUSED THE ORBIT. The executor's vehicle final-approach branch fires inside VEH_FINAL_APPROACH_DIST -- 1200 units -- and says in its own comment: "never stop to pivot: a stationary rotate-and-launch cycle at this range can only ORBIT the aim." For a car inside its own turning circle that is right, and #68 proved it at Balamb. For a machine that can stop dead and spin on the spot it is exactly backwards, and 1200 units is HALF A SECOND of Ragnarok travel. The ship crossed the zone with the throttle pinned before any arc-steering could bend it, came out the far side, pivoted at about 1600, launched back in, and crossed again. The ring in the trace -- 1830, 1770, 1113, 1645, 958, 1618, 1281 -- is that cycle. IT WAS NEVER FLYING A CIRCLE. IT WAS BEING FORBIDDEN TO STOP. And the evidence for the correction was sitting in the same trace the whole time: it holds ONE POSITION FOR THIRTY-THREE CONSECUTIVE FRAMES while it pivots. A vehicle with a thousand-unit turning circle cannot do that, and I read those frames as a pause rather than as the refutation they were. WHAT CHANGES. The throttle pulse stays, but for the honest reason: not to bleed off a turning circle that does not exist, but so that ONE PULSE IS SHORTER THAN THE DISTANCE LEFT -- the 288-unit arrival disc is a tenth of a second of cruise, and a hop that overshoots it has to be undone. The tight aim cone stays, and is now justified properly: rotation is free and instant, so there is no reason to accept any bearing error worth correcting -- aim, THEN spend the pulse. AND THE NEW PIECE IS THE ONE THE CORRECTED MODEL MAKES POSSIBLE. If a hop carries the ship PAST the target, the throttle shuts the instant the distance grows, and it re-aims from a standstill. A car cannot act on that -- stopping and restarting is how #68's orbit began, which is why the branch below forbids it. This ship can. The test is scoped to the braked approach only: fifty kilometres out the distance grows every time the ship turns onto its bearing, and shutting the throttle there would stall the drive before it started. TESTING. Four new mutants, four kills -- ignoring the overshoot (which is v0.85.0 exactly), letting it fire on the long haul, treating the first tick as an overshoot, and treating an unchanged distance as one. Eleven in the file overall. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. WHAT IS STILL UNPROVEN: nobody has flown any of this. The braked approach and the overshoot stop both reach the game for the first time on Aaron's next build, and [RAGSTEER] logs distance, heading, bearing error, cone, throttle and overshoot once a second for exactly as long as the approach runs, so the next log explains itself instead of being reconstructed from position lines a second apart. It is bounded: if it still cannot close, the progress-scored give-up from v0.85.0 stops the drive out loud in about eighteen seconds.

## v0.85.0

THE TAKE-OFF CHECK WORKED, HE FLEW, AND THE DRIVES STILL NEVER ARRIVED -- BECAUSE THE SHIP WAS IN ORBIT. v0.84.0's height test read real altitudes for the first time: shipZ=-1647 groundH=-518 gap=1129 AIRBORNE, and later gap=3133, gap=901, gap=277. The airborne figure is now MEASURED rather than inferred, and 200 was the right boundary -- every genuine flight reads hundreds to thousands of units of daylight. The un-wedge bursts are gone from Ragnarok drives (the only ones in this log are the on-foot walk to the parked ship, where they belong). What is left is the thing all of that was hiding. THE ONE-SECOND POSITION TRACE OF THE DEEP SEA RUN, IN UNITS FROM THE PAD: 1830, 1770, 1113, 1645, 958, 1618, 1281. IT IS FLYING A RING AROUND THE DESTINATION. It closes to about a thousand units, swings back out to eighteen hundred, comes round again -- for fifty-eight seconds, until Aaron cancelled. It never entered the 288-unit arrival disc because IT CANNOT: at 2,500 units per second the airship's turning circle is a thousand units and more across, and a controller that simply steers at the target flies a ring around it forever. This is the oldest failure in guidance and the cure is always the same. YOU CANNOT LAND AT CRUISE SPEED. ONE. THE BRAKED APPROACH. The car's final-approach branch says in its own comment "never stop to pivot: a stationary rotate-and-launch cycle at this range can only ORBIT the aim", and for a car INSIDE its own turning circle that is exactly right. For the airship it is precisely backwards, because the airship's turning circle is BIGGER than the zone. Inside 4,000 units flight now aims first -- an 8.4-degree cone instead of the car's 50, because at this speed fifty degrees of bearing error is a mile of arc -- and then spends a SHORT PULSE OF THROTTLE, one slice in three. Speed decays between pulses until the turning circle fits inside the arrival radius. This is asking the ship for something it already does: the same trace holds one position for THIRTY-THREE CONSECUTIVE FRAMES while it pivots, so it can stop dead when the throttle is shut. Scoped to flight; the car's branch is untouched. TWO. AND IF IT STILL ORBITS, IT HAS TO SAY SO. The BAT ran "Stuck check 1/6, 2/6, 1/6, 2/6" for fifty-eight seconds and NEVER REACHED SIX, because the give-up counter resets on MOVEMENT and a ship in orbit is moving beautifully -- three thousand units a window. v0.84.0 fixed exactly this for the turn budget and left the give-up counter alone, WHICH WAS HALF A LESSON LEARNED. For flight the strike is now scored on PROGRESS, the one measure an orbit cannot fake, so a ring around the destination gives up in about eighteen seconds and says "Stuck. Cannot reach destination." instead of circling until he cancels. Deliberately NOT applied on foot or in the car: there a drive shoving itself off a wall is making no progress either, and the reverse-burst recovery #67 spent many builds tuning depends on those strikes being spent slowly. THREE. AND THE NEXT DIAGNOSIS SHOULD NOT HAVE TO BE ARCHAEOLOGY. Every reading of this orbit so far has been reverse-engineered from position lines a second apart. [RAGSTEER] now logs the control numbers once a second for exactly as long as the braked approach runs: distance, heading, bearing error, the cone in force, whether the throttle is open, and the keys actually pressed. If the braking is not enough, the next log says why in its own words. HONEST ABOUT THE RISK: the braked approach is a control change and no one can fly it from here. It is bounded by TWO -- if it fails, the drive now gives up out loud in eighteen seconds rather than orbiting silently. TESTING. Seven mutants, seven kills, including the two that reproduce v0.84.0's exact behaviour -- the throttle always open, and the strike scored on motion -- each killed by a number from the 12:59 trace quoted by name. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.84.0

THE SCREENSHOT SETTLED IT: HE WAS NEVER IN THE AIR. Aaron: "Somehow got stuck while flying to Esthar City. Took an F11 screenshot." The picture shows the Ragnarok sitting on red rock beside a lake, nose down, parked -- and the arithmetic says it louder than the picture. This drive covered about 2,500 units in 64 seconds. The Fisherman's Horizon FLIGHT two hours earlier covered 63,283 in 35. FORTY-SIX TIMES SLOWER. He had walked to the ship, boarded it where he left it, and driven off without taking off; a sighted player sees that instantly and he had no way to know. THREE THINGS, AND THE FIRST TWO ARE MINE FROM v0.80.0. ONE. THE REVERSE UN-WEDGE BURST WAS THE STALL, NOT THE CURE. The log fired THIRTEEN of them: "Hard wedge -> reverse un-wedge burst 1/4 (off=1568, dist=26502)" and on and on, with the distance going 26502, 26502, 26266, 26028, 25931, 25936, 24108, 24445, 24504, 24202 -- forward, backward, forward. That machinery is a car backing off a cliff it has driven into, and the Ragnarok cannot drive into anything: 0x53E6B0 -- may this vehicle move onto this polygon -- falls through to `return 1` for vehicle 0x32, so every polygon on the map is open to it whether it is airborne or on its wheels. A burst fired at a ship that was never stuck simply undoes the progress it has made, which keeps net displacement under WEDGE_NET_EPS, which stops the wedge anchor resetting, which fires the next burst. THE LOOP IS SELF-SUSTAINING AND IT IS ENTIRELY OF THE MOD'S OWN MAKING. Both trigger sites -- the hard-wedge fast path in the executor and the stuck-check burst -- now refuse for the Ragnarok, and tests/lint_rag_guard.py fails the build if either loses its guard, alongside the forward-collision guard it has protected since v0.80.0. TWO. THE TURN BUDGET REFUNDED ON MOTION, SO IT WAS NEVER A BOUND. v0.80.0 let flight spend a no-strike pass on a real heading change "BOUNDED AT THREE", and said in its own changelog that the bound is the whole reason the excuse is safe: an unlimited excuse is a drive that spins in one place forever and never gives up. The refund fired whenever the ship had MOVED more than the stuck threshold -- and a ship being shoved back and forth moves a great deal while getting nowhere. The BAT reached "no strike 3/3" and reset FIVE TIMES OVER. Distance to the target is the one measure motion cannot fake, so that is what refunds it now; a drive's first check is exempt, because there is no previous reading and starting one strike down is wrong. THREE. AND NOW IT TELLS HIM TO TAKE OFF. Both numbers come from the engine and neither is a guess. The world-map slot dump at 12:37:08 reads the character's altitude as -544 and the engine's live ground height at that position as -544: ON THE GROUND MEANS THE ALTITUDE IS THE GROUND. The threshold is the engine's own -- the set-down predicate at 0x54B860 refuses when |entity.y - groundH| >= 200, which is the game saying in its own voice that 200 units of daylight is no longer "on the ground", so a 199-unit gap is still grounded and the boundary sits where the engine put it. A Ragnarok drive started from the ground is now REFUSED with "The Ragnarok is on the ground. Take off first, then start auto-drive." -- the next action, not a diagnosis. ONLY A POSITIVE MEASUREMENT REFUSES: an unreadable altitude proceeds exactly as v0.83.0 did, because grounding a working feature on a number nobody has yet validated in flight would be the worse mistake. Every start logs shipZ, groundH and the gap, so the next BAT confirms the airborne figure rather than leaving it inferred. TESTING. Eight mutants, eight kills, including the two that reproduce v0.83.0's exact behaviour -- the burst still firing aboard, and the refund on motion -- each killed by a BAT number quoted by name. Two more on the lint. My own test had the 200-unit boundary backwards and the code was right: the engine refuses AT 200, so 199 is still on the ground. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.83.0

THE RIGHT NUMBER AND THE WRONG CONCLUSION, AND THE BAT IS THAT ARITHMETIC HAPPENING. Aaron: "Made it to FH fine, but failed to land at Esthar Airstation or the Deep Sea Research Center." All three drives arrived and announced correctly, so this was never the drive -- it was WHERE it stopped. v0.79.0 shipped one arrival radius for every destination, RAG_ARRIVE_DIST = 512, and the comment beside it read: "The pads are hundreds of units across -- the Deep Sea Research Center's is 768 by 768 -- so this lands on them rather than beside them." 768 ACROSS IS 384 FROM THE MIDDLE. 512 > 384, so the drive was free to stop a hundred and thirty units clear of the pad it was aiming at. The three pads, measured at polygon precision from wmx.obj: Fisherman's Horizon has 889 units of landable ground around its point, the Deep Sea Research Center 384, the Esthar Airstation 465. He stopped at 501, at 464 and 499, and at 506. Only the first is inside its own ground, and only the first landed. The polygons under the two failures say it without reference to any radius: TERRAIN 34, OCEAN, under one Deep Sea stop; TERRAIN 29, A CLIFF FACE, under the Esthar one. And the engine's own live ground height at 0x0203FE30, which the log records at every stop, agrees with this reading at all four -- 0 and -19 at FH, -378 and -401 on the Deep Sea pad, -100 on the Esthar mountain -- so the offline polygon test is validated against the game rather than trusted. ONE. THE RADIUS IS NOW PER ROW, MEASURED FROM THAT ROW'S OWN GROUND. offline/rag_clear.py computes the radius of the largest all-landable disc around each landing point, sampling at 64 units. The shipped radius is that clearance less 96, floored at 288 and capped at 512. The floor is not arbitrary: the airship's move step is 0x100 = 256 units from the engine's step table at 0x53E84D, and a radius at or under one step cannot be hit reliably. TWO. AND THE LANDING POINTS MOVED, WHICH IS THE BIGGER HALF. Checking the other thirty-seven rows found the same defect everywhere, untested only because he had not flown to them: 23 OF THE 40 SAT ON GROUND 64 TO 256 UNITS WIDE. The generic rule took the NEAREST cell that is landable AND foot-walkable AND foot-connected -- and that conjunction is most easily satisfied exactly ON THE SEAM between landable and walkable terrain, which is a strip a couple of cells across. A landing point with 64 units of room is one the airship cannot set down on, because it never stops on the exact coordinate and off the strip is ocean or cliff. The chooser now prefers ROOM, then nearness: among qualifying cells it takes the closest with at least 384 units of clearance -- the bar is the tightest pad, because a walk landing nobody can believe in is worse than a longer walk. The minimum clearance across all forty rows goes from 64 TO 320, every row's radius now fits inside its own ground, and the cost is walking distance: Balamb Town 704 -> 986, Chocobo Forest 4 1797 -> 2346, which is still inside the 2.5 km the landing test has always held it to. THREE. THE ONE NUMBER NOBODY HAS EVER MEASURED. If a landing still refuses after this, the question is whether the ship was in the wrong PLACE or at the wrong HEIGHT, and nothing in this mod has ever logged the second. The arrival now records the engine's live ground height beside the row's own, the ship's altitude at WM_POS_Z, and their difference against the engine's own 200-unit set-down gate at 0x54B860. The 10:08 failures would have shown outright: the Esthar stop read -100 against a row height of -1349. DELIBERATELY A DIAGNOSTIC AND NOT A GATE -- a gate that disagreed with the data would leave the drive with no way to end, which is the failure v0.80.0 spent a whole build removing. TESTING. Three mutants, three kills: ignoring the row's radius for the old constant (killed by the Deep Sea and Esthar stop coordinates by name), treating a zero radius as instant arrival, and a row radius at or under the move step. The Fisherman's Horizon case is asserted as a REGRESSION -- 501 inside 512 is the one landing that worked and nothing may break it. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.82.0

TWO ISSUES FROM THE 09:22 BAT, AND THE FIRST ONE ALSO EXPLAINS WHY v0.81.0 LOOKED LIKE IT DID NOTHING. Aaron: "Catalog is not complete - there are many locations that are not appearing in the catalog when I am aboard Ragnarok. We need to ensure that as the player embarks/disembarks Ragnarok that the catalog updates accordingly... Also there is no entry for the Ragnarok itself in the catalog once landed. Just like Mobile B-Garden, there needs to be an entry for the Ragnarok so the player can navigate to it and board it on the world map." ONE. THE WHOLE SESSION CONTAINS ONE CATALOG BUILD. "Catalog built (11 entries)" at 09:22:17, on foot, filtered to the ten destinations a walker could reach plus his Garden. He then boarded the Ragnarok -- the engine vehicle id read 50 three separate times, and the drive steered as a vehicle on it -- and the catalog was NEVER REBUILT. He flew the entire session cycling the on-foot list: eleven destinations out of the thirty-six the airship can go to. WHY THE EXISTING WATCHER DID NOT FIRE. CheckVehicleChange is driven by the locomotion byte at 0x02040A5E, which DEVNOTES has called an ANIMATION-state byte since .255 and which the v0.20.56 corroboration gate exists specifically to distrust. In this session it never presented 50 for four consecutive polls -- the only verdict logged reads "the locomotion byte said -1" -- and there is no [VEH-REJECT] line at all, so it never even reached the gate. The ENGINE VEHICLE ID at 0x020409E0 read 50 cleanly throughout. The catalog BUILDER has preferred that id since v0.18.3.258; nothing ever WATCHED it. CheckVehicleIdChange now does, and it is safe on terms that would be reckless twenty lines away: ITS ONLY POWER IS TO INVALIDATE A CACHE. It never assigns s_lastVehicle and never repoints GetWorldMapPosition_Active at a vehicle mirror -- the two things that made v0.56.0's Esthar failure expensive -- so a wrong answer here costs one redundant rebuild and the rebuild re-resolves the vehicle from scratch anyway. It compares LIKE WITH LIKE: the class recorded at build time is derived from the id ALONE, not from the builder's byte-then-id resolution, because if the two derivations could disagree a mismatch would be permanent and this would rebuild every tick forever. Same function both sides, so a settled state is a fixed point. Guarded off the world map, mid-drive (arrow injection cycles every vehicle byte the engine owns -- v0.14.94 learned that), while a rebuild is already queued, before anything has ever been built, and inside the world-map re-entry animation window; debounced four polls, because a rebuild runs a reachability flood and speaks. AND IT IS WHY v0.81.0 LOOKED INERT. That build stopped offering Mobile Balamb Garden while flying. This log shows him selecting it at 09:22:51 and flying to it at 09:22:53 -- not because the rule failed, but because the catalog it filters was built at 09:22:17 while he was standing on the ground, and the rule had already correctly decided to include it. A filter cannot fix a list nobody rebuilds. TWO. THE SHIP HE FLEW IN ON IS A DESTINATION. Same slot the ownership test reads, and the property that made THAT test wrong at v0.81.0 is exactly what makes this one easy: ragnarok_pos holds the ship's PARKED position and is zero while he is inside it, so a live coordinate means "yours, and not under you" -- precisely when a destination is useful. Appended after the reachability filter for the same reason the mobile Garden is: it is his ride, not a place, and a walker who cannot reach it still needs to be told where it is. The two injections now share one distance-ordered inserter rather than two copies of a shift-right loop. TESTING. Seven mutants, seven kills across src/wm_catalog_refresh_pure.inl (never-stale -- which is the v0.81.0 status quo and is killed by the BAT assertion by name -- plus each dropped guard, immediate commit, and a flicker accumulating instead of restarting) and the parked-Ragnarok rule. tests/catalog_story_test.cpp drives the real BuildDistanceCatalog through four states and now asserts the Ragnarok entry in each; its exact-count assertions are what hold the shared inserter to the behaviour the two hand-written copies had. WHAT NOBODY CAN TEST FROM HERE: whether walking into the parked Ragnarok boards it. The entry gives him the coordinate and the drive; boarding is the game's own touch response, exactly as it is for the mobile Garden. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.81.0

TWO CATALOG RULES AARON GAVE, AND ONE OF THEM WAS A STRUCTURAL BUG RATHER THAN A MISSING FEATURE. Aaron: "Mobile Balamb Garden should not be an option in the catalog when flying Ragnarok. To get to Garden you land at FH where Garden is parked. Also, White SeeD Ship is no longer on the world map after you get Ragnarok. It should not appear on the world map catalog again regardless of vehicle at this point." ONE. THE OWNERSHIP TEST WAS ASKING WHERE THE SHIP IS PARKED, AND THE ANSWER IS "NOWHERE" EXACTLY WHILE HE IS FLYING IT. v0.20.101 shipped the White SeeD Ship's closing edge already -- disc >= 3 opens the window, having the Ragnarok closes it -- and read ownership out of ragnarok_pos (WORLDMAP +0x18). That is half the answer, and the half it misses is the half he lives in. The slot holds the ship's PARKED position and reads ZERO while he is inside it. It is the exact analogue of bgu_pos, which is why the mobile-Garden catalog entry has always been injected in the NOT ABOARD branch -- the same fact, already relied on twenty lines away in the same file, never applied here. The 2026-08-25 log is the proof, two catalog builds ninety seconds apart in one session: at 23:03:38 engine vehicleId=50, aboard, ragnarok_pos zero, "Ragnarok not held -> White SeeD Ship PRESENT", and thirty-one seconds later he cycled onto it -- "[LOCATION] White SeeD Ship. 59 kilometers away." At 23:05:09, landed and on foot, vehicleId=0, slot live, "Ragnarok held -> White SeeD Ship absent". So the ship came back onto the map every time he took off and only left again when he landed, which is precisely the "regardless of vehicle" failure he is describing. Being aboard the Ragnarok is the least ambiguous proof of ownership there is, so it is now asked first and the parked slot is only consulted when he is not flying. TWO. THE MOBILE GARDEN IS NOT SOMEWHERE AN AIRSHIP CAN LAND, AND FH IS. The log confirms the geography rather than taking it on trust: the Garden's live savemap coordinate at 23:03:38 was (20360,-3850), and Fisherman's Horizon's landing pad -- one of only three RAG_PAD rows in the whole table, picked out by the engine's own poly[14] bit 7 -- is (20480,-2560). ONE THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED AND NINETY-FIVE UNITS APART. The Garden is parked at FH, so FH is not a detour on the way to it; FH IS the way to it, and unlike the Garden it is ground the ship can actually set down on. Offering the Garden as well offered a worse route to the same place: a moving hull with no landing row and none possible, since its coordinate is read live from the savemap and no offline pass can generate ground for a thing that moves. Withheld in flight only -- on foot and in the car the mobile Garden is still how you find your ride again, which is the entire reason that entry exists -- and withheld out loud, naming FH, rather than silently. WHAT THIS DOES TO YESTERDAY'S RAG_OVER_MARKER. v0.80.0 added an arrival for flying destinations with no landing row, because Mobile Balamb Garden was one. After these two rules it has no live path left: the three MOBILE destinations were the only rowless ones, Mobile Galbadia Garden has been retired at disc 3 since v0.20.100, and all forty catalog destinations resolve. IT STAYS ANYWAY, and this is a deliberate call rather than an oversight -- it is the difference between a graceful stop and a drive that presses UP forever, and the ~12 unnamed wmsetus records are exactly the kind of thing that would arrive without a row. A safety net that has never caught anything is not the same as a safety net that is not needed. TESTING. src/wm_story_pure.inl holds all three questions -- does he have the Ragnarok, is the White SeeD Ship on the map, is the mobile Garden offered -- as pure predicates #included by both the real build and tests/wm_story_test.cpp, so the probe exercises the shipped rules rather than a restatement of them. Six mutants, six kills, and the one that reproduces v0.20.101's exact behaviour is killed by the "regardless of vehicle" assertion by name. tests/catalog_story_test.cpp then drives the whole of BuildDistanceCatalog through four flying states against a fake savemap and catches both wiring mutants end to end; it also caught the four undeclared-symbol errors in this change before MSVC would have, which is the gap it was built for at v0.20.99. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.80.0

ONE. THE COLLISION GUARD WAS KEYED ON THE WRONG FACT, AND THE BAT PROVED IT INSIDE ONE SESSION. v0.79.0 turned off the vehicle steering law's forward-collision probe -- the one that refuses to press UP into ocean or a steep mountain -- whenever a landing row had been found. That is the right switch on the wrong signal. The thing that makes the probe meaningless is FLIGHT: 0x53E6B0 falls through to return 1 for vehicle 0x32, so the hull goes over everything, and whether the mod happens to own a generated landing coordinate for the destination has nothing to do with it. Aaron's 23:04-23:07 flight ran the controlled experiment without meaning to. Sorceress Memorial HAS a landing row, so the guard was off: 53 km, arrived at 478 units, correct announcement. Mobile Balamb Garden has NO landing row and never can -- its coordinates are read live from the savemap, so no offline pass can generate one -- so the guard stayed on, and the trace is the airship being steered sideways down a coastline and coasting to a stop: 355, 339, 270, 209, 148, 88, 27, 6, 0 units per window, then six "moved 0 units" checks and "Stuck. Cannot reach destination." Twice. The guard is now keyed on s_ragFlying, latched at StartAutoDrive from the locomotion mode, and tests/lint_rag_guard.py fails the build if anyone ever keys it back on the landing row or drops the condition -- two mutants, two kills. TWO. EVERY FLYING DRIVE NOW ARRIVES, INCLUDING THE THREE THAT CAN NEVER HAVE A LANDING ROW. Even with the guard fixed, a destination with no row had no arrival test at all and the ship would have pressed UP over the marker forever. The three MOBILE destinations -- Mobile Balamb Garden, Mobile Galbadia Garden, White SeeD Ship -- are exactly that case permanently. RAG_OVER_MARKER stops at the same 512 units as everything else and says "Over %s. Try landing the Ragnarok here." TRY, because there is no generated ground under a Garden that is under way and promising a parking space beside it would be inventing one. THREE. A TURN IS NOT A WEDGE. The world map's controls are tank-style: LEFT and RIGHT rotate, UP moves the facing, so a vehicle swinging onto a new bearing genuinely does not translate -- and the stuck detector measures translation over a 3-second window with six strikes. On foot and in the car the turn disappears inside the window; the Ragnarok is slower to come about, and the drive that WORKED spent one of its six lives on a heading change before it had moved an inch (Stuck check 1/6 at unchanged dist=53038). Flight now spends a no-strike pass instead when the heading moved more than ~11 degrees, BOUNDED AT THREE, and the bound is the point: the un-wedge burst changes the heading too, so an unlimited excuse is a drive that spins in one place forever and never gives up -- worse than giving up, because a give-up at least says so out loud and hands control back. Real translation refunds the budget. Scoped to flight deliberately; the foot and car thresholds are BAT-tuned over many builds and this does not touch them. FOUR MUTANTS, FOUR KILLS on the arrival and turn rules; two more on the lint. WHAT THIS BAT ALSO SETTLED: v0.79.0 built clean under MSVC ("Build successful", "Version: 0.79.0"), which was the flagged risk, since world_map.cpp cannot be host-syntax-checked against the winshim. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.79.0

v0.79.0 (#RAGNAROK THE DRIVE -- IT FLIES TO THE LANDING AND ASKS HIM TO SET IT DOWN). v0.78.0 shipped the data; this wires it, in four small edits to the drive that already works for every other vehicle rather than a new executor nobody has run. Aaron answered the two questions that shaped it: "I think you use the same key to land Ragnarok that you do to disembark the mobile Garden. Let's not have auto-drive automatically land and instead prompt the player to land just like we do with Garden." ONE. THE AIRSHIP GOES WHERE IT CAN LAND, NOT WHERE A WALKER GETS IN. StartAutoDrive's whole target-selection tail -- the refined entry coordinate, the decoded firing area, the aim retarget -- exists to make a DOOR fire, and a door is the wrong target for a vehicle that arrives from above and cannot enter anything until it has set down. When the player is flying, the landing table replaces the lot and the entry-aim machinery is skipped outright rather than left free to move the target back onto a footpath. A destination with no landing row is still flown to; what is missing is only the mod's opinion about where to come down, which is logged rather than silently withheld. TWO. THE FORWARD-COLLISION GUARD MEANS NOTHING IN FLIGHT. The vehicle steering law probes the fine grid one cell ahead and refuses to press UP into ocean or a steep mountain -- correct for a car, meaningless for a hull the engine lets through everything: 0x53E6B0 falls through to return 1 for vehicle 0x32. Left in, it would decline to fly straight over any coastline and steer sideways down the whole length of one. THREE. THE ARRIVAL THAT HAS NO FIELD LOAD, WHICH IS WHY THERE WAS NEVER A RADIUS HERE. Every other drive in this mod ends when the game-mode watcher sees MODE_FIELD, which is both simpler and more truthful than any distance -- and it works because walking, driving and sailing all end by touching a door. Flying does not.
