The ship arrives ABOVE a piece of ground and nothing happens at all until the player sets it down, so for a pad the field would eventually load and the ordinary path would cope, but for the other thirty-seven destinations the drive would press UP over the spot forever. RAG_ARRIVE_DIST is 512 -- two of the airship's own move steps, 0x100 each from the engine's step table at 0x53E84D. The Deep Sea Research Center's pad is 768 units across, so a tighter radius flies past it and a much looser one stops short of it. FOUR. AND IT DOES NOT LAND FOR HIM. Three shapes of announcement, because there are three situations: over a pad ("Land the Ragnarok to go in", and nothing about walking, because landing on a pad IS the arrival); over the closest ground with a short walk left (the distance in hundreds, the compass word, and the key that starts the walk); and past five kilometres, where it switches to kilometres and says plainly that it is a hike -- the lesson the Garden learned at v0.20.88, that "one hundred and twenty-two hundred units" is not a distance anyone can hold in their head. Every one of them asks HIM to land. THE STALE-ROW BUG THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET. s_ragLanding is read only inside UpdateAutoDrive and cleared at every drive start, so a leftover row cannot be seen today. It is cleared at StopAutoDrive as well, because a stale row is exactly the shape of the defect that would switch off the ON-FOOT collision guard and end a walk with "land the Ragnarok". tests/rag_arrival_test.cpp is the first host test to compile world_rag_arrival.inl; four mutants, four killed: firing the rule when not flying, collapsing a pad and a spot into one answer, landing for him instead of asking, and dropping the long-walk wording. WHAT NOBODY CAN TEST FROM HERE: the shipping build. world_map.cpp cannot be syntax-checked against the winshim (it needs mmsystem.h), so the four edits above reach MSVC for the first time on Aaron's next build -- they are deliberately small and mechanical for that reason. And no one has flown this: the Ragnarok savemap slot is empty in all 41 saves on file. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.78.0

v0.78.0 (#RAGNAROK THE LANDING TABLE -- DATA ONLY, NOTHING IN-GAME CHANGES YET). Aaron: "We're going to have the Ragnarok soon in-game. Make sure everything is in place for Ragnarok auto-drive ... For most locations Ragnarok should stop as close as possible where it can land and within walking distance of the destination. For those locations that Ragnarok can land on such as FH, Deep Sea Research center, and Esthar Airstation, the Ragnarok should drive to the spot to land on/at these locations." This build ships the DATA that has to exist before any of that can be written, and nothing else: the new table is included only by its test, so the shipping DLL behaves exactly as v0.77.0 did. THE RAGNAROK IS THE EASIEST VEHICLE ON THIS MAP AND THE HARDEST TO PARK. Easiest because it has no movement mask at all -- 0x53E6B0, "may this vehicle move onto this polygon", runs a switch on the vehicle id and falls through to return 1 for 0x32. It flies over ocean, mountain and forest alike, so unlike every other vehicle in this mod it needs no navmesh and no route: a straight line is the correct plan. Hardest because the only question the world map asks about it is where it may SET DOWN, and that is a different bit on a different byte: 0x53E730 reads (typeTriple >> 8) & 0x80 -- poly[14] bit 7 -- and 0x54B860 additionally refuses if |entity.y - groundH| >= 200. THE MASK IS REAL AND IT LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE AN AIRSHIP. Of the 473,193 polygons in wmx.obj, 77,447 carry the landing bit: 97% of terrain 7 and 6 (plains), 99% of 14/9/16/17/25, and 0% of 32/33/34 (ocean), 0% of 29 (mountain) and 0% of the forest types 0-5 and 10 -- which are 100% foot-walkable. You can walk into a wood; you cannot land a spaceship in one. 77,060 of the 77,447 are also foot-walkable, so a landing spot is almost always somewhere he can then walk from. THE THREE PADS ARE THE GAME'S OWN, NOT MINE. wmsetus.obj section 7 (file offset 5580) is a 64-entry table of 12-byte records -- int32 X, int32 Z, int16 height, int16 flags -- and Balamb Town, Deling City, Fisherman's Horizon and the Deep Sea Research Center all sit in it at their known coordinates, so it is the game's own list of places. Cross-referenced against the two polygon bits, exactly THREE of its fifty-two live records are landable and NOT foot-walkable: #13 (20480,-2560) h=-500, #21 (-118784,86016) h=-868, and #27 (54791,5650) h=-1849. Those are Fisherman's Horizon, the Deep Sea Research Center and the Esthar Airstation -- the three Aaron named, picked out of fifty-two by a signature the engine draws rather than a list I typed. A place you can set down on but cannot walk onto is a place you arrive at by landing. AND THE GENERIC RULE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE GARDEN'S. A Garden berth is deliberately held 2-3 km off because the hull cannot approach a town; the Ragnarok sets down in a field, so the rule is the NEAREST cell that is landable AND foot-walkable AND foot-connected to the destination marker under the engine's own step gate. All forty catalog destinations now resolve. Twelve land on the marker itself; the longest walk left anywhere is Chocobo Forest 4 at 1,797 units, and thirty of the forty are under 700. ESTHAR IS THE ONE THE DATA HAD TO ARGUE FOR. Esthar City's marker has no landable cell anywhere on its own foot component -- the city plate is not somewhere an airship sets down -- and the nearest pad is the Airstation 8,249 units away, far outside the 4,000-unit radius a pad may claim a name from. So it is wired explicitly rather than by proximity, which is also how a sighted player gets there: land at the Airstation, walk in. tests/rag_landing_test.cpp holds the table to the catalog it serves -- every destination covered, exactly three pads, a pad's coordinate unrounded (a platform a few hundred units across is not a cell centre), no walk over 2.5 km, and an unknown name resolving to nothing rather than to row zero. WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND IT IS THE half that needs him: no catalog filter, no steering law, no landing. The executor has exactly two branches -- foot and "vehicle" -- and the vehicle one is tuned to a 1,043-unit car turn radius with a forward-collision guard against terrain that means nothing in flight. And nobody has ever flown this: the Ragnarok's savemap slot is empty in all 41 saves on file, correctly, as a disc-3 vehicle not yet obtained. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.77.0

v0.77.0 (#112 THREE THINGS THE 20:25 LOG SAYS, NONE OF THEM THE ONE HE ASKED ABOUT). Aaron: "I think that works! ... Check for any other issues/concerns in the log." The passenger compartment is confirmed -- three catalog entries in that room now, "Yellow Propagator", "Terminal" and the real gateway exit, with "JSM exit 'alien01' ... dropped: it is a Propagator" on every refresh and no dedup line eating the monster. And his reading of the remaining behaviour is right: the terminal cannot be reached before the fight because the monster stands between him and it, which is the game's rule and now applies to him the same way it applies to a sighted player. Three real things in the log. ONE, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COULD HAVE COST HIM A FIGHT: ZERO IS NOT A DISTANCE. Every gated room in the log opens with "gating entN at 0 units" -- on the first tick the rebuilt entity array can still have the party and the monster reading the same point -- and one second after that line rgroad1 announced "Green Propagator within reach. Press Confirm to fight it." with the thing across the corridor. The announcement is the harmless half. The same reading satisfies the RELEASE test, so a Confirm pressed on the frame he walks in -- which is exactly when a player is still mashing the key that closed the last room's dialog -- would un-gate a monster he has never seen, for the rest of the scene. Two entities cannot really occupy one point to the unit; if they ever did, the cost of refusing to measure it is one frame. PgDistance now reports "not measured" for zero. TWO: THE IDENTITY LINE REPORTED THE ANSWER AND NOT THE KEY. rgroad1 logged "alien01 is live entity 3 by **script slot -- a guess**" and never logged anything again, because the line only prints when the INDEX changes and rgroad1's script slot happens to equal its model rank. The model key almost certainly upgraded that guess to proof a tick later and the log has no way to say so, which leaves anyone reading it -- including me, next week -- to conclude the whole room ran on a guess. It now prints when the key changes too. This is the same defect as the v0.73.0 "veto fired 0 times", which read identically whether the hook was missing or merely unasked, and it is the same fix: report the state, not the outcome. THREE: THE NAVIGATION OBSERVER WAS MEASURING DOORWAYS. The two worst readings in the log are rgroad2 UP at DIVERGE=177deg -- delta (81,-1841), the exact opposite of the prediction -- and rgexit1 LEFT at 138deg, and both are timestamped on the second the field changed. Nothing was wrong with either room: a sample is a subtraction between two player positions a few hundred milliseconds apart, and a transition moves the player by teleport, so a window spanning one measures the door. That is worse than log noise, because on a field whose CA is missing or degenerate these samples feed the empirical calibration that OVERWRITES the movement axes -- so a bogus one is a candidate for permanently steering him backwards in the one situation where he has no correct axes to fall back on. The consensus check makes that unlikely; walking through the same door repeatedly makes it less unlikely. The window rule now lives in src/nav_observe_window_pure.inl and re-anchors on a raw field-id change (raw, because the debounced name arrives several samples too late to save any of them). Four mutants, four killed: trusting a zero distance (kills both the cue and the release probes), logging the identity only on an index change, dropping the field check from the window rule, and letting a field change promote a diagonal into a sample. REPORTED, NOT CHANGED -- three things worth his call rather than mine. (a) BattleTTS logs "FFNx=FAIL": the FFNx GF-timer hook finds its signature but cannot locate the function entry, so it is skipped. The native GF hook installed fine and GF reads OK, so this is a fallback path failing rather than the feature; worth watching the next time he summons. (b) Two diagnostic hooks are still switched off from v0.09.08 -- "update_field_entities hook DISABLED for infirmary glitch test" and "Dispatch patch DISABLED" -- sixty-seven builds later, with no record of whether that was ever meant to be permanent. (c) The security-lock message decodes as "[Security Lock Released" with an opening bracket and no closing one, so either the closing byte is unmapped in the row-8 table or the page cut lands before it; a raw-byte dump of that window would settle it in one BAT. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.76.0

v0.76.0 (#112 A MONSTER IS NOT A DOOR / AND THE TERMINAL HAS A NAME). Aaron: "when I enter the passenger compartment the propagator is now frozen and pressing confirm worked to trigger the battle as expected" -- so v0.75.0's cutscene gate is confirmed, and the log agrees: "passenger-compartment cutscene released after 795 deferred frames". "However, I didn't see the terminal in the log until after I killed the propagator. Any idea why?" Yes, and it was two things, neither of them the HIDE filter, which worked: the log carries "[SCAN-KEEP] ent3 sym='comp' hidden but its init calls HIDE and TALKON together" on every single refresh, before the kill and after it. ONE. THE TERMINAL WAS THERE ALL ALONG AND WAS CALLED "NPC". The catalog line at 19:50:30, twenty seconds before the battle, reads "cat0 ent3 model=3 type=NPC name='NPC'". It was in the room, navigable, and named nothing. A sighted player sees a console on the wall and knows what it is at a glance; a blind player hunting for a terminal hears "NPC" and walks past it. PG_OBJECTS now names it Terminal, field-scoped for the same reason the Propagator colours are -- `comp` is a symbol, not a meaning, and the room it stands in decides what it means. TWO. AND THE THING HE WAS ACTUALLY LOOKING AT WAS THE MONSTER, LABELLED AS THE WAY OUT. rgguest2's alien01 script ends in MAPJUMP3 to Aisle 2, because that is how the forced-battle cutscene finishes -- by ejecting the player from the room. The scanner therefore classified the Propagator JSM_ENT_MAP_EXIT, and the catalog offered "Exit to Ragnarok - Aisle 2" standing at (0,-500), which is exactly where the monster is. Then the v0.62.1 dedup did what it is supposed to do and dropped the live "Yellow Propagator" as a duplicate of its own exit. So the room he walked into listed a door where the monster was, and no monster: two entries, one of them a trap. Navigating to that exit walks a blind player straight into the thing the last four builds have been about keeping him away from. THE TALK-SCRIPT RULE COULD NOT CATCH IT and the provenance test is the same one. v0.63.0 already knows that a person you talk to is not a door -- that was Ellone in the escape pod -- but it needs hasTalkSetup, and a Propagator has no TALKON because there is nothing to talk to. A MAPJUMP at the end of a battle cutscene is a consequence, not a route, and PG_LIST already knows exactly which eight entities those are. So a map exit whose owning entity is a Propagator is dropped, and the room's real INF gateway supplies the way out -- which is what it was already doing after the kill. WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL THE KILL, WHICH IS THE PART HE NOTICED. It self-corrects on death: once the yellow one is dead its script's story gate reads false, the log says "JSM exit 'alien01' LOCKED (story gate false) -- suppressed", the Propagator survives dedup and the catalog goes from two entries to three. The room was only wrong while the monster was alive, which is the whole time the player needs it to be right. Four fixtures, four mutants, four killed: the monster-is-not-a-door rule removed (and the diff is the reported symptom exactly -- the exit reappears at the monster's position and the Propagator vanishes), the rule widened to drop every map exit in a Propagator field, the object name applied without its field scope, and the object name never applied. A control fixture keeps a genuine door in the same room a door. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.75.0

v0.75.0 (#112 THE PASSENGER COMPARTMENT, AND THE TERMINAL THAT WAS NEVER IN THE CATALOG). Aaron: "all the propagators, except the one in the passenger compartment, were properly frozen and did not trigger a battle as expected" -- so v0.74.0 is confirmed on all seven -- "Let's try to freeze the one in the passenger compartment as well. I know that one is a bit different but it is jarring the way it works right now. Also, in the passenger compartment is the terminal you are supposed to interact with to hear the briefing on the Propagators, but the terminal is not appearing in the catalog." ONE. THE CUTSCENE, HELD AT ITS FIRST INSTRUCTION INSTEAD OF ITS LAST. rgguest2's Propagator is neither a patrol nor a chase, and neither existing mechanism reaches it: its script contains no ISTOUCHING at all, so there is no contact test to refuse, and the wait after its charge is an eight-FRAME count rather than a wait for the move to finish, so pinning the speed would stop the monster walking and the battle would arrive a fifth of a second later regardless. Worse, the fade runs BEFORE the battle, so anything held after that point is held behind a white screen with his control already taken away. THE ENGINE HAS ITS OWN WORD FOR "NOT YET" AND THIS BUILD USES IT. A field-script opcode handler that returns 1 makes the executor re-run the SAME instruction next frame -- that is how MOVEWAIT (0x07D) blocks: "cmp word [ctx+0x21E], 2; sete al; inc eax", and the executor at 0x005235A7 turns 1 into re-execute and 2 into advance. So the mod hooks 0x04E, the event-start opcode the cutscene opens with, and answers 1 for THAT entity while the yellow one is alive and he has not pressed Confirm. Nothing is faked and nothing is skipped: the script simply has not reached instruction 7. No control lock, no music change, no charge, no fade -- he walks around a normal room. When he walks up to it and presses Confirm the deferral stops, 0x04E runs, and the scene plays exactly as Squaresoft wrote it, fade and charge and BATTLE 816 and the pair bookkeeping and the MAPJUMP out, in their own order. WHY THIS ONE IS DECIDED INSIDE THE HOOK. Every other Propagator is armed by the module tick, which waits for the debounced field NAME and is therefore seconds late -- fine for a monster that has to cross a room, useless for a script that starts on the first frame of the field. So the test is made from things that are true immediately: the RAW field id, the entity's own model id in its live block, and var[446]. 0x04E is a global opcode that every scripted scene in the game opens with, so the probe pins all three: another field, another entity in the same room, and a dead one are each not deferred, because a deferral aimed one entity wide is a room that never finishes loading. TWO. THE TERMINAL IS INVISIBLE ON PURPOSE, AND THE CATALOG READ THAT AS ABSENT. rgguest2's `comp` init is SET3 / HIDE(0x061) / TALKON(0x057). FF8 paints the terminal into the background art and leaves a hidden model behind it purely to carry the talk target -- the same trick it uses for panels, consoles and signs all over the disc. The catalog drops HIDE-flagged entities on both of its paths, and it is right to: that filter was built for the sewer's not-yet-knocked-down ladder and for scene actors parked off-stage. But those hide themselves and say nothing. Hidden AND talk-enabled in the same breath is the opposite claim. So the scanner now derives invisibleTalkTarget -- HIDE and TALKON, both in method 0 -- and both filters exempt it. THE NARROWNESS IS THE POINT AND IT NEEDED ITS OWN TEST. The catalog harness sets that flag directly, so it cannot tell whether the scanner derives it correctly, and a mutant that asked only for HIDE passed all 54 fixtures. tests/jsm_invistalk_test.cpp drives the real scanner over the real rgguest2 bytes plus three copies with exactly one word changed each: init TALKON removed, init HIDE removed, and -- the one nothing on this disc provides -- init TALKON removed and a TALKON injected into the TALK method instead, which is what separates "in its init" from "anywhere in its scripts". All four Ragnarok fields that hide something in their init also enable talking on it in the same init, which is corroboration for the rule and useless as a test of it. Nine mutants, nine killed: the guest gate ignoring the field id, the model id, or the death bit; the hook chaining before deferring (killed by the crash its truncated 32-bit table pointer causes, not by an assertion -- the probe cannot call through that table); both catalog exemptions removed; the exemption keeping every hidden entity; and the scanner asking for HIDE alone, TALKON alone, or either anywhere rather than both in the init. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.74.0

v0.74.0 (#112 FREEZING AND CONSENT ARE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS, AND THIS TABLE HAD ONE COLUMN FOR BOTH). Aaron: "Found another one that activated without me pressing X." The battle in the 12:30 log is on rgroad1 -- the green one in the lift corridor -- and rgroad1 is one of the two Propagators the mod deliberately never touched. WHAT THE REST OF THE LOG SAYS FIRST, because v0.73.0 is confirmed by it: rghang2 resolved to "live entity 2 by model id (model 7 -> 2, catalog join -> -1, script slot 9) (the script slot would have been wrong here)" -- a SECOND field where the script slot was wrong and nobody knew, found by the key that v0.73.0 made primary. rgroad2, rgexit1 and rghang1 all resolved by model id and ran vetoes into the hundreds. The un-latched identity line also did exactly its job: rghang2 and rghang1 both logged the script-slot guess on the first tick and the corrected answer on a later one, which the old latched line would have hidden. NOT MOVING DOES NOT MAKE A PROPAGATOR HARMLESS. rgroad1 and rgair1 have no move opcode of any kind, so PG_LIST marked them not freezable and DriveHold returned immediately -- and their scripts run 0x013 0; 0x05B; PSHL 0; JMPZ into BATTLE 815 and 819 sixty times a second, standing perfectly still, waiting to be walked into. The mod read "nothing to freeze" as "nothing to do". A sighted player walks around those two; a blind player crossing the corridor under the mod's own navigation walks straight into one, which is the exact thing this whole feature exists to prevent. SO freezable SPLITS IN TWO. `freezable` now means only "pin its movement" and the new `gate` column means "refuse its contact test until he presses Confirm". Every Propagator he is meant to choose to fight is gated -- all seven. Freezing is the extra thing the five movers need. In the code the single armed pointer became a pointer plus a flag: s_heldBlock arms the contact veto for every gated one, s_pinSpeed arms the movement veto only for the five, and a gate-only hold no longer waits for a nonzero speed to save before arming -- waiting for a speed on an entity whose script never sets one means waiting forever with the gate open. rgguest2 remains gated by neither, and gating it would be inert anyway: its script contains no 0x05B at all, the battle comes from the cutscene running through to BATTLE 816, and promising a Confirm that does not exist is worse than saying nothing. THREE SMALLER THINGS THE SPLIT FORCED, EACH A REAL DEFECT. The silent-veto warning added in v0.73.0 tested only the movement counter, which a gate-only Propagator can never increment -- it would have accused rgair1 and rgroad1 on every single hold, and the fastest way to make the loudest line in a log meaningless is to print it when nothing is wrong. It now needs BOTH counters at zero, and the contact test is the thing every Propagator runs whether it walks or not. A gate-only release wrote nothing and therefore logged nothing, so "nothing to give back" and "nothing happened" were the same silence; it gets its own line now. And a Propagator that dies while held was being announced as "Released." -- that word is the answer to a key he pressed, and a monster that just died did not ask him anything; PG_HOLD_DEAD lets it go without a word. Eight mutants, eight killed: gating on freezable again, dropping rgroad1's gate, gating rgguest2, pinning the speed on a gate-only field, waiting for a saved speed before arming the gate, announcing a death as a release, testing the silent-veto warning on the movement counter alone, and arming the contact veto behind s_pinSpeed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.73.0

v0.73.0 (#112 THE LIVE INDEX IS NOT THE SCRIPT SLOT, AND v0.72.0 DIAGNOSED THE WRONG THING). Aaron: "Just wandered around the ship a bit and the Propagator in Aisle 6 still attacked without pressing confirm." Aisle 6 is field id 844, rgroad3. FIRST, THE CORRECTION, BECAUSE IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIX. v0.72.0 read the 11:27 log as the battle stripping the mod's opcode hooks out of pExecuteOpcodeTable -- the veto counters went from 27 before the passenger-compartment fight to 0 after it, and there was one "movement veto installed" line and none following. That reading was wrong. The 11:52 log carries the "hooks live 3/3 (re-installs 0)" that v0.72.0 added, and it reads 3/3 on the field where the Propagator still attacked. The hooks were never lost. What actually happened in the earlier log is that the fields either side of the battle were different fields: rgroad2 before, rgroad3 after. rgroad3 is the one that never worked, in any build, and the battle was a coincidence I built a whole release on. THE LIVE ARRAY IS COMPACTED AND THE SCRIPT SLOT IS NOT AN INDEX INTO IT. It holds the entities the scene instantiated, so a script object with no model takes no place in it. Seven of the eight Propagator fields put the model-less "dic" AFTER the monster, so the script slot and the live index coincide and the table was right by luck. rgroad3 puts dic at slot 2, ahead of alien01 and alien02: alien02's script slot is 4 and its live index is 3. Every hold in Aisle 6, since v0.66.0, was pinning dp01 -- the draw point -- perfectly still, reading back its own zeros, and reporting "speed reads 0/0" as proof it was working, while the actual Propagator charged. THE NUMBER THAT TOLD THE TRUTH WAS THE ONE NOTHING READ. The veto only increments when the real entity's script runs an opcode. On rgroad3 it read 0 while rghang1, rgroad2 and rgexit1 in the same session read into the hundreds. "speed reads 0/0" cannot tell a held monster from a lamp post; the veto count can, and it sat in the log through two builds saying so. SO THE MODEL ID IS THE KEY NOW. SETMODEL's parameter is written by the entity's own script and the live block carries it at +0x218, so compaction cannot disturb it -- it is the same key the catalog's live/script join has trusted since v0.62.0, asked directly here because the join is built by the catalog refresh, which has not necessarily run on the tick this module first asks. A unique match wins; two matches is refused rather than guessed, because picking one of two Propagator-shaped things by coin toss is the failure the function exists to prevent; the catalog join is the second opinion and the script slot is now documented as a last-resort guess. The search stops at the live entity count, because the array is refilled rather than cleared and a block past the end is the previous field's. AND THE IDENTITY LINE STOPPED LATCHING. The model key needs the live array populated and the join needs the catalog to have run, so the first tick in a field can legitimately fall through to the guess and the second tick correct it. The old code logged once and latched -- which is exactly why "script order says 4" is the only line rgroad3 ever produced. It now logs once per distinct answer, and names which key replied. AND THE MOD NOW READS ITS OWN VETO COUNT. A hold running three seconds with all three hooks live and the veto never once firing is not a hold losing a race -- a hold losing a race still fires. It is almost certainly the wrong entity, and it now says so in one loud line naming the field, the expected model and the slot, instead of leaving the next person to notice a zero. Eight mutants, eight killed: ignoring the model key, accepting an ambiguous one, reverting rgroad3's row to the slot value, deleting the silent-veto warning, firing it regardless of the veto count, repeating it every second, latching the identity log again, and reading past the live count. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.72.0

v0.72.0 (#112 A HOOK IS NOT A THING YOU INSTALL ONCE). Aaron, after the 11:27 run: "Terminal now works great! Noticed a bug with the Propagators though, after I entered the passenger compartment and the forced encounter with the Propagator in there, it seemed like the freeze stopped working on all the rest ... I got attacked twice after the passenger compartment without pressing confirm as expected." He is exactly right, and the log says why in three lines. Before that fight, 11:28:31: "held ent2: speed reads 0/0, 807 units away, veto fired 27 times (last asked for 8000), contact refused 12 times". Then 11:32:50: "battle entered; field='rgguest2'". After it, every hold, 11:37:05 and :06: "veto fired 0 times (last asked for 0), contact refused 0 times" -- and at 11:37:06 the battle on rgroad3 starts without him pressing anything. ZERO IS NOT A RACE BEING LOST. A hold that loses a race still fires; a veto that fires 27 times in one room and 0 in the next is not slow, it is absent. The whole log contains exactly ONE "movement veto installed" line, at 11:28:25, and none after. THE BATTLE GIVES THE ENGINE ITS TABLE BACK. pExecuteOpcodeTable is rebuilt on the battle -> field return and the three entries the mod had patched -- 0x03D set-speed, 0x079 MOVEAPPROACH, 0x05B ISTOUCHING -- go back to being the engine's own handlers. PgInstallHooks could not do anything about that, because its first line was "if (s_hooksInstalled) return;" and that flag had been true since he boarded the Ragnarok. The per-tick pin was still writing zeros, which is why the speed reads 0/0 in those lines and why the freeze LOOKED half-alive; but the contact veto is the one that decides whether he gets to press Confirm or just gets attacked, and there is no per-tick substitute for it. SO THE LATCH IS GONE AND THE QUESTION IS ASKED INSTEAD OF REMEMBERED. Every tick aboard the Ragnarok, the three table entries are compared against our own hook addresses. All three ours, which is the case on all but one tick in a thousand: three compares, no writes, nothing logged. An entry that is not ours is the engine's -- so that value is saved as the original and patched over, and the log says RE-INSTALLED rather than installed so the next BAT can see it happen instead of inferring it from counters that read zero. THE COMPARE IS NOT DECORATION, IT IS THE PART THAT MAKES A PER-TICK RE-PATCH SURVIVABLE. Re-patching without it would save OUR hook as the original on the second pass, and the hook would then call itself: a stack overflow on the first move opcode, in a build whose entire point is that it does not crash. The probe asserts the saved original is the engine handler and never our own. AND THE DIAGNOSTIC LINE NOW SAYS WHICH ZERO IT IS. "held ent2: ... veto fired 0 times" reads identically whether the hook is missing or simply has not been asked yet, and that ambiguity is why this survived a BAT. It now carries "hooks live 3/3 (re-installs 1)" -- the state of the table right now, not a count of what has happened to it. Three mutants, three killed: putting the latch back, re-patching without the compare (caught by the saved-original assertion, exactly as designed), and dropping the per-tick call so only the first field is hooked. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.71.0

v0.71.0 (#112 THE PAGE LIMIT AT ALL THREE CALL SITES, NOT ONE). The Propagator hold is confirmed working -- Aaron: "Propagator hold worked just as expected / desired." The contact veto does what v0.70.0 said it would: he walks up, nothing happens, he presses Confirm, the fight starts. THE TERMINAL STILL REPEATED ITSELF, AND THE DIAGNOSIS WAS RIGHT WHILE THE FIX WAS IN THE WRONG PLACE. v0.70.0 found the cause -- ff8_win_obj + 0x08 is the CURRENT PAGE inside the message, not the message, so decoding to the terminator yields this page and every page after it -- and then applied the limit to the show_dialog reader, which the 11:11 log shows was already being suppressed on every single page: "SHOW_DIALOG-TEXT win[1] (already spoken by opcode hook)", fourteen times in a row. The path that was actually SPEAKING is ScanAndSpeakAllWindows, which serves both the poll and the AMESW/RAMESW opcode hooks, and it still read to the limit. The log is the sentence in evidence: 11:11:38 "We eliminated all the monsters ... The monsters are 3-6 meters tall ... They are fero"; 11:11:58 "The monsters are 3-6 meters tall ... They are ferocious carnivores ... There are 8 independent m"; 11:12:02 "They are ferocious carnivores ... There are 8 independent monsters ... The monsters can be kille". Each utterance starts at the page he had just turned to, runs two pages past it, and stops mid-word at the decoder's 512 characters. He heard the report four times over, each pass shifted along by one screenful, which is precisely what he described twice. SO THE LIMIT STOPS BEING SOMETHING A CALL SITE REMEMBERS. DecodeDialogPage() is now the function every reader of a window text pointer calls, and it applies the page limit itself: copy, find the 0x01 the engine parks on, decode that much. Four call sites moved onto it -- the poll/AMESW scanner, the choice-window re-read, the show_dialog reader, and the lifecycle snapshot whose whole job is to produce the same string the scanner does, and which would have started disagreeing with it otherwise. 0x02 is a LINE break and still does not end a page; the terminal's pages are up to four lines and cutting there would speak a quarter of one. AND A LINT, BECAUSE THE COVERAGE IS THE PART THAT FAILED. tests/lint_dialog_page.py fails the build if any dialog file decodes a window pointer -- text1, text2, textPtr -- through DecodeDialogWithExpansion instead of DecodeDialogPage. The fix in v0.70.0 was correct and the build could not tell that it was applied in one place out of three; this is the thing that can. Verified by reverting the poll to the unlimited decode: the lint names the file, the line, the argument and the replacement. Two mutants on the page arithmetic itself, both killed: ignoring the page break, and cutting at line breaks instead. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.70.0

v0.70.0 (#112 CONTACT IS A QUESTION, AND THE MOD ANSWERS IT / ONE PAGE, NOT THE REST OF THE REPORT). Two things, both from the 00:02 run, and both were diagnosed wrong the first time. ONE. THE BATTLE STILL STARTED BY WALKING UP, AND v0.69.0 COULD NEVER HAVE STOPPED IT. Aaron: "Looks like the Propagator battles trigger just by walking up to them, pressing Confirm isn't required. Can we make it required? This would give blind players the same ability as sighted players to dodge them." The log has the whole story in one line: at 00:02:59 the Propagator is 213 units away, still held -- "speed reads 0/0, veto fired 464 times" -- and the battle starts anyway. The movement veto stops the monster MOVING. It does nothing about the monster's SCRIPT, which is still running its loop sixty times a second, and that loop ends in "op 0x05B; PSHL 0; JMPB 76" then "BATTLE 85". Holding a monster still and then walking into it is still walking into it, and the Confirm gate was guarding a door the fight was not coming through. WHY NOT VETO THE BATTLE OPCODE. Because everything after it in that script is the pairing bookkeeping -- var[445], var[446], var[447], var[437] -- so a BATTLE that returns without fighting drops the script straight into the code that marks the Propagator dead. That would record a kill that never happened and make the puzzle unsolvable in a way the player could not see. So the veto goes one instruction EARLIER, on the question rather than the answer: while a Propagator is held, the contact test is answered "no", and its script goes round the loop again without ever reaching the battle. Nothing is faked -- not touching is exactly true of a monster the player has not yet said yes to -- and the moment he does say yes, contact means contact again, because a Propagator that can never be touched can never be killed. The hook is the third on the same table the movement veto already patches, it keys on the same block pointer, and it writes the VM local (ctx+0x140) the opcode leaves its answer in, which is why the script's very next instruction is PSHL 0. TWO. THE TERMINAL, AND THIS TIME THE CAUSE RATHER THAN THE SYMPTOM. Aaron: "the terminal still did not seem like it was acting right. I had to press confirm many times to get the full message." His F11 shots are what settled it: five screenfuls, each a clean page of the same report -- "We eliminated all the monsters on this ship", "They are ferocious carnivores", "They seem immortal, but they are not. Killing them in a certain order prevents them from reviving one another." Nothing is wrong with the picture. What is wrong is where the mod reads from. ff8_win_obj + 0x08 IS NOT "THE MESSAGE". It is the start of the CURRENT PAGE inside the message, written by 0x004B9270, and the engine advances it every time the player presses Confirm on a page break. Decoding from it to the string terminator therefore yields this page AND EVERY PAGE AFTER IT -- so the report was read out in full on page one, then again from page two, then again from page three. Each read really is new text, which is why v0.69.0's containment tests could not tidy it up and why its scroll handler, which was a reasonable reading of the same evidence, treated a page turn as a scroll. The decode now stops where the engine stops a page: at code 0x01, the break it parks on waiting for input. What is spoken is what is on the screen. 0x02 is a LINE break and deliberately does not end a page -- the terminal's third screenful is four lines and cutting there would have spoken a quarter of it. The global decoder is untouched: 0x01 has meant "newline" to every other caller in this mod for a long time, and this is the one path that has to agree with a window. NOT DIAGNOSED, AND HE SHOULD KNOW: the mod stopped logging at 00:04:21 with DLL_PROCESS_DETACH while FFNx kept writing until 00:12:20 and F11 kept producing screenshots, so the session the terminal complaint comes from left no log at all. The fix above rests on the window layout and the screenshots, which is enough to be confident, but the confirmation will have to come from the next run's log. Four mutants, four killed: ignoring the page break, cutting at line breaks instead, refusing everyone's contact test rather than the held one's, and not hooking it at all. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.69.0

v0.69.0 (#112 HELD UNTIL HE SAYS SO / THE TERMINAL STOPPED REPEATING ITSELF). Four things from the 23:04 run, and the veto from v0.68.0 is confirmed working first: "held ent2: speed reads 0/0, 2750 units away, veto fired 1138 times (last asked for 8000)". The script asks for the charge speed sixty times a second and gets a zero every single time; the distance does not move. ONE. HELD UNTIL HE REACHES IT AND PRESSES CONFIRM. Aaron: "I had one case where the monster was close by the door I entered and it triggered its chase sequence... could we make it so the monster is held in place until the player gets within 2 steps from the monster and presses X / the Confirm key? That would prevent the player from being chased at all and essentially let them walk up to the enemy to start the battle." The distance bubble is gone, and it deserved to go: a proximity rule cannot tell "he walked up to me" from "he walked in", which is exactly what happened at that doorway. A Propagator is now held from the moment the mod can see it until he is within two steps AND says yes. Two steps is 520 units -- the mod's own navigation logs about 255 units a step -- and Confirm is read from the field button word the fight itself reads, bit 5 or bit 6 (Circle or Cross, D or X on his keyboard) or Enter, because which of those a player thinks of as Confirm depends on the game he played last and guessing wrong means a monster that cannot be fought. Once released it stays released: nothing re-holds an engaged Propagator, or it would be one that can never be killed. AND IT SAYS ONE THING, ONCE. A held monster makes no sound and does not move, so a player can stand on top of one indefinitely without knowing what starts the fight. When he comes within reach: "Red Propagator within reach. Press Confirm to fight it." Once per approach, with hysteresis so pacing past one does not chatter. TWO. THE POST-BATTLE ANNOUNCEMENTS ARE GONE. Aaron: "scrap the post-battle announcements... The whole point is the player is supposed to listen to the terminal in the passenger compartment, which tells them to kill them in matching color pairs. The current post-battle help text essentially does this and makes the dialogue in the passenger compartment redundant." Right, and it is the same mistake the arrival announcement was: the game teaches this puzzle itself, in its own words, at a terminal the player is meant to find, and a mod that recites the rule after every kill has not made the game accessible -- it has replaced the part worth playing. The board is still tracked every tick and the help key still reports all of it, including where the match is. It simply is not narrated. THREE. THE TERMINAL WAS READING ITSELF FOUR TIMES, and that one is ours. "it seemed to repeat itself, like it was loading parts of the message repeatedly." It did: 23:11:15, :16 and :17, each read starting further into the same passage. That terminal's message is longer than its box, so FF8 SCROLLS it and the mod re-reads the window on every scroll -- and each read is also cut off at the decoder's 512-character limit, so consecutive reads OVERLAP WITHOUT EITHER CONTAINING THE OTHER. Both of the containment tests already in the dialog code need containment. Both fail. It speaks again. The signature of a scroll is that the new read STARTS somewhere inside the old one, and that is what the new rule looks for -- and it does something better than suppressing: it works out how much of the new read is genuinely new and speaks only that, backed up to a word boundary because read one had been cut mid-word. So the passage is spoken once, in order, ending where it actually ends. Suppressing outright would have lost "That is all the information we have. Good luck" for good, which is the sentence that matters. Only for long passages: forty characters have to match and both strings must be longer than that, so two short prompts sharing an opening can never be mistaken for a scroll. FOUR. WHY THE PASSENGER-CABIN ONE IS STILL NOT HELD, and it is not an oversight. rgguest2's Propagator is not a patrol or a chase, it is a cutscene: its script runs straight through -- fade, a scripted approach through opcodes 0x0F2/0x0F5, screen flash, BATTLE 816, the pair bookkeeping -- and ends in the MAPJUMP3 out of the room. Its move is not the 0x03D/0x079 pair the veto covers, so holding it would mean blocking that scripted approach behind an already-faded screen with no way out but the jump the script never reaches. That battle is unavoidable by design and it is one charge, once. The catalog names it; the mod leaves it alone. The scroll rule now lives in src/dialog_scroll_pure.inl, included by the shipping path and by tests/dialog_scroll_test.cpp, which drives it with the three real strings out of Aaron's own log. Six mutants, six killed: always suppressing, losing the word boundary, dropping the length floor, releasing on proximity again, re-holding after engagement, and dropping the reach cue. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.68.0

v0.68.0 (#112 THE PIN LOST A RACE, SO IT STOPPED RACING). Aaron's first run at the Propagators: "Suppression didn't seem to work as I stood still and each one ran for me it seemed." He is right, and the log agrees with him in every field. Take rgroad2: "16:25:10 holding ent2 still at 2595 units (speed 7929/7929 saved)" and then, two seconds later, "16:25:12 released ent2 (he walked into range)". He did not walk anywhere. The distance fell from 2595 to under 600 in two seconds -- about 930 units a second, which is a charge speed of 8000 through the engine's own >> 8. The Propagator crossed the room while the mod held it still, and the same shape appears in rghang1, rghang2 and rgexit1. WHY IT FAILED, and the v0.66.0 comment said so out loud without either of us noticing what it meant: "the pin is a race with the script and the loser of that race is the player." Writing [ent+0x1FE] once per mod tick is a race against a script that re-issues its speed every few frames, and a mod tick is not a frame. Every tick wrote a zero; in between, the script wrote 8000 back and the engine spent the gap walking. SO IT STOPS RACING AND VETOES AT THE SOURCE. The mod already patches the field opcode table for the Trabia dragon's ANIME hook, and the same one line does it here. Opcode 0x03D is "set this entity's move speed" (0x005233E0, writes +0x1FE and +0x200) and 0x079 is MOVEAPPROACH, which copies +0x200 into +0x1FE when a move starts. Both receive THE ENTITY'S OWN VM CONTEXT as their first argument -- the same block the speed lives in -- so the hook does not have to guess who is calling. It lets the original run, and if the caller is the Propagator being held it puts the zero back inside the same call, before the movement pass can read it. Frame-exact by construction, and no amount of looping can outrun it. The per-tick pin stays as belt and braces. AND IT REPORTS ON THE THING IT IS HOLDING, not on itself. The failed run produced a log full of confident "holding" lines with a monster crossing the room underneath them, which is exactly how it went unnoticed for a whole scene. Once a second while a hold is on, the log now carries what the entity's speed words ACTUALLY read, how far away it is, how many times the veto fired and what the script last asked for. If the next run still fails, that line says which of the four possible reasons it is. A BUG IN THE FIX, CAUGHT BY MUTATING IT: PgZeroIfHeld wrote through s_heldBlock rather than through the ctx it was handed. Equal by the guard above it, so it worked -- and a mutant that removed the guard still passed, because the veto went on zeroing the right entity for the wrong reason. It writes through the argument now, and the probe asserts that a call about somebody else does nothing at all, not even to the entity being held. NOTED, NOT YET FIXED: rghang2's live index is unstable -- the model join answered -1 on the first visit and 2 on the second, while the field's own script order says 9, and the log shouted about the disagreement exactly as it was built to. The hold works either way for now because the veto keys on the block pointer, but the identification needs settling and the next run's diagnostic line will say which index is actually moving. Four mutants, four killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.67.3

v0.67.3 (#105 THE LEGEND NAMES ITS KEY / THE BOX GETS OUT OF THE WAY). Two things from the 15:05 Trabia BAT, and the second is much bigger than the scene it was found in. FIRST, THE BOX WORKED AND THEN SAT UNDER THE SCENE'S OWN LEGENDS. "[BGBTL-DLG] window 7 opened ... box 193x133 at (55,8)" and "[DRAGON] controls box open in the game's own window" -- exactly as asked, in FF8's own grey window with its own font. And the shot shows the dragon fight's own two legend boxes, "A to defend!" and "W to attack!", sitting on top of its left-hand third with the first three lines behind them. Slot 7 really was free; the collision was POSITIONAL, and no amount of checking ctx+0xD3 would have caught it. A fixed corner cannot fix it either: the Garden battle parks at the top because ITS legend is at the bottom, and Trabia's is at the top. So the box asks. Every window carries its rectangle at +0x00 and its open flag at +0x16, so the mod reads what is on screen and places itself somewhere else -- five candidates, top first so the two scenes where it was already right do not move, and if every one collides the least-covered wins and the log says so, because a partly covered box still beats no box. The placement is pure arithmetic in PlaceBriefBox and the probe checks it against Trabia's real geometry, the Garden battle's, an empty screen and a screen with no clear space at all. SECOND, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: THE BUTTON ICON WAS BEING THROWN AWAY. Aaron: "the legend doesn't announce the actual controls. Can we ensure as those legend items appear they also announce their respective control?" They could not. FF8 text code 0x05 draws the key bound to a game action, and this mod's decoder dropped it as "no text by design" -- so tvglen3 string 23, which is 05 27 followed by " to defend!", reached him as "to defend!" with no subject at all. THIS IS NOT ONE SCENE. A scan of all 841 field .msd files finds 183 of them, twelve distinct buttons: "{Square} to defend", "Press the {Select}", "{Start} to end concert", "{L1} to quit". Every one is a prompt whose entire content is the icon, and every one has been silent. THE RESOLUTION IS THE ENGINE'S OWN. Parameter 0x20..0x2F is an action index remapped through the savemap at 0x01CFE740 when 0x01CFE73C bit 0x20 is set; 0x30..0x3F is the pad button directly; the button indexes the live keymap at 0x01CD0208 + device*0x20 + button, device chosen by 0x00B8600E and falling back to the keyboard exactly as sub_4A2F80 does. Verified against his own screenshot: 05 24 is action 4, Triangle, keymap 0x11, W; 05 27 is Square, 0x1E, A. WE NAME THE SCANCODE OURSELVES rather than reading the engine's string table at 0x00B86010, and the second reason is the important one: that table is written for a four-character on-screen slot, so Escape is "ES", numpad 7 is "N7", and Enter, Space, Backspace and both Page keys are all literally "NONE". Reading "NONE to end concert" to a blind player would be worse than the silence it replaces. AND IT IS TESTABLE NOW. The resolution reads fixed engine addresses, which is to say code that would otherwise only ever be checked by playing the game -- and this code decides what a blind player is told to press. One read path behind a hook the probe fills in, and tests/text_decode_compile.cpp puts Aaron's own keymap in front of it and asserts the sentences: "A to defend!", "W to attack!", Start on Space named as Space where the engine gives up, an unbound button naming nothing and counting the loss, a truncated string reading no further, and a pad touched once falling back to the keyboard binding rather than silencing every prompt in the game for the rest of the session. Six mutants, six killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.67.2

v0.67.2 (#105/#minigame-bgbtl CONSISTENT CONTROLS BOXES). Aaron: "Can you verify that the Garden Battle punch mini-game and the Trabia Canyon Dragon Fight mini-game also use an in-game dialog like this for displaying their Game Controls at the start of the mini-game? We want to be consistent whenever we implement a Game Controls dialog prior to the start of a mini-game." Verified, and one of the two was not. THE GARDEN BATTLE ALREADY DOES -- field_minigame_bgbtl.inl:1013 calls the same OpenBriefDialog the space rescue does, and it is where that facility was written. THE TRABIA DRAGON DID NOT. It was spoken and nothing more: DfSay and no window anywhere in the module, so anyone watching had no idea what the mod had just told him. It has a box now, opened through the same call, and closed from three places -- Enter or the timeout or the skip, the death that ends a round, and Reset -- for the same reason the space rescue releases its freeze from four: no arrangement of keys may leave one up over the scene that follows. SEPARATE SCREEN TEXT, because the spoken brief is a paragraph and the box cannot be. FF8 sizes the window to its text and clamps there: past about 34 columns a line wraps, past ten rows the box scrolls sixteen frames at a time and has lost its opening lines by the time anyone reads them. DF_SCREEN_FMT lives in dragon_fight_model.inl -- the pure model -- precisely so the probe can measure it without a Trabia Canyon, and THE PROBE IMMEDIATELY EARNED ITS KEEP: the first draft put both keys on one line, "Hold %s block   Tap %s attack", and it measured THIRTY-FIVE columns the moment it was given a five-letter key name like "Space". One column past the wrap, in a scene nobody would have looked at again. A line each, 32 columns by 7 lines, checked at both the widest and the narrowest key names the learner can produce. AND THE FACILITY IS NOW SAFE TO REUSE. It began as one screen in one fight, where window 7 had been observed free; it is now the house style for three, and the next scene to use it is one nobody has checked. OpenBriefDialog reads the engine's own per-window open mask at ctx+0xD3 first and REFUSES a slot the game already owns -- because taking it would replace the game's text with ours and say nothing about it, which is worse than not drawing at all. The briefing is still spoken; the log says why the box is missing. THE ENCODER GETS A COVERAGE TEST rather than a per-screen one. Three mini-games share it and a fourth will be written by somebody who assumes the punctuation works, so the probe now requires the whole ordinary printable set -- letters, digits, and !"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?[]_ -- to have a glyph code. That is the check that would have caught v0.67.0's missing colon eleven months earlier than a screenshot did. Four mutants, four killed: a too-wide line, a too-tall screen, a dropped semicolon, and taking an occupied window. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.67.1

v0.67.1 (#111 THE PUNCTUATION THE ENCODER WAS EATING). v0.67.0 worked. The 14:11 capture is the first picture ever taken of this box with all ten lines in it: FF8's own grey window, its own font, its own border, at (44,8) measuring 215x181 in the game's 320x224 space -- REACHING RINOA, the pause lines, HOLD an arrow down, right down to Enter start / repeat / F9 skip. The log agrees: "freezing after 203 ms -- the game's box reports its text complete", and the mod's own overlay stayed down, so there is one box on the screen and it is the game's. The frozen-field measurement held too: TWO frames presented across a twenty-seven second pause. AND THE PICTURE IMMEDIATELY SHOWED SOMETHING NO LOG WOULD HAVE. It read "Boost  hold W." instead of "Boost: hold W.", "4x speed  burns boost fuel." instead of the semicolon, " Centred  means let go." with the quotes gone, and "Enter start  repeat F9 skip" with the slash gone. EncodeChar's `default: return 0x20` had been turning every punctuation mark outside a hand-written five-case switch into a space, silently, since v0.20.123 -- in this box and in the Garden battle's briefing before it. THE FIX IS THE MOD'S OWN TABLE. ff8_text_decode.cpp already carries the 224-entry glyph grid that turns these bytes back into text everywhere else in the mod; the encoder now uses the codes read out of it, so the two cannot disagree about a character. Colon 0x2D, semicolon 0xB5, slash 0x2C, plus the twenty-odd others the grid has and the switch did not -- brackets, dollar, percent, plus, minus, equals, ampersand, asterisk, parentheses, underscore, angle brackets. The double quote is the one exception and is documented as such: the grid is blank there because FF8 uses the Japanese quote pair, and the decoder maps 0x3E to '"', so encoding to 0x3E round-trips through the mod's own reader and draws the game's own opening quote. Unknown characters still become spaces, which is still right -- a glyph the font does not have cannot be drawn -- but the set that falls into it is now accented letters rather than the colon. THE PROBE NOW ASKS THE QUESTION THE SCREENSHOT ASKED: take the text the mod actually puts on the screen and require that no character in it encodes to a space unless it IS one. That assertion fails on the v0.67.0 encoder and names the first character it loses. Two mutants, two killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.67.0

v0.67.0 (#111 THE GAME'S OWN WINDOW, FINISHED). Aaron, on the mod's Game Controls screen: "I don't think it looks very good if our injected dialogs / text doesn't look the same as the rest of the game... for now let's just focus on consistency." He asked for the game's own font at the game's size, and the right way to get that is not to imitate FF8's font -- it is to keep using FF8's window, which this code has been opening since v0.63.0 through the game's own set_window_object / measure_text / open_window, and to stop it being caught half-typed. WHY IT WAS ALWAYS HALF-TYPED. The window is drawn by field_main, so whatever it has managed to type at the instant the byte at 0x00471F70 becomes 0xC3 is what stays on the screen for the entire pause -- and v0.66.1 established that the frozen field then presents nothing at all, so that frame is frozen too. Every screenshot of this scene shows the consequence: "REACHING RIN" in the 22:45 run, "REACHING RINOA" plus a stray "N" at 00:05. THE FIX IS ONE ENGINE CALL. The window state array is 0x01D2B330 + winId*0x3C. Its +0x10 is the text speed in 4.12 fixed point, accumulated at 0x004A000A -- and 0x004A0013 SHORT-CIRCUITS THE GATE WHEN THE SPEED IS ZERO, after which 0x004A010A..0x004A0113 selects "consume the next character" rather than "re-check the gate" and re-enters the dispatcher inside the same frame. So speed 0 does not mean fast, it means the whole string is consumed in ONE update and the box is complete on the tick it opens. That is in-domain rather than invented: it is exactly what the game's own {SPEED 1} text opcode writes at 0x004A00AC, through the same setter at 0x0049FBC0 that the field itself calls for all eight windows on every field init. The opener is now the instant variant at 0x004A0640 as well, because 0x004A0620 animates the frame over eight frames and types nothing until the scale reaches 0x1000. AND IT WAITS FOR THE ENGINE TO SAY SO rather than trusting that it worked. +0x28 is the window's own "message complete" flag, set at 0x004A0144 when the terminator is reached; 0x004A06E0 is a one-line accessor for it and the field MESSAGE opcode polls it exactly this way at 0x00529956. The freeze now holds off until that byte reads 1, with SP_DRAW_MS still the floor and a two-second cap above it -- and if the cap ever fires the log says the box on screen may be part-typed, rather than letting a silent half-message pass for a working one. THE MOD'S OWN OVERLAY BECOMES THE FALLBACK. Showing both put our 372x240 box inside the game's 459x320 one, which is what the 13:12 frame actually shows; it is now drawn only when the game's window will not open. Everything the last six builds learned about it stays in place and working -- it is simply not the box the player looks at any more. ALSO FIXED, FOUND ON THE WAY: ADDR_CLOSE_WINDOW was 0x0049FBF0, which is not a closer at all. It returns the i16 at +0x1C, the window's open scale (0x0049FBFA). Closing appeared to work because the two ctx bits cleared underneath it took the box off screen. The engine's closers are 0x004A0660 (animated) and 0x004A0680 (immediate); the immediate one is now used, because this box is dismissed by a keypress the player has already made. THE PROBE OWNS THE NEW CONTRACT: the field is still running while the box is mid-sentence, stops the instant +0x28 reads complete, says which of the two reasons it froze for, does not put our overlay up beside the game's, and freezes on the cap with a warning when the flag never arrives. Four mutants, four killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.66.2

v0.66.2 (#111 THE BOX IS ON THE SCREEN). Five builds after Aaron asked "is there anything we can do to get the Game Controls visible on the screen?", here is the picture: Logs/screenshots/overlay_521156.png, 640x480, the mod's own box at (134,120) measuring 372x240, ten lines of white text on the dark ground inside its light border -- REACHING RINOA, the pause lines, HOLD an arrow down, Boost: hold W, right down to "Enter start / repeat F9 skip" -- next to the game's own 1:28 timer on an otherwise black frame. The measurement agrees with the picture rather than standing in for it: "IN THE CAPTURE: ink per line 97,157,136,141,128,68,137,102,124,137", taken inside DoGLCapture from the bytes that became that PNG, matching the read-back number for number. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, after four wrong answers: bgfx leaves a SHADER PROGRAM BOUND. Every fixed-function fragment the overlay produced ran through it, got resolved against bgfx's own textures, and vanished -- with glGetError clean throughout, which is exactly why nothing ever looked broken. v0.66.0 unbinds it; that was the fix. AND THE DIAGNOSTIC RULED OUT ITS OWN ALTERNATIVES IN THE SAME RUN. Beacon B is a bare glDrawPixels of one constant colour and it came back at exactly 0/255/255, so the pixel-transfer path was never at fault and neither was the RGBA stride that v0.65.3 chased; beacon A, a glBegin quad, came back at exactly 255/0/255, so fixed-function geometry reaches the screen too. The textured-quad path added alongside is therefore belt and braces rather than the cure, and it stays: it costs one quad a frame and it is insurance against the next driver or the next FFNx. Both beacons are now GATED OFF rather than deleted -- FP_BEACONS 0 -- because a diagnostic that has to be rewritten from scratch is one nobody reruns, and because two coloured squares in the corner are not something to leave in a build Aaron cannot see. THE SELF-CAPTURE STAYS ON. It is the only channel through which anyone finds out what this box looks like, it costs 16 KB once per scene, and it fires 90 ms after the box opens -- in the gap before the freeze, which is the only window a capture can be serviced in. AND THE FROZEN-FIELD FINDING SURVIVED CONTACT WITH ITS OWN MEASUREMENT, slightly bruised. The engine presented ONE frame across a twenty-five second pause, not the literal zero the first draft asserted. The difference does not matter and the log no longer pretends otherwise: it reports the count and the duration, calls two frames or fewer a stopped engine, and leaves the reader to draw the line rather than tripping over an exact threshold. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.66.1

v0.66.1 (#111 THE FROZEN FIELD PRESENTS NO FRAMES). The 12:39 BAT finally says where the overlay has been, and the answer is not a GL problem at all -- it is a premise in my own header that has been false since v0.65.0. FIRST, THE STATE LINE PAID FOR ITSELF: "draw fbo=0 read fbo=0 program=3 texture unit=0x84C0 vao=0 ... GL 4.6.0 Intel Arc 140V". A SHADER PROGRAM WAS BOUND, which would indeed have swallowed every fixed-function fragment we drew, and v0.66.0 unbinds it. The framebuffer half of the guess was wrong: bgfx had 0 bound, so we were always drawing at the window. BUT THE SHOT STILL CAME BACK WITH NOTHING IN IT -- no box, and not one pixel of either beacon, including a solid 48x48 magenta quad. Two things in that log explain it together. The overlay logged "first blit" ONCE, at 12:39:35, in the 200 ms between the box opening and the freeze engaging -- and never again, not even after the second Show at 12:39:43 which resets that latch. And ProbeCapture, which measures the capture buffer from inside DoGLCapture, never logged AT ALL, across two F11 presses. Then the filesystem closed it: Aaron pressed F11 twice, at 12:39:40 and 12:39:50, and there is exactly ONE file -- written at 12:39:51.996, the precise second Enter released the freeze. THE FROZEN FIELD DOES NOT PRESENT. No SwapBuffers means the hook does not run, which means the overlay does not draw, DoGLCapture does not fire, and an F11 pressed during the pause sits unserviced until the swap after Enter -- by which time Hide() has run and the box is gone. Three builds of GL forensics were investigating a frame that was never rendered. THE LINE IN field_overlay.h THAT SAID THE OPPOSITE -- "the SwapBuffers hook is the one part of the render path the field freeze does not touch", with Aaron's screenshot cited as proof -- is now marked as the mistake it was. AND IT MAY NOT MATTER, WHICH IS THE GOOD NEWS. If the engine stops presenting, THE LAST FRAME IT PRESENTED STAYS ON THE SCREEN. The box does not need to be drawn during the pause; it needs to be in the frame that is on screen WHEN the pause begins -- which is exactly what the SP_DRAW_MS gap between opening the box and engaging the freeze already arranges, and what the read-back has been confirming all along. What could never work was capturing it. SO THIS BUILD MEASURES BOTH THINGS INSTEAD OF ASSERTING THEM. NoteSwap() counts every presented frame from the top of the hook, unconditionally, so the count is a fact about the ENGINE rather than about whether the overlay happened to be drawing; the space rescue records it at engage and reports the delta on release. Zero across a pause proves the finding; anything else disproves it, and either way it is one line in the next log. AND THE MOD NOW TAKES ITS OWN SHOT, in the only window where a shot is possible: 90 ms after the box opens, 110 ms before the field stops, one request per scene, on the next swap. That image is the first that can contain the box, and it settles a question three builds of F11 presses could not. THE PROBE OWNS THE ORDERING: one shot, asked for before the byte at 0x00471F70 changes, exactly one and not one per tick, plus the zero-frames line on release. Three mutants, three killed -- capturing after the freeze, capturing every tick, and dropping the measurement. Also corrected: the read-back numbers being byte-identical across runs at two different viewport sizes and two different box positions was never evidence about the screen. They are counts of ink in OUR OWN rows, so identical text gives identical counts wherever the box lands. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.66.0

v0.66.0 (#111 THE OVERLAY DRAWS INTO BOTH TARGETS / #112 THE PROPAGATOR HUNT, REWRITTEN). Two pieces of work, both from Aaron on 2026-08-24. PART ONE: WHERE THE OVERLAY HAS BEEN GOING. FFNx's own log names the renderer -- "Backend: OpenGL" on opengl32.dll -- and FFNx drives it through bgfx, which is a modern renderer wearing an old API's clothes. bgfx leaves two pieces of state behind that will silently swallow anything a legacy overlay draws, and either one explains the contradiction the last three builds could not. FIRST, A FRAMEBUFFER OBJECT MAY BE BOUND. Everything we draw then lands in bgfx's offscreen target instead of the window -- and, damningly, a glReadPixels taken straight afterwards READS THAT SAME TARGET and finds our pixels exactly where we put them. That is precisely what the read-back has been reporting: ten lines of ink, into a buffer that may never have been the one on screen. SECOND, A SHADER PROGRAM MAY BE BOUND. With a program current the fragments glDrawPixels and glBegin produce go through bgfx's fragment shader, which samples ITS textures and knows nothing about our colours; the draw "succeeds", glGetError stays clean, and nothing recognisable appears. So Draw() now unbinds the program, the vertex array and the texture unit, logs what all of them were (a non-zero in that line is the answer, in one line, after three builds of not having it), and DRAWS INTO BOTH CANDIDATE TARGETS: bgfx's, exactly as before, and then the window's own framebuffer. We cannot know from inside this hook which of the two is the frame that reaches the screen -- both stories fit every observation to date -- and picking one and being wrong costs another BAT. Drawing the same pixels at the same coordinates into both costs one extra blit of a 372x240 image per frame and cannot be wrong. AND THE BOX IS NOW A TEXTURED QUAD AS WELL. glDrawPixels needs a valid raster position, obeys glPixelZoom, and is the first call a translation layer implements badly; a textured quad is how every overlay that has to survive an unknown renderer draws itself. Both paths run, identical pixels in identical places, so whichever the renderer honours the box appears exactly once. Plus v0.65.6's two beacons -- a magenta quad through glBegin, a cyan block through glDrawPixels, both in the empty corner -- and ProbeCapture, which measures the F11 buffer from inside DoGLCapture on the exact bytes about to become the PNG. Between them the next shot says which of the four remaining possibilities is true, and three of the four are already fixed by this build. PART TWO: THE RAGNAROK PROPAGATOR HUNT. Aaron played v0.55.0 and asked for something quite different: "We don't want to simply announce when entering the field. We also don't want to proactively inform the player where to find it's pair. Instead we want the NPC in the catalog to say Red Propagator, Purple Propagator, etc. We also need to prevent the Propagator from moving when the player and the Propagator are on the same field, otherwise the player is going to get caught while using navigation tools in the mod." All three, and they pull the same way: the mod should make the hunt POSSIBLE to a blind player, not perform it for him. ARRIVAL IS SILENT. v0.55.0 announced the colour, the rule and the pair's room on every entry. Nothing is spoken on arrival now. THE COLOUR COMES THROUGH THE CATALOG, as "Red Propagator", "Purple Propagator", "Green Propagator", "Yellow Propagator" -- the same route by which every other thing in a room reaches him. One source of truth: the colours live in PG_LIST, which is also what the pair logic reasons about, so the name spoken and the name reasoned about cannot drift apart. rgroad3's NINTH ALIEN is dropped from the catalog: it carries a second alien01 whose whole default method is three words long and which can never be fought, and listing it would send him across the ship to a Propagator that is not there. THE PAIR'S LOCATION IS ANSWERED, NEVER VOLUNTEERED. What a kill MEANS is still spoken, because the consequence is otherwise invisible until you walk back into a room and find the thing standing there again -- but it says the rule ("the next kill must be the other green one") and stops. Where that one is comes only from the help key. AND THEY ARE HELD STILL, by the engine's own per-entity move speed. The field update pass at 0x004790E7 walks an entity by unit(facing) * [ent+0x1FE] >> 8; write 0 into that word and the step is zero. The arrival test at 0x004799FF compares the remaining distance against speed squared, so the move never completes, the script blocks on its move opcode at 0x0052359F, and it therefore never reaches the contact test or the BATTLE after it. Nothing is lied to: +0x23C stays 1, the walkmesh triangle stays valid, facing and animation keep updating, and restoring the word resumes the move exactly where it stopped. Both +0x1FE and +0x200 are written every tick, because the pin is a race with the script and the loser of that race is the player. IT IS A BUBBLE, NOT A FREEZE. In four of these five rooms the monster's own charge is the ONLY thing that ever starts a battle, so a Propagator held still forever is one that can never be fought -- and all eight have to die for the lift to open. So it is held while he is far enough away that any movement would be an ambush, and released once he has deliberately walked into arm's reach: 600 units to let go, 900 to take hold again, because a monster flickering on the boundary would be worse than either. THREE ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. rgair1 and rgroad1 contain no move opcode of any kind -- they stand where SET3 put them and battle on contact -- so there is nothing to hold, and a write with no purpose in a scene nobody has run the mod in is exactly what the space rescue spent four builds paying for. rgguest2 is not a patrol, it is a cutscene that ends in the MAPJUMP3 out of the room; freezing it would block the script before its own exit and strand him there. AND THE HOLD KNOWS WHEN TO FORGET RATHER THAN RESTORE. The live entity array is rebuilt on every field load, so slot 2 in the next room is somebody else entirely: a "restore" fired after a transition does not give a Propagator its speed back, it hands a stranger a number. pCurrentFieldName, which this module keys on, lags the transition by seconds; pCurrentFieldId does not. So the id observed when the name last changed is remembered, and the moment the live id walks away from it everything is dropped and nothing at all is written until the name catches up. chase_kani_freeze needed that same defence and learned it by crashing. WHAT IS STILL NEVER WRITTEN: var[446], var[447], var[445] bit 2, var[437]. Those are the puzzle's answer, not its controls. THE PROBES. tests/disc3_wiring_compile.cpp now runs the hold against a real 32-entity Others array at the real stride, with the script fighting back the way dic does; tests/disc3_models_compile.cpp checks the bubble, the hysteresis, the colour of all eight and that a pair announces the same colour in both rooms; tests/catalog_harness.cpp gains three fixtures and the golden grows to 53. Twelve mutants, twelve killed -- including re-announcing on arrival, leaking the pair's room into the unprompted line, pinning once instead of every tick, freezing the cutscene one, holding an entity whose distance we cannot measure, and restoring a speed across a field transition. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.65.6

v0.65.6 (#111 TWO READS, ONE BUFFER, TWO ANSWERS). The 00:56 BAT is the first F11 shot ever taken with the overlay drawn BEFORE the capture, and it settles nothing except that my model is wrong. EVERYTHING ELSE IN THAT RUN IS CLEAN. The deferred timer announcement works exactly as designed: hold requested at 00:56:14 with no clock yet, detected at 00:56:15 and applied at raw=88, "initial announcement DEFERRED", silence for the whole seventeen seconds of the screen, and at 00:56:31 "HOLD off (Enter): resumed at raw=88" followed by "Timer detected. 1 minutes 28 seconds remaining." with no interrupt. The freeze engaged in state 4 and released one byte for one byte after 17516 ms. He won on the first attempt again -- centred at 00:57:16, held to the verdict. THE OVERLAY IS STILL NOT IN THE PICTURE, and now that is a real contradiction rather than an ordering mistake. Draw() runs first in the hook now; its own glReadPixels, taken immediately after the blit, reports the same ten lines it always has (97,157,136,141,128,68,137,102,124,137 against ink 1202..1584). DoGLCapture reads the same buffer a few instructions later in the same hook invocation and the saved frame contains NOT ONE PIXEL of the overlay: I searched the whole 1280x800 image for the box background (12,16,32) and for its border (200,210,235) and both counts are zero. Two glReadPixels calls cannot disagree about one buffer, so one of them is not reading what it thinks it is. AND THE BOX IN THE SHOT IS THE GAME'S, CONFIRMED TWICE OVER. f11_005625 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to f11_224537 from the v0.65.1 run two hours and one process restart earlier -- same MD5 -- which is what a deterministic frozen scene looks like: the same held clock reading 1:28, the same black field, and the game's dialog typewriter stalled at the same character. The 00:05 shot differs only in having got two characters further before the freeze caught it. SO THIS BUILD STOPS GUESSING AND SPLITS THE QUESTION. Two beacons, drawn only while the overlay is up, in the corner where nothing else is: A is a solid magenta quad through glBegin/glEnd -- fixed-function GEOMETRY -- and B is a solid cyan block through glDrawPixels with forty-eight rows of one constant colour, so nothing about strides, formats or alignment can be blamed. The overlay is B with complicated data. And FieldOverlay::ProbeCapture() now measures the capture buffer itself, from inside DoGLCapture, on the exact bytes that are about to become the PNG -- per-line ink at the box's own coordinates plus the colour at each beacon's centre -- so the measurement and the file cannot drift apart the way the read-back and the file have. One BAT now separates four cases that three builds have been unable to tell apart: B present and the box absent means our buffer is wrong; A present and B absent means glDrawPixels is the wrong call against this renderer and the box becomes a textured quad; neither present but ink in the probe means the capture-to-file path is at fault; neither present and no ink means nothing this hook draws is ever presented, and the whole approach needs replacing -- which after three builds of assuming otherwise is worth an hour to find out. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.65.5

v0.65.5 (#111 THE SCREENSHOT WAS NEVER LOOKING AT THE OVERLAY). Aaron asked whether I had actually checked the latest F11 shot before calling the overlay done. I had not -- I had taken the read-back numbers and inferred the rest -- and the shot does not say what v0.65.4 said it did. WHAT THE SHOT ACTUALLY SHOWS. f11_000518 (1280x800): a black screen, the FF8 timer HUD reading "1:2..." in the game's own bold numerals, and one large bordered box from x255 to x968 and y52 to y656 containing "REACHING RINOA" and, on the line below, the single letter "N". Nothing else. THAT BOX IS NOT MINE. The mod's overlay is 372x240 at (454,280); this one is 713x604, which is not that at any zoom. And the 22:45 shot from v0.65.1 has the SAME box at the SAME pixels reading "REACHING RIN" -- three characters shorter. A box that gains characters between two runs is a TYPEWRITER, and the mod's box is rasterised whole by GDI in one call and cannot be caught half-written. It is the GAME's dialog window, the one GardenBattle::OpenBriefDialog opens with the same text, revealing itself a character at a time and stalling where the field freeze catches it. So the "only the first line renders" that v0.65.1 diagnosed, and that v0.65.2 and v0.65.3 then chased through GdiFlush, DC teardown and the RGBA stride, was never a description of the overlay. Two of those three fixes were real bugs found on the way -- the DIB really was being read while selected into a DC, and FFNx really does read RGBA regardless of what you declare -- but the symptom that motivated them belonged to a different box. WHY THE OVERLAY IS IN NO SCREENSHOT AT ALL, and it is a one-line ordering bug of mine. DoGLCapture() reads the back buffer at the TOP of HookedSwapBuffers; FieldOverlay::Draw() wrote into it at the BOTTOM. A capture on frame N therefore sampled the buffer before that frame's overlay went in, every time, no matter how well the blit worked. The overlay has never had a chance to appear in an F11 shot since the day it was written. THE FIX IS THE ORDER. Draw() now runs first in the hook. "Last" was the wrong instinct anyway: the game finishes rendering before it calls SwapBuffers, so nothing between the top of this hook and the swap draws game content, and the top is exactly as late as the bottom -- it is just the half F11 can see. The battle paths that read pixels below it read them only in battle, where the overlay never is. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE. The glReadPixels read-back in Draw() reads the real frame buffer immediately after the blit, and it reported ten lines whose light-pixel counts track the rasteriser's ink line for line at a steady ~12:1 -- 841/68 for the short "Boost: hold W." among them. That is still the strongest evidence there is that the box reaches the screen, and it is unaffected by which end of the hook the draw happens at. But it is one instrument reporting on itself, which is precisely the position I was in when I told Aaron the overlay was confirmed. The next F11 shot is the independent check, and now it can be one. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.65.4

v0.65.4 (#112 THE TIMER TALKED OVER THE BRIEF). Aaron: "Also noticed a bug that the game timer interrupts the announcement of the game controls when the controls initially appear." It does, and the log has it to the second. From the 2026-08-24 00:05 BAT: "Outer Space 5" at 00:05:11, the space rescue asks for the hold at 00:05:12 ("no timer yet -- it will be applied when one is detected"), the engine writes 90, 89, 88, detection fires, "HOLD applied at detection: raw=88" -- and on the very next line "Timer detected. 1 minutes 28 seconds remaining." with (interrupt). That interrupt lands two sentences into a nine-sentence brief that is the only thing standing between a blind player and a scene he cannot see. IT WAS ALSO UNTRUE THE MOMENT IT WAS SPOKEN. The hold is applied on the line above it. The clock that announcement describes is already standing still, so it was announcing a countdown that was not counting, over the top of the module that had just stopped it. THE FIX IS TO DEFER IT, NOT TO DROP IT. Aaron asked for the clock to stop, not to be kept secret, and how long he has is exactly the sort of thing a player needs before he starts flying.
