A timer detected while a hold is in force records a debt instead of speaking; SetHold(false) pays it, QUEUED rather than interrupting, reading what is actually left rather than what the engine first wrote -- and the release is the first moment that number means anything, because it is the moment the clock starts moving. EnterInactive cancels the debt: a timer that ended behind the screen owes nobody an announcement, and the dead-clock warning the space module already speaks at Enter covers that case properly. THE PROBE NOW OWNS BOTH HALVES. tests/countdown_hold_test.cpp drives the real countdown_timer.cpp against the game's own mmap'd globals, and its detection-under-hold section now asserts silence at detection and the deferred line at release, including WHICH kind of speak it is -- the shim records the interrupt flag now, because "it spoke" and "it interrupted" are different bugs and this one was the second. Three mutants, three killed: speaking at detection anyway, dropping the deferred line, and making the deferred line an interrupt. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. AND THE OVERLAY IS DONE. The same BAT closes out v0.65.3's open question with two lists of ten numbers: ink per line 1202,1823,1762,1690,1706,841,1564,1330,1420,1584 and read back from the frame buffer 97,157,136,141,128,68,137,102,124,137 -- ten lines rasterised, ten lines measured coming back OFF the screen, a consistent ~12:1 ratio line for line, including the short "Boost: hold W." at position six (841 and 68). The box is on the screen in full. Three builds of guessing about one glDrawPixels ended the moment the mod was made to check its own blit.

## v0.65.3

v0.65.3 (#111 FOUR BYTES A PIXEL). The 2026-08-23 23:39 BAT settles where the overlay text was going, and it was not where I guessed twice. THE BITMAP IS PERFECT. v0.65.2's new diagnostic: "[OVERLAY] ink per line: 1202,1823,1762,1690,1706,841,1564,1330,1420,1584" -- ten lines, ten non-zero counts, and the short one (841) is "Boost: hold W." exactly as it should be. So deselecting the DIB from the DC before reading its bits DID fix the rasteriser, and the fault is entirely in the blit. THE GIVE-AWAY IS THE GEOMETRY. A box declared 372 wide came out about 279 on screen, and 279 is 372 * 3/4. The layer under this glDrawPixels consumed our 372x3 bytes as 279 FOUR-BYTE pixels: it ignores GL_RGB and it ignores UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, and reads RGBA regardless. Row 0 is therefore nearly right and every row after it drifts by a quarter of a row -- which is exactly the banding in his screenshot, and exactly why the top line survived and the other nine dissolved. So give it what it is going to read anyway: the buffer is 32-bit RGBA now, rows 4-aligned by construction, GL_RGBA is core GL 1.1 and needs no extension, and since the DIB was already 32-bit the copy now only swaps R and B rather than repacking. There is no longer a stride for anything to disagree about. AND THE MOD NOW CHECKS ITS OWN BLIT. Three builds have gone on inference about this one call and each costs Aaron a rebuild and an eight-minute scene, so Draw() now reads the frame buffer back -- one row per text line, straight after the draw, with the same glReadPixels that battle_tts_screenshot.inl already uses from this same hook -- and logs the same light-pixel measure the rasteriser reports. Two lists of ten numbers: agreeing means the box is on the screen and anything left is the screenshot path; disagreeing says exactly where the transfer goes wrong and by how much. Once per Show(), no allocation on the render thread, one static row buffer. EVERYTHING ELSE IN THAT RUN WAS CLEAN: he won again on the first attempt (centred by 23:41:20, held to the verdict, "Rinoa: Squall...thank you." at 23:42:34), the clock held through the freeze, and the escape pod's handle stayed out of the catalog. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.65.2

v0.65.2 (#111 WHERE THE TEXT IS BEING LOST). The 2026-08-23 22:45 BAT is clean on everything the last release set out to fix. THE CLOCK HELD: raw goes 90, 89, 88 and then STOPS for the whole thirty-two seconds the screen is up -- the next decrement is at 22:45:57, the exact second Enter released it -- and Aaron pressed T three times while it was frozen and heard the same 88 each time (state=2, FROZEN). THE FREEZE ENGAGED in field_main state 4 and released on Enter, one byte out and the same byte back. HE WON ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT: centred at 22:47:06, held to the verdict at 22:47:24, "Rinoa: Squall...thank you." at 22:47:47. No retry. And the escape pod's handle is gone from the catalog -- "[catalog] ent4 sym='handle' dropped: field-scoped exclusion for 'sspod2'" -- with Piet, Quistis and Ellone untouched. WHAT IS STILL WRONG IS THE OVERLAY, and only the overlay. It reaches the screen: 372x240 at (454,280), zoom 1, 1280x800 viewport, glGetError=0x0000, bordered and positioned. But of its ten lines only the first renders, truncated, on a background that was never painted. v0.65.1's GdiFlush() did not fix it, so the diagnosis was wrong. THE STRONGER RULE: while a DIB section is SELECTED INTO A DC, reading its bits by pointer is not defined, and flushing is not the documented remedy -- deselecting is. The DC is now torn down completely (bitmap deselected, font deselected, DeleteDC) before a single byte is read; the DIB section's memory stays valid until DeleteObject, which is why that one call now comes after the copy. AND A DIAGNOSTIC, BECAUSE TWO BATs HAVE NOW GONE ON A GUESS. Each guess costs Aaron a build and an eight-minute scene. Show() now counts the light pixels in each text row of the bitmap it just built and logs one number per line: "[OVERLAY] ink per line: ...". Ten non-zero numbers mean the rasteriser is right and the fault is in the GL blit; one non-zero number means the rasteriser is still dropping nine lines and GL is innocent. Either way the next log settles it without another guess. NOT EXERCISED THIS RUN: the sspod2 "Capsule" rename. The pod line stayed inert both times he passed through -- "line0 'pod' inert: gated on var[256]=2554 op6 2556", then 2560 -- so it never entered the catalog and the rename never had a chance to fire. It is covered by tests/catalog_harness.cpp's field_scoped_pod fixture and still unconfirmed in the field. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.65.1

v0.65.1 (#111 THE CLOCK WAS NEVER FROZEN). Aaron: "This one was broken. The game timer was running on the controls screen and it was not possible to catch Rinoa on the first attempt." Both halves are one bug, and it is mine from v0.64.0. THE FREEZE DOES NOT STOP THE COUNTDOWN. v0.64.0 dropped CountdownTimer::SetHold from the freeze path on the reasoning that stopping field_main stops the countdown global with everything else. It does not. The 2026-08-23 22:05 log: [FIELDPAUSE] ENGAGED at 22:05:07, and 0x01CFE92C goes 90, 89, 88, 87 -- one a second, straight through it -- reaching ZERO at 22:06:35 with the Game Controls screen still up. Whatever decrements that global is not field_main. v0.64.0 only looked right because its arrival gate opened the screen BEFORE rinoa::default reached SETTIMER, so there was no running clock to expose it; v0.64.1 moved the freeze to after the scene arms itself and the truth came out on the next BAT. AND THAT IS WHY HE COULD NOT CATCH HER. The clock hit zero behind the box, so the instant Enter let the scripts run again timer0::start0 set var[1037] = 1, director1's control loop exited, and no key moved Rinoa ever again: x sat at 2500 y=-800 for FOUR MINUTES of "still well right and down", trend 0 every single call. The scene was over before he started it. THE FIX is the one line v0.64.0 deleted: the clock is held whenever the screen is up, freeze or no freeze. Two mechanisms for one job is the right number when one of them provably does not cover the other. AND ENTER NOW CHECKS. One check at one moment, with no false-positive window: if the countdown is already gone when the screen closes, the mod says "the mission clock has already run out -- if nothing responds, press F9 or take the retry" instead of reading bearings into a scene that has ended. It should never fire now; "should" is exactly what v0.64.0 said about the countdown. THE OVERLAY DREW -- and his F11 screenshot shows both halves of that. It is on screen, bordered and positioned (372x240 at (134,120), zoom 1, 640x480 viewport, glGetError=0x0000, and field_main confirmed in state 4), which settles that the SwapBuffers hook reaches the screen through the freeze. But only the FIRST of its ten lines had rendered and the background was garbage, because GDI BATCHES: the drawing calls were queued, not executed, and reading a DIB section by pointer does not force them out. GdiFlush() before the read is the whole fix, and it is the one line that makes a DIB section safe to read that way. Four mutants, four killed -- including v0.64.0's own mistake, put back deliberately to confirm the probe now catches it. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.65.0

v0.65.0 (#111 THE BOX IS OURS NOW, and #123 two things in the escape pod). Aaron, after the field freeze worked: "Now that is working is there anything we can do to get the Game Controls visible on the screen? Can we independently fire the dialog renderer or something like that while freezing the scene?" NOT THE GAME'S RENDERER, NO. field_main's steady state (0x0047246E) is one instruction -- `call 0x004767B0` -- and that single function is the whole per-frame field: scripts, movement and window drawing together, with no draw-only entry to call. The two calls bracketing it (0x004A2940, 0x0049E8E0) are a different subsystem, and 0x004A0880, which the retired Garden-battle note named, is the window system's INIT and runs at field load. Freezing the field takes the box with it, and his F11 screenshot is what that looks like: a black frame with nothing on it but the mission timer HUD, which survives because it is drawn after field_main in field_main_loop. BUT THE MOD ALREADY HAS A FOOT IN THE RENDER PATH THE FREEZE DOES NOT TOUCH. battle_tts_screenshot.inl hooks SwapBuffers and calls glReadPixels there -- which is how that screenshot got taken DURING the freeze, on the game's own render thread with a live OpenGL context. So the box is ours: src/field_overlay.* rasterises the text with GDI on the mod thread and blits it with glDrawPixels from that hook, and it appears regardless of what field_main is or is not doing. That is better than restoring the game's box -- it is not bound to the 320x224 window or the 34-column wrap, and every Game Controls screen in the mod can use it. THE SPLIT IS THE SAFETY. Show() runs on the mod thread and does all the allocation, all the GDI and all the logging; Draw() runs on the render thread and does nothing but blit a buffer that was published complete. The buffer is never freed while shown. Draw() logs ONCE per Show(), with glGetError, because if this renderer turns out to be a core profile the fixed-function path is a silent no-op and that line is the only thing that will say so. AND THE ARITHMETIC IS TESTED, because "the box runs off the bottom of the screen" is a bug this project already shipped once (v0.20.125) and it was arithmetic then too. Measure/ZoomFor/PlaceFor live in field_overlay_pure.inl with no Windows and no GL in them, and tests/field_overlay_test.cpp compiles THOSE DEFINITIONS rather than a copy: ten lines by 32 columns fits, over-wide and over-tall text reports clamped rather than overflowing, the zoom is integer and shrinks until the box fits, and an oversized box starts at the origin because a negative glRasterPos2i is dropped by GL and reads exactly like "the overlay does not work". THE HOST CAN NOW PARSE IT: tests/winshim gained gl/GL.h and the GDI surface, and run_gates.sh syntax-checks field_overlay.cpp alongside field_archive.cpp -- two releases have reached Aaron's compiler green because a file the host could not parse is a file the host cannot check, and this is the newest such file. THE ESCAPE POD. "There is an empty capsule Squall has to enter and it is being identified as an exit to Desert. It should just read out as Capsule. There is another item in the catalog for handle that is only interacted with by the scene automatically so it can be excluded as well." Both are true and neither can be fixed on the SYM alone: `handle` is ALSO the Missile Base valve wheel the player really does turn (bgmd1_4, gfcar1), and dropping it globally would take that with it. So FIELD_SCOPED_ENTITIES is keyed on FIELD AND SYM -- a null display drops the thing, a non-null one names it and, on an exit-bearing line, replaces the "Exit to <destination>" the destination would otherwise earn. sspod2's `pod` is line 0, a SCREEN_BOUND the scanner resolves to field 638; the destination is not wrong, it is just not what he is walking towards, so it stays an exit and only the words change. sspod2/sspod3's `handle` has no TALKRADIUS, no dialogue and no MAPJUMP -- its talk and push methods are animation opcodes only, and the 20:23:41 scan agrees (talk=0 push=0 jsmTalk=0 rtRad=0 talkable=0). Two new catalog fixtures, and the second one is the Missile Base case proving the wheel survives. Nine mutants, nine killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.64.1

v0.64.1 (#111 TWO THINGS THE SCREENSHOT SHOWED). The freeze worked and Aaron won the space rescue on his FIRST attempt -- 20:37:05 Enter, centred at 20:38:03, held to the end. [FIELDPAUSE] ENGAGED at 20:36:21 and released (Enter) after 43687 ms, one byte out and the same byte back. He also took F11 screenshots while the Game Controls were up, and they settle the question the last release could not: THE FIELD GOES BLACK. 99.6% of the frame is pure black and the only thing drawn is the mission timer HUD, reading 1:29 -- which is the other half of the answer, because that is 89 of 90 seconds SEVENTEEN SECONDS after the field loaded. The clock is genuinely stopped, and the HUD survives because it is drawn outside field_main. He had already said "if we lose the drawn box so be it", and this is what that looks like: a black screen with a frozen timer on it. Two real bugs in the same log. THE BRIEF OPENED BEFORE THE SCENE EXISTED. "game controls open at x=0 y=0" on the SAME SECOND as "entered ssspace3". v0.64.0 gated arrival on the clamp alone, and zero is inside a clamp -- but the field-variable block is ZEROED ON FIELD LOAD, so the first readable frame passed. The consequences were all benign this time and none of them were meant to be: field_main was frozen for forty-four seconds while it was still LOADING the field, her position was pinned at a zero that was never a position, and Enter produced a spurious "centred" before the scene had picked anywhere to start. The scene's own init is the gate now. rinoa::default 16-17 writes var[1052] = 8000, and 20-126 picks one of eight starting offsets -- (-1800,-2000), (3000,3700), (3000,-350), (-2700,200), (900,-43), (-3300,1500), (2500,-800), (1100,2000) -- not one of which is (0,0). Both together, or the module says nothing and freezes nothing. AND THE REPEAT CONTRADICTED THE BRIEF. At 20:36:42 he pressed slash and heard "the mission clock is held while this screen is up, but the scene itself is not" -- the FALLBACK wording, thirty seconds after being told nothing moves at all. FieldPause::Available() looks for the UNPATCHED signature, so between Engage and Release it failed on its own 0xC3 and every wording chosen from it flipped. It now reports true while engaged, which is also the honest answer to the question it is asked. ALSO: Engage logs field_main's state machine byte (0x01CE4A64) so the next run says which state the freeze actually lands in -- logged and not gated, because a gate on a number nobody has measured is a gate that can refuse for ever, and the arrival gate above is what keeps the freeze out of the load path. The probes map a real page at that address, because the winshim's __except is a C++ catch and catch(...) does not catch a bad address -- the first version of this segfaulted the host rather than returning -1. NOT FIXED, NOTED: [F11-SCREENSHOT] logs "captured" at REQUEST time, before the async SwapBuffers capture completes, and the 20:36:31 shot never reached disk while the 20:36:38 one did. The log claims a file that is not there. Different module, no bearing on this scene, and it is the kind of thing that should be fixed on purpose rather than in passing. Three mutants, three killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.64.0

v0.64.0 (#111 THE FIELD STOPS). Aaron: "Is there no way we can suppress the actual scene behind the Game Controls screen, that way when the player presses enter that is when Rinoa begins to move?" There is, and v0.63.x's answer -- stop the mission clock and warn that the scene runs on anyway -- was the honest version of the wrong thing. THE ENGINE HAS EXACTLY ONE PAUSE POINT. field_main_loop (0x0046FEE0) calls field_main (0x00471F70) only when [0x01CE4A68] and [0x01CD2EBC] are both zero; everything after that call -- the frame present at 0x4700E0..0x47017A, the sound, the input, the frame counter -- runs regardless, so "field_main is not called" is a state the engine is DESIGNED to sit in: it is what its own pause menu does. And the call passes no arguments, which makes one 0xC3 at the entry a complete and stack-safe field freeze. field_main is the whole field, so with it stopped rinoa::default cannot reach the verdict at index 160, the approach cannot advance (it is a 2700-frame move -- opcode 0xF3 at 147 waited on by 0xF5 at 159, and 2700 frames at 30fps IS the ninety seconds), the countdown global is not decremented, and Rinoa does not move. Enter is the moment the scene starts. WHAT IT COSTS. The Garden battle did exactly this until v0.20.123 and its note says plainly that it worked; it was retired because window rendering hangs off the same function (field_main -> 0x00471010 -> 0x0052BC00 -> 0x004A0880), so a frozen field cannot redraw the Game Controls box. Aaron, asked directly: "If we lose the drawn box so be it." The box was always a courtesy to a sighted onlooker; the spoken brief comes off the mod's own thread, which the freeze does not touch. So the module opens the box, lets SP_DRAW_MS (200 ms, six frames) go by so it is drawn at least once, and only then freezes -- a fifth of a second of scene against the forty-six seconds his 19:37 run spent. AND THE WAIT IS GONE WITH IT. Squall's three lines were only ever a problem because they landed on top of a brief the scene ran through; a frame that never happens cannot open a dialogue, so the freeze path briefs immediately and the dialogue-quiet machinery, its settle and its two caps are kept only as the FALLBACK. Which path runs is decided by FieldPause::Available() BEFORE the screen opens, so a build whose field_main does not read A1 64 4A CE 01 gets v0.63.3's behaviour rather than none, and the screen and the brief say which pause they actually got -- "Nothing moves until you press Enter" when it is true, and v0.63.3's "she drifts on" when it is not. NEW: src/field_pause.inl, and it is written like what it is -- the most dangerous byte in the mod, because a restore that does not happen leaves the field frozen with no way out but closing the game. Five rules: never patch what we did not recognise (the five entry bytes must read A1 64 4A CE 01); never patch blind (the address comes from FF8Addresses' own main_loop -> field_main_loop+0x148 chain, now kept as field_main_fn rather than logged and dropped); restore from every exit (Enter, F9, the backstop, leaving the field, FieldNavigation::Shutdown, all through one idempotent Release); a watchdog that does not need the caller (FieldPause::Watchdog runs from PollBattlePauseResume, above every on-field early return and even in battle, and force-releases past a ten-minute ceiling); and restore the ORIGINAL byte, read before the patch. TESTS: tests/field_pause_test.cpp maps a real RWX page at the game's own 0x00471000 with field_main's real opening bytes in it and asserts each of those five rules against actual writes it reads back -- including one wrong byte at each of the five signature positions, a VirtualProtect that refuses, and both idempotence directions. disc3_wiring_compile drives the space rescue through BOTH strategies, choosing between them the way the module does, and checks that the byte goes back on Enter, on F9, on leaving the field and on the watchdog. Eleven mutants, eleven killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.63.3.1

v0.63.3.1 (#111 BUILD FIX). v0.63.3 did not compile: "field_disc3_space.inl(346): error C2513: 'const int': no variable declared before '='". The boost nudge named its local `far`. windows.h still defines far, near, pascal and huge as EMPTY macros -- the segmented-memory keywords of 16-bit Windows, kept for source compatibility thirty years after the memory model that needed them -- so `const int far = ...` reaches MSVC as `const int = ...`. Renamed to wideErr. THE REAL FAILURE IS THAT EVERY GATE WAS GREEN, and this is the second time a v0.6x release has reached Aaron's compiler because a probe compiled a different program from the mod; v0.62.3's JsmGateSatisfied is why tests/lint_harness_includes.py exists. The host probes hand-roll their Win32 surface, so they never had the macro that erases the identifier. Two guards now, because they fail in different places. (1) tests/winshim/windows.h and tests/disc3_wiring_compile.cpp define far/near/pascal/huge, placed after every standard header so they poison the mod's identifiers and not libstdc++'s -- the probe now reports "expected unqualified-id before '=' token" on the exact line MSVC did. (2) tests/lint_msvc_macros.py scans src/ for any identifier named after one of them, translation-unit independent, so a file no probe compiles is covered too. It strips comments and string literals first, so prose may say "a long way out" and the Game Controls screen may read "Boost if she is far out" without tripping it. WINAPI, CALLBACK and CDECL are deliberately NOT on the list: those expand to calling conventions and `static DWORD WINAPI AccessibilityThread(LPVOID)` is correct code. The list is the macros that expand to NOTHING, because that is the set whose misuse compiles here and vanishes there. Both guards were verified against the real line before being trusted. No behaviour change: v0.63.3's four log fixes are unaltered. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.63.3

v0.63.3 (#111 WHAT THE LOG SAID). Aaron won the space rescue on v0.63.2 -- second attempt, unboosted, sixty seconds to spare -- and asked for a log review before locking it in. Four things in it, three of them mine. THE FALSE EMPTY. 18:34:47, in the middle of the "Try again" prompt: "Boost fuel gauge empty." The retry is MAPJUMPO 878, which is ssspace3 again, so Here() never goes false and nothing in the module resets. The scene tears down with var[1052] reading 0 for a frame, and the tracker took that for a tank running dry. Worse, it then latched: attempt 2 refilled to 8000 and the tracker was still sitting at empty, so the whole ninety seconds could not have announced anything. The gauge only ever falls inside an attempt, so a rise is the retry -- followed silently now, which re-arms it -- and a fall of more than one band between two ticks is a scene resetting rather than a drain, because the bands are 25 points apart and the gauge drops at most 8 of 8000 per script frame. THE PAUSE IS HALF A PAUSE, AND THE SCREEN SAID OTHERWISE. It claimed "Everything is paused until you press Enter -- the clock too." The clock, yes: the log has raw oscillating 88/87 for sixty-three seconds, the engine decrementing and the mod writing it straight back. The SCENE, no. Attempt 1 was judged with FORTY-SEVEN seconds still showing -- KILLTIMER at 18:34:33 against a 60-second boundary announced at 18:34:20 -- because the approach the verdict hangs on is not the countdown, and it cannot be stopped: the Game Controls box has to be DRAWN, window rendering hangs off field_main, and that is exactly why the Garden battle's RET-over-field_main pause was retired in v0.20.123. So the screen now says the clock is held and the scene is not, and Enter says what the pause actually cost: "The scene ran on for those 63 seconds, so the end comes sooner than the clock says." AND A NUDGE TOWARD THE BOOST. Attempt 1 was lost 280 units out and STILL CLOSING, from a start of x=2500 -- 52 seconds of unboosted travel at the measured 48 a second, against a scene the briefing had already eaten into. Thirteen seconds of boost covers it. The brief has said the boost exists since v0.63.2; a line said WHEN the error is wide is the one that gets used, so the first wide bearing of each attempt names the key, once, queued behind the bearing. FIFTY TIMES "CENTRED". Attempt 2 centred at 18:35:14 and sat at x=16 y=-31 until the verdict at 18:36:17: sixty-three seconds at the 1.2-second near cadence. That cadence is for a gap that is CLOSING; parked on the target there is nothing to resolve. It now speaks every three seconds while nothing moves, and says "still centred" after the first -- the idiom the steering calls already use -- and one unit of movement puts the fast rhythm straight back. Still speaking, because silence in a scene with no other feedback reads as a mod that died. AND THE FROZEN CLOCK STOPS NARRATING ITSELF. A freeze is the engine decrementing and CountdownTimer writing the value back, so the global really does oscillate, and v0.63.2 logged every edge: a hundred and thirty "live raw=" lines saying nothing but "the freeze is working". Suppressed while FROZEN; the transitions were always logged. CLEAN OTHERWISE: the catalog was silent on ssspace3 for both attempts, the brief waited out Squall and opened at 18:32:55 with the clock already stopped, slash repeated it twice, Enter closed it, the boost key resolved to W through the learner, and no new errors or warnings appear anywhere in the run. Ten mutants, ten killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.63.2

v0.63.2 (#111 THE BOOST, AND WHOSE VOICE THE SCREEN SPEAKS IN). Three corrections from Aaron after the flight that worked. THIRD PERSON. "The text of the game controls were in first person, using 'when I', instead let's use third-person like 'when the mod' so it matches the other game controls screens." Done, and the probe now asserts the brief contains no "I" at all -- the dragon fight has said "Hold %s to block, tap %s to attack" since v0.20.x and the space screen was the odd one out. THE BOOST, CONFIRMED IN THE EXE AS ASKED. "I am fairly sure this is toggled by holding down X, but please confirm in the game exe." It is mask 0x0010 and on his keyboard that is not X. The Garden battle's key learner measured all four of its masks across two runs on his own machine -- 16 with W, 32 with D, 64 with X, 128 with A, on 0x01CE48B0, the same field button word this scene reads -- so X is 0x0040 and the boost is W. The screen names it through that learner rather than hardcoding it, and LearnButtons now runs during the space scene too, so a remap is picked up and the arrow keys (which are not in its candidate list) cannot teach it a wrong name. AND IT IS FOUR TIMES THE SPEED, NOT TWICE. The multiplier is applied in TWO places, both gated on the same mask: director1::default 13-23 puts 8 in var[1034] instead of 4, and then rinoa::keyl 5-25 multiplies var[1034] by 2 again before adding it. Sixteen a frame against four. Every one of the eight handlers carries the same pair, diagonals included, and each plays a different thruster SFX for the two cases (341632 boosted, 42704 not), which is how a hearing player already knows. tests/disc3_models_compile.cpp asserts all of it against three windows of the real ssspace3 bytecode, because reading either place alone reports half the truth. The offline sim now flies the matrix boosted: 9/9, far corners included -- 8100 units at 16 a frame is about 42 seconds of a 90-second clock, where at 4 it is 169 and the scene is over first. HOLD THE ARROW, DO NOT TAP IT. "We should inform the player they need to hold down the arrow keys in the direction they want to go." BTN_HELD (0x6D) is a level test and director1 re-dispatches the handler on every pass while the mask stays down, so a tap moves her exactly once. The screen says HOLD in capitals and the spoken brief says why. THE FUEL HAS A VOICE. "We need to inform the player when their boost is exhausted. I believe a sighted player can tell by the movement but a blind player will need to be explicitly informed." rinoa::default 16-17 sets var[1052] = 8000 and every pass of director1's loop with a direction held does var[1052] -= var[1034] -- 4 a frame, 8 while boosting -- and writes it to gauge 0 with opcode 315, which is the bar on screen. The mod now speaks the bands on the way DOWN only: half, low, empty. Queued, never interrupting, because a bearing is the thing he acts on. Slash reads "Boost on. Fuel 62 percent." behind the bearing, and the boost half of that comes from var[1034] -- the game's own live step -- rather than from the keyboard, so it is right whatever the key is bound to. WHAT THE EMPTY LINE DOES NOT SAY. Nothing reads var[1052] back. Not one script in ssspace1/2/3, and FF8_EN.exe holds no reference to its address; opcode 315 (0x00529BF0) stores the value and calls 0x004B7C90, which clamps the BAR against the gauge struct at 0x01D2BAB2+id*16 and touches nothing else. So the gauge empties and the boost keeps working, and the announcement is "Boost fuel gauge empty" rather than "boost gone" -- a mutation that changes it to the latter is killed on purpose. The sim says the case is real rather than theoretical: getting to her never costs half the tank (worst 3968 of 8000), but holding the boost for the whole ninety seconds does empty it, because a real player keeps correcting after it arrives. Thirteen mutants, thirteen killed. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.63.1

v0.63.1 (#111 THE PAUSE). Aaron flew the space rescue to the end on v0.63.0 -- "Successfully completed the mini-game using manual navigation" -- and asked for two things on the way out. THE BEEP IS GONE. "Let's get rid of the beep sound effect. It is extremely distracting and the TTS announcement I think is sufficient." The radar went in because words cannot resolve 180 units out of 8100 and I could not then show that they could; he then went and did it, which settles the question the beep was hedging. So all of it goes -- the pulse, and the two-note cue on entering the aim box with it, because the module already says "centred" on exactly that transition and a cue that repeats one sentence while covering the next is a cost with nothing on the other side. SrRadarHz and SrRadarGapMs are deleted; SrRadarT stays, because it was never the beep -- it is the normalised worse-axis error the "still right" trend is built on. The probe keeps its PlaySoundA counter and now asserts it reads ZERO across the entire approach, because a removal nothing checks grows back. THE GAME CONTROLS SCREEN IS NOW A REAL PAUSE. "The Game Controls screen never had time to appear and announce. It was interrupted by Squall's speech at the start, and it didn't freeze the time for the player to read the controls either. The controls should essentially pause everything until the player hits Enter to proceed." Both halves failed for one reason: v0.63.0 treated a ninety-second clock as the thing it had to fit inside. It waited for the scene's dialogue -- but asked "is a dialogue open" on the frame the field loaded, when Squall had not started, so it briefed at 16:10:54 and his first line landed on top of it at 16:10:57; and it took the screen away after fifteen seconds unread, "[SPACE] game controls closed (timed out)" at 16:11:09. So stop the clock instead. CountdownTimer::SetHold pins the engine's own countdown global with the same rewrite-every-frame machinery Shift+T has used since v0.15.13, silently, and it is a REQUEST rather than an order because detection is decrement-gated (#59) and the engine does not classify its own countdown until two seconds in -- "ENTER ACTIVE: rawValue=88" against a 90-second timer. EnterActive applies a pending hold the instant it detects one; two seconds of ninety is the whole price of the pause and it is the engine's price. With the clock stopped nothing costs anything: the brief waits out all three of Squall's lines (quiet now means "a dialogue ENDED", not "none is open" -- the gap between those two sentences is the entire v0.63.0 bug), the screen has no timeout, her position is pinned so an arrow pressed while reading does not fly the ship, and a reminder that never interrupts repeats what ends it. Enter gives the clock back. So do F9, the ten-minute backstop, and walking out of the field -- one owner, one release path, and the probe checks each. AND SR_TICK_HZ WAS WRONG. It said 30, from "field scripts run once a frame", which is a reasonable belief and not what the game does: Aaron's log has x = 896, 848, 800, 752 on consecutive seconds under one held arrow -- FORTY-EIGHT units a second, not a hundred and twenty. Nothing the player hears depended on it; the OFFLINE PROOF did, which is worse. At the true rate a far corner is 8100/48 = 169 seconds away with ninety on the clock, so tests/space_sim_test.cpp no longer passes those starts by accident: the matrix is split by the budget, every start the clock can reach must be WON, and a start outside it must still close at the full rate on both axes for the whole approach -- it runs out of clock, not out of instructions. All three of the scene's own starting errors are inside the budget, which is why he could win it by hand. NEW TEST: tests/countdown_hold_test.cpp RUNS src/countdown_timer.cpp on the host -- its own detection state machine, its own SEH-guarded reads and writes, at the game's own addresses, mmap'd -- and is the first test of any kind over a module that has carried the Dollet and Fire Cavern timers on BAT evidence alone since v0.15.12. It found the one thing that would have broken this release in the field: the stall watch measures time since the value last changed, the value does not change for the whole hold, and without resetting that clock on release the very first Update after Enter throws the timer away. Thirteen mutants, thirteen killed -- including v0.63.0's own quiet test, the fifteen-second timeout, the missing pin, the returning tone, and SR_TICK_HZ back at 30. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.63.0

v0.63.0 (#111 THE SPACE RESCUE, FLYABLE). Aaron, after clearing the escape: "The mini-game was not accessible still for manual play, but the F9 bypass did successfully catch Rinoa and proceed, that means the mod understands how to perform the catch the problem is just announcement and precision. We also need a Game Controls screen like we did for the punch and dragon mini-games. The TTS should speak frequently throughout the game, with maybe a 3-5 second pause in between." And: do it offline, because the scene has an eight-minute story sequence in front of it. WHAT THE LOG SAYS WENT WRONG. v0.62.x called a bearing once a second but swallowed an unchanged phrase. Attempt 1: "right and down" at 14:52:59 with x=2500, and then NOTHING FOR FIFTY-THREE SECONDS, at the end of which x read 2504 -- one unboosted step. He was holding DOWN (Y travelled 628 units) and nothing ever told him the other half of the instruction was not taking. That is the whole failure, and it is a failure of feedback, not of steering. THE OFFLINE SIM. tests/space_sim_test.cpp reproduces the scene from the model's own reading of rinoa::key{l,r,u,d} -- SrStepFrame IS those handlers -- and flies it with a pilot who is given nothing but the strings SrCall produces, on the module's real cadence, with a 400 ms reaction. Aaron's three real starting errors and both far corners all land within a few units of dead centre; the same matrix passes again with a pessimistic sideways drift the log does not show, so the design does not rest on the no-drift reading. The old scheme is run through the same loop and its silence is asserted, so the fix cannot lose its reason. WHAT CHANGED. (1) A GAME CONTROLS SCREEN, in one of the game's own dialog windows -- the same OpenBriefDialog the Garden battle draws -- read aloud and dismissed with Enter, or after fifteen seconds so it can never strand him. It WAITS for the scene's own three lines of Squall's thoughts to finish, because briefing over them means the mod interrupts the game and the game then interrupts the mod; capped at twenty-two seconds, because the approach is on a ninety-second clock. F9 is read before all of it: an escape hatch behind a modal box is not one. (2) A BEARING EVERY 3.5 SECONDS, 1.2 when she is close, SPOKEN WHETHER OR NOT IT CHANGED -- and "still right" when the call repeats and no ground has closed, which is the sentence attempt 1 needed. (3) A RADAR. Words cannot resolve 180 units out of 8100. A beep now plays under everything whose pitch rises (360 Hz to 1320) and whose gap shortens (900 ms to 160) as she centres -- a reversing sensor, which every player can already read. The probe measures the pitch by counting zero crossings in the PCM the module built, so it is checking the audio and not a number. (4) STEER TO THE MIDDLE OF THE BOX. SrMaskFor* stopped asking for a correction at exactly 180, which parks the player on the boundary of a test taken once, at an instant he cannot see coming; a 400 ms reaction is already 48 units of overshoot. The steering deadband is SR_AIM_BOX (60) and "centred" is not said until he is inside it. The verdict is still the game's own 180 -- SrCentred is untouched, because that is the thing being predicted rather than the thing being asked for. The finer bands go with it: "a hair" under 400, "just" under 900, where the old table said nothing at all between 600 and 2700. AND THE CATALOG GOES QUIET. Aaron: "there were some catalog glitches along the way, most notably Ellone being identified as an exit." Two things. On ssspace3 the only catalog entry is Rinoa, listed as "Exit to Outer Space 5" because her script carries the MAPJUMP the win path takes -- and the 14:54:22 log has auto-drive setting off toward her in the middle of the attempt he was flying. There is nothing to navigate to in open space, so the catalog is suppressed for the duration. On sspod2 `elone` carries her MAPJUMP in her OWN talk script, and v0.62.1 dropped the live Ellone in favour of the door at her feet: the one person he needed was announced as an exit. The discriminator is provenance, not distance -- a REQ-follow exit is a mechanism you step on (the pod lift, the Deling buses, all unchanged), while a MAPJUMP in an entity's own talk script, on an entity with a model standing in the room, is a conversation with a consequence. Go to the person. A model-less entity keeps its exit: a trapdoor has nobody to send him to instead. TESTS: disc3_wiring_compile now compiles the REAL window code rather than a stub of it -- the engine's entry points are mapped as bare `ret`s so OpenBriefDialog actually runs -- and asserts the screen, the wait, the cap, the cadence, the "still", the radar's rising pitch and shortening gap, and F9 through all of it. Eleven mutants killed; two candidate branches were deleted rather than kept after no mutation of them could be made to fail. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. THE BOX FITS: nine lines at most 32 columns. The Garden battle's six lines measured 108 px on a 224 px screen, so about eighteen a line and eleven is the ceiling; the probe counts the lines and the widest column rather than trusting the draft, because v0.20.125 already had to go back and add slack under a box that reached the bottom. NOT VERIFIED, and the one thing a BAT still has to settle: that nothing but the player moves the error. The log says so across fifty-three seconds on one axis; the sim passes either way.

## v0.62.3.1

v0.62.3.1 (#123 BUILD FIX). v0.62.3 did not compile: "field_catalog.inl(2916): error C3861: 'JsmGateSatisfied': identifier not found". The gate evaluator was defined in field_archive_jsm_decode.inl, which belongs to the SCANNER's translation unit (field_archive.cpp). The CONSUMER is the catalog, which is compiled inside field_navigation.cpp, and that TU never includes it. Moved to field_archive.h, the header both sides already share, and the call is qualified FieldArchive::JsmGateSatisfied. WHY EVERY GATE HERE WAS GREEN. tests/catalog_harness.cpp compiles field_catalog.inl on its own, so it needs its own includes -- and when I added the evaluator I added `#include "field_archive_jsm_decode.inl"` to the harness to make it resolve. That one line meant the harness was compiling a program the mod does not: 46 fixtures passed, the scanner golden matched, run_gates said fail=0, and the only machine that saw the real translation unit was Aaron's. The same shape as the two duplicated rules v0.62.3 already fixed -- a second copy of something that quietly stopped agreeing with the first -- except here the copy was of the build itself. So the gate now checks for it: tests/lint_harness_includes.py fails if the catalog harness includes a src/ header that is not reachable from field_navigation.cpp. Verified by re-introducing the exact v0.62.3 line and watching it fail. The winshim also gained VOID/LPVOID/LPCWSTR/LPWSTR/WCHAR while checking whether field_navigation.cpp could be syntax-checked wholesale; it cannot -- it carries inline __asm that g++ will never parse -- so the include lint is the check that actually holds. No behaviour change: both goldens are byte-identical.

## v0.62.3

v0.62.3 (#123 THE THIRD PERSON IN THE POD). Aaron, in the escape pod: "It said 3 NPCs, which is/should be correct - Quistis, Piet, and Ellone. However, only two of the three seemed to navigate correctly... I did navigate to the 3rd NPC and it said I was in range, but nothing seemed to happen. There was also an unexpected exit to 'desert 1'." Both come from one line, and the third NPC was never Ellone. THE `pod` LINE. sspod2's only trigger line runs `var[256] == 2556 ... MAPJUMPO 638` -- the pod's departure, gated on a story point the player has not reached. The catalog offered it as "Exit to Desert 1" AND, because a SCREEN_BOUND line is a barrier, let the screen filter cut the room in half along it. Ellone stands at (117,459), beyond y=452; the player at (-34,-13) is on the near side; she was filtered out. The three entries he heard were Quistis, Piet and `handle` -- the pod's release lever, which carries a model and so typed as a person. He walked to a lever. So: A LINE WHOSE OWN SCRIPT IS GATED SHUT IS INERT -- not an exit, and not a wall. v0.62.2 read the story gate on scripted exits; this extends the same decode to any method carrying a MAPJUMP, which is where a trigger line keeps its. Re-evaluated every refresh, because the variable moves while you play, and consulted in all three places a line matters: the exit list, the entity screen filter, and the A* barrier test. AND THE GATE NOW HAS TO COVER THE JUMP. Opcode 0x03 adds its param to the instruction pointer and returns 4, which the VM loop at 0x0052A671 reads as "do not auto-advance" -- so a failed test lands at 4 + n relative to the method start, and a gate only governs an instruction BEFORE that. `pod` m7 is 93 words with the jump landing at 92 and MAPJUMPO at 91; `ele` m3 is 27 with the jump at 26 and its REQ at 25. Both are covered, but 51 of the 272 decodable guards on the disc are not, and those are no longer treated as gates. 221 entities carry one that governs. NAMES: `piet` -> "Piet" (four fields; he was one of three people in the pod, announced as "NPC") and `handle` -> "Handle" (sspod2/sspod3 pod lever, bgmd1_4/gfcar1 valve wheel). A lever announced as a person is a person the player goes looking for. AND A TEST THAT WAS NOT TESTING: catalog_harness kept its own copy of IsSeparatedByTriggerLine. The fixture written to prove the screen-filter fix passed the fixed code and filtered anyway, because the harness was running its restatement of the rule. Both sides now compile src/field_nav_screenfilter.inl, and the harness includes the real gate decoder too rather than a copy of the operator table. TESTS: line_story_gate is sspod2 -- a gated SCREEN_BOUND line with Ellone behind it -- and asserts she survives and no exit is offered. Six mutants killed: the screen filter's gate check, the exit path's, the per-refresh evaluation, the coverage check, skipTo, and the line-gate decode. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.62.2

v0.62.2 (#123 A LIFT THAT IS NOT OPEN YET, AND A SAVE POINT LISTED TWICE). Aaron: "Saw the pod in the catalog this time and it said I arrived at it, but nothing happened even when I pressed the confirm button to activate the lift... Also, noticed this build re-introduced a duplicate 'interaction' at the save point location. It should just have save point in the catalog." (1) THE LIFT WAS NEVER BROKEN -- THE STORY HAD NOT OPENED IT. Everything about reaching it worked: the exit was catalogued at (-30,30), auto-drive walked him onto the platform, and the F11 shot shows Squall standing on it. `ele`'s script opens `PSHM_W var[256]; PSHN_L 2552; ==; JMPZ` and does nothing whatever unless the story word already reads 2552 -- and 2552 is exactly the value `elone`'s talk script writes to var[256] (`PSHN_L 2552; POPM_W 256`) when you speak to Ellone in Control Room 1. She was in the catalog, correctly named "Ellone" by the v0.62.0 model join, on the refresh after arrival. The pod is not a bug; it is the step after the one he had not done. So the catalog now READS THE GATE. The engine's comparison table is at 0x00B8DE4C (6 == 7 > 8 >= 9 < 10 <= 11 !=), dispatched by opcode 0x01's inline param, with 0x03 as jump-if-zero; PSHM_B/W/L (0x0A/0x0C/0x0E) read 1/2/4 bytes zero-extended at 0x01CFE9B8 + param. The scanner decodes the guard a REQ-follow trigger opens with when it has exactly that shape, and the catalog evaluates it against the live variable and drops the exit while it is false. 13 entities on the disc carry a decodable gate, nearly all of them on var[256] -- FF8's story-progress word. The live entity running a shut script goes with it: otherwise closing the gate simply puts the platform back in the list as a nameless "NPC", which is the thing he walked to two builds ago. (2) THE DUPLICATE AT THE SAVE POINT IS A v0.58.0 LEFTOVER. Three catalog lookups map a captured trigger line to its JSM entity as `s_jsmDoors + t`. field_scripts_init consumes the group array Lines, Doors, Backgrounds, Others -- v0.58.0 established that and fixed the scanner, but not these three consumers, so on any field with a door they read the DOOR instead of the line. On ssmedi1 (1 door, 1 line) that made the save-line test ask the door whether it was a save line; the answer was no, the v0.18.3.272 "never add a second Save Point" guard never fired, and the save point's own activation zone was announced beside it as "Interaction 1". The other two lookups were equally wrong on the same fields: the curated line name (Squall's desk, notice boards) and the door-open-trigger suppression. All three now use the line's real group index. It only surfaced now because until v0.62.0 the save point reached the catalog as a JSM injection and the line got folded into it earlier; the model join makes the LIVE entity the save point, so the fold has to happen here. TESTS: two fixtures. saveline_with_door is built on a field WITH A DOOR and exercises all three lookups at once -- a save line that folds, a 'Cliant' line that must read "Desk", and a 'door01' line that must be suppressed beside its screen-bound exit. mapexit_story_gate has one exit gated ==2552 against a live 2550 (dropped, and its platform with it) and one gated >=2000 (kept). The scanner dump gains a gate= column. Seven mutants killed: all three line indices, the gate check, the gate operator table, the gate decode, and the shut-script entity drop. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0.

## v0.62.1

v0.62.1 (#123 THE LIFT, PROPERLY). Aaron on the v0.62.0 BAT: "Exit to the pod did not show in the catalog in this test. There is also an NPC that I arrived at but didn't seem to do anything." One object, `ele` -- the red platform in the Lunar Base control room 2 -- and three separate things wrong with it. (1) THE EXIT WAS FILTERED, NOT MISSING. v0.62.0's REQ-follow correctly made `ele` the exit at (-30,30): the log says so twice, "REQ-follow: ent8 'ele' triggers ent9 method48, which MAPJUMPs to 870 -- it IS the exit" and "ent9 'director1' ... is retired in its favour". Then: "JSM exit 'ele' dest=870 filtered (no matching INF gateway on this field)". The v0.12.08 filter drops a scripted destination no INF gateway serves, on the reasoning that it is probably a stale variable read -- and exempts destinations the mapjump resolver produced, which are authoritative (paramFromInterp). The REQ-follow copied the destination but not its provenance, and it ran BEFORE MapjumpResolver::Run, so there was no provenance to copy yet: on sscont2 the resolver reaches 870 through the variable block and marks it INTERP. The pass now runs after the resolver and takes the owner's param AND its paramFromInterp, which is right in principle as well as in effect -- the destination belongs to the entity that owns the MAPJUMP, and only the resolver knows it for certain. (2) THE NPC HE ARRIVED AT WAS THE LIFT. `ele` was in the catalog twice: once from the runtime scan as a plain "NPC" and once as the exit. He walked to the NPC, and a platform you are standing next to does nothing. A live entity whose OWN script has already been catalogued as a JSM special or exit is now dropped -- and this is not a distance test, which is what makes it safe: the v0.62.0 model join says outright which live entity runs which script, so the two entries are provably one object and the one that says what it does survives. (3) AND AUTO-DRIVE STOPPED 300 UNITS SHORT. A scripted exit has no gateway line to cross and no talk radius to stop at, so it fell through to DRIVE_ARRIVE_DIST_DEFAULT. You get onto a lift the way you get onto a save point -- by standing on it -- so a JSM-injected exit now uses arriveDist=30, the same walk-onto distance save points have used since v0.17.6.0. TESTS: three mutants killed (the live-is-the-JSM-object drop, and both halves of the destination/provenance carry). mapexit_live_slot and mapexit_party_member both lose their live duplicate, which is the new rule working; the scanner dump gains an interp= column so the golden can see provenance at all -- it could not before, which is exactly why this shipped broken. tests/run_gates.sh: overall fail=0. The arriveDist change is the one thing here no harness covers; it is a constant on a target type and shows up in the drive log as "scripted exit ... -> arriveDist=30".

## v0.62.0

v0.62.0 (#123 WHO IS THAT, ACTUALLY). Aaron, on the Lunar Base control room: "the catalog included Rinoa, Selphie, and Quistis, but only Quistis is present. When I spoke to 'Quistis' in the catalog it turned out to be a different NPC. I believe this is because we determined long ago SYM names are unreliable... Perhaps we can check the specific model the NPC is using and tell from that?" He is right about the fix and, it turns out, half right about the cause: the SYM STRINGS are fine. What was wrong is which live entity each one was being pinned to. (1) THE LIVE ARRAY IS NOT INDEXED BY SLOT. Everything that named or typed a running entity did it as `s_symNames[s_symOthersOffset + i]` or FindJSMByRuntimeSlot(i) -- "live entity i is script slot i". field_scripts_init does fill the script-object table at 0x01D9D020 that way, but the array the catalog walks, pFieldStateOthers, is a different array: it holds only the entities the running scene instantiated, compacted. On sscont1 the live models read 0, 5, 6, 6, 8, 9 while the script slots in order are squall=0 squallsp=1 irvine=2 rinoa=3 selphie=4 quistis=5 man0=6 man1=6 oldlag=7 woman0=8 piet=9 -- so live ent5 is PIET, and slot-indexing announced him as Quistis. Replayed over every field load in the BAT log, the live index equalled the slot in 17 of 90 cases. (2) SETMODEL'S PARAMETER IS THE KEY. It is this entity's index into the field's chara.one model list -- sscont1's is [d052 d060 d016 d024 d027 d018 p166 d062 p167 p164 p002 d061], and its scripts assign squall=0(d052) irvine=2(d016) quistis=5(d018) piet=9(p164), so the model files corroborate the SYMs name for name -- and the live entity block carries the same number at +0x218. The script assigns it per entity, so no compaction can disturb it. 95.6% of model ids are unique within their field; the rest are shared by name-twins (soldier1/soldier2, quistis/quistis2), broken by nearest static SET3 position and then by collapsing names that differ only in a trailing digit. Entities the script never gave a model -- save points, script objects -- are matched on sitting EXACTLY where their own SET3 put them. Replayed against the BAT log: 138 of 138 placed entities resolved, none ambiguous, none unmatched. Where nothing proves an identity the answer is now no name and no script-derived type, which is a great deal better than a confident wrong one. (3) AND SO THE CATALOG CAN NAME PEOPLE. Aaron: "I love the idea of the catalog identifying NPCs when it can." A live NPC now takes its display name from its own script's SYM whenever that SYM is in ENTITY_DISPLAY_NAMES -- an uncurated SYM is an internal dev symbol and is still never spoken (v0.18.3.291). v0.61.0's duplicate-drop name transfer needed a second JSM copy of the same person to exist before it could name anyone, and, joining on the slot, is exactly what put "Quistis" on Piet. (4) THE LIFT. Aaron: "you have to go down a lift to proceed but auto-drive failed to get me there. There was no specific elevator or lift in the catalog." There was one -- "Exit to Lunar Base - Pod 1" -- attributed to `director1`, a script object with no position, so it sat at (0,0) and navigation answered "Target not yet located." The thing you step on is `ele`, the red platform at (-30,30); its script REQs director1's method 48, and the MAPJUMP3 to field 870 lives there. Attributing an exit to the entity that TRIGGERS it gives the exit a position for free. That rule has existed since v0.07.84 and had never once fired as intended, for two independent reasons, both fixed here: it ran inside the per-entity scan loop so it could only see methods already scanned (and directors are declared last), and s_entityReqs was empty on every field in the game. (5) REQ, READ CORRECTLY. The recorder wanted three stack values and took the target off the stack. REQ takes two: the compiler emits `PSHN priority; PSHN methodId; REQ <entity>` and the target is the INLINE param (handler 0x0051CD8D indexes the object table with it). Since v0.59.0 clears the push run after every non-push opcode, pushCount at a REQ is exactly 2, so `pushCount >= 3` was never true. The scanner's own [REQ-TARGET] diagnostic has been printing the right answer beside it the whole time. The method id is the GLOBAL entry-table index -- the same number the method's own prologue (0x05) carries -- so the consumer's `startMethodIdx + tgtMeth` was double-adding; verified exhaustively on sscont1, where moonscope's REQs to methods 18, 129, 4, 5, 9, 75 and 84 each land inside the method range of the entity its inline param names. That containment is now asserted rather than assumed. (6) THE TERMINAL, FOR THE RIGHT REASON THIS TIME. v0.61.0 restored the moon scope by promoting on hasDialogReqTarget -- but with s_entityReqs empty, what actually fired was the "does this field contain ANY Interactive Object" fallback beside it. With REQ targets resolving, that coincidence is gone and `moonscope` REQs six entities of which none has a single dialog opcode. The real signal is in the line's own script: it calls LINEOFF in its init and LINEON in a method that `irvine`, `selphie` and `quistis` each REQ from one the SYM names `moon_lineon0`. Both halves are load-time facts, and a passive cutscene tripwire has neither. (Exe-confirmed: opcode 0x3A writes 1 and 0x3B writes 0 to the line object's enable byte at +0x194, handlers 0x0051DCE0 / 0x0051DD00.) 28 lines on the disc change on this signal alone. (7) A PARTY MEMBER IS NEVER A DOOR: the REQ-follow is right for a lift or a Deling City bus and wrong when the trigger is the leader's own cutscene script, so a scripted exit whose live entity reads a party setpc is dropped. TESTS: catalog_harness gains live_join_passes (every branch of the join, with static positions deliberately unequal to live ones) and mapexit_party_member, and now #includes the REAL join source rather than a restatement of it; nine mutants -- model key, position tiebreak, twin collapse, model-less position pass, own-script naming, party-exit guard, REQ method operand, method-index double-add, line promotion, positionless-exit retirement -- all killed. field_archive_jsm_scan.inl crossed the 80 KB gate and its two cross-reference post-passes were extracted to field_archive_jsm_reqpass.inl and field_archive_jsm_linepass.inl. NOT DONE, and the better answer when it comes: +0x194 is readable at runtime, so the catalog could offer a trigger line only while the game actually has it switched on, instead of inferring it at load.

## v0.61.0

v0.61.0 (#122 THE LUNAR BASE BAT). Aaron, on the room his save loads into: "it said there were 3 NPCs, but there were really just two"; on the control room: "it had quite an extensive list of NPCs but there seemed to be phantoms and duplicates among them"; and "there is also a control panel you are supposed to look at / operate and I couldn't find it... I also couldn't find the NPC to let me talk to Quistis in this scene. The terminal you are supposed to use is next to Quistis." Four causes, one of them mine from two versions ago. (1) THE TERMINAL IS A v0.59.0 REGRESSION I INTRODUCED. The moon scope on sscont1 is the Line entity `moonscope`, runtime slot 20, and `irvine`, `selphie` and `quistis` each REQ it from a method named `moon_lineon0` -- talking to any of them switches the terminal on. v0.59.0 deleted `foundExtDispatch` because the decode work proved the opcode it keyed on was being read wrong; what I did not do was replace what it had been standing in for, which was the last thing classifying a dialog-dispatching line as interactive. `moonscope` fell to the eventOp branch and became an Event Trigger, which the catalog treats as transparent scenery and never announces. A line that dispatches to an entity that talks is now promoted LINE_EVENT -> LINE_INTERACTIVE on `hasDialogReqTarget` -- the signal the old flag was a bad proxy for. Disc-wide effect measured before committing: exactly 89 lines change, every one of them cat1, every one Event Trigger -> Interactive Line, no other field in the 866-field golden moves. (2) THE THIRD NPC IN THE INFIRMARY. ssmedi1 listed `irvine`, `rinoa` and `squallrinoa`; the third sits at exactly (559,-882), which is the save point. The runtime-vs-special dedupe that exists for precisely this required its special to be a captured TRIGGER LINE (sentinel -200..-299) -- but on this field the save LINE had already been folded into the JSM save point earlier in the same refresh, so by the time the dedupe ran there was no line left to match and the model standing on the save point stayed in the list. It now accepts a special from any non-runtime source and resolves its position through CatalogEntryPos, which reads every source the same way. A special is a special wherever the catalog got it from. (3) THE SAME ENTITY, TWICE. The control room listed ten things for four people and two doors. Three of the ten were `rinoa`, `selphie` and `quistis` injected as JSM objects at their static SET3 positions -- (43,30) and (194,130) twice, one position for two different people -- while the very same entities were already in the catalog from the runtime scan at their real live positions. Runtime Others slot i is JSM group (nLines+nDoors+nBg+i), so the two entries are provably the same object and the live one holds the true position: the JSM copy is dropped. (4) AND THAT IS ALSO WHY QUISTIS WAS UNFINDABLE. The runtime scan calls every visible character "NPC"; the name lived on the JSM copy that was being dropped. So when the copy goes, its curated ENTITY_DISPLAY_NAMES name moves onto the live entry -- "NPC" becomes "Quistis". Only a curated name transfers; a generic type name teaches the live entry nothing. (5) A CARD PLAYER WHO IS NOT IN THE SCENE. `piet` was offered as a Card Game at a static position with nobody standing there: his live entity reads model=-1 tri=0 pos=(0,0), exactly what the v0.20.31 scene-actor test already drops -- except that test is gated on `jt == ENT_OBJECT`, so a special sailed straight past it. Card games and shops are people and are now held to the same test. Save and draw points are deliberately exempt: they are not people and are routinely script-only with no live entity at all -- the infirmary save point in (2) is one -- and the draw point has its own sparkle gate. catalog_harness gains three fixtures (a JSM object duplicating a live slot, with a curated name, an uncurated one and a slot with no live entity; an unplaced card game beside an unplaced save point that must survive; and a runtime model standing on a JSM-injected save point) and both goldens are re-baselined. The only pre-existing catalog fixture that moves is jsm_drawpoint_consolidation, where the co-located NPC is now correctly consolidated into the draw point. All four new rules mutation-checked: disabling any one of them fails the harness.

## v0.60.0

(#121 THE WAY OUT TO THE WORLD MAP). Aaron, on the 12 fields the v0.59.0 exit audit found with no listed exit: "in those cases there should still be an exit to the world map in the catalog." Right, and it is a wider set than those 12 -- 59 fields in the game have a way out to the world map, and it was going missing two different ways. (1) THE TRIGGER LINES. WORLDMAPJUMP (0x10D, handler 0x00521820) sets the transition mode at 0x01CE4760 to 7 where every field-to-field jump sets 1, and the scanner already marks its destination with the sentinel -2, which the line-exit path already knows to call "Exit to World Map". But the v0.20.29 camera-view-transition rule identifies those lines by the word "jump" appearing in the SYM name, and NINETEEN world-map lines match it -- including the line named literally `Jump` in every one of the seven Chocobo Forest woods, plus `WorldJump`, `wmjumpline0`, `WMJumpline1..4`, `worldjumpline0` and `WmJump`. They were labelled "Camera transition" and then zone-filtered like one, which is exactly how a field whose only way out is the world map ends up with nothing in the catalog at all. A world-map exit is now never a camera transition: there is no camera view of the world map to transition to, and the test is the destination sentinel, not another name. (2) THE SCRIPTED ONES. -2 is negative, so `param < 0` suppressed every world-map MAP_EXIT on any field that also has INF gateways -- which is most of the fields that have one, because they are town gates and garden entrances. Fourteen exits across eleven fields, among them `ekiin` the station attendant on ggsta1, `carman0` on glrent1 and `RentaCar1`/`RentaCar4` on gmout1 -- the train and the rental car, i.e. two of the ways you leave a town. An INF gateway's destination is a field id and the world map has none, so the gateway-match filter could never be satisfied by one of these; both suppressions now exempt it. ALSO, same class of bug as v0.58.0 and found while tracing this: the unpositioned-MAP_EXIT live-position fallback read `je.jsmIndex` as if it were a runtime slot. Its comment argues the two are 1:1 "with NO subtraction", citing glprein1's trapdoor (jsmIndex 2, seen as ent2) and glwater1's sakua/sakub/oku (jsmIndex 17/18/19) -- but glprein1 has 2 background entities, so its first Other IS group 2 and runtime slot 0 and the two readings disagree there, and glwater1 has 5 lines and 4 backgrounds, so 17/18/19 are slots 8/9/10, which also dissolves the stated reason for believing the unshifted reading. Reading the wrong slot fabricates a position for a map exit out of some other entity's feet: a phantom exit that looks perfectly plausible. It uses JSMEntityInfo::runtimeSlot now, and so does the SETLINE-owner match beside it. catalog_harness gains three fixtures (a world-map trigger line, a world-map exit on a field with gateways, and a live-slot position fetch with a decoy sitting at the old index) and its dump now carries the RESOLVED POSITION of every entry, through the catalog's own CatalogEntryPos -- a phantom is usually a wrong position rather than a wrong name, and without the column the golden could not tell a fabricated exit from a real one. Re-baselined; every pre-existing line is byte-identical apart from the new column. Both new behaviours mutation-checked. NOT changed, and worth recording: the "*jump*" name test is wrong in the other direction too. Of the 149 Line entities whose name contains "jump", 108 jump to a genuinely different field and ZERO have a self-destination, while 7 lines that DO have one (`el1` elevators, `ladline4-6`, `bossbattle1/2`) are not named that way at all. Replacing it needs a real discriminator; the obvious candidate -- does the arrival point lie inside the source field's own walkmesh -- does not separate them (gnroad2 and the eccway12 Pandora line both read as "inside"), so it stays for now rather than being swapped for another guess.

## v0.59.0

(#120 THE INSTRUCTION DECODE WAS WRONG, AND EVERYTHING DOWNSTREAM WAS COMPENSATING FOR IT). Continuing the field-catalog review. The field script VM's decoder is at FF8_EN.exe 0x00530760 and it says: if the high byte of the word is zero the WHOLE WORD is the opcode and there is no parameter; otherwise the opcode is the high byte and the parameter is the sign-extended low 24 bits. The scanner had read a high-byte-zero word as a LITERAL PUSH since v0.07.x, and opcode 0x07 as 'PSHM_W, push a word from memory'. Both are wrong. 0x07 is PSHN_L (0x0051C990) and pushes its own inline parameter, and a high-byte-zero word is simply how every opcode above 0xFF is encoded -- MENUSAVE 0x12E, ADDITEM 0x125, DRAWPOINT 0x137, CARDGAME 0x13A, SETDRAWPOINT 0x155. THE COST: the old model turned every NON-NEGATIVE 0x07 parameter into a fake 'comes from runtime memory' marker, and 8289 of the 8625 SET3 placements on the disc have at least one non-negative coordinate -- so 96% of all entity positions in the game were discarded as unresolvable. That is what the triangle-centroid approximation, the late-resolve pass and the struct-position scan have all been compensating for. It also invented positions: 51 entities were being placed at coordinates read off a drifting simulated stack, and EVERY ONE of them has no SET or SET3 anywhere in its script -- 'director0', 'moviedir', 'tmpdir', 'check', 'map'. Invisible controllers, given a spot on the map. Read correctly, 4539 of 4593 static positions (98.8%) land strictly INSIDE the walkmesh triangle their own SET3 names -- an independent check, since the triangle is the opcode's inline parameter and the coordinates are popped values. MEASURED ACROSS ALL 866 FIELDS, old scanner vs new: +2984 entities gain a real position, 51 lose a fabricated one; Map Exit 375 -> 810 (435 exits that were invisible); Card Game 0 -> 98 (every Triple Triad opponent in the game was undetected); Draw Point 114 -> 227; NPC 11 -> 134; and Interactive Object 2104 -> 454, because 'hasExtDispatch' -- which fired whenever opcode 0x1C appeared, i.e. in 92.8% of all entities -- was promoting inert scenery. 0x1C is a two-instruction no-op (0x0051D710); there is no extended dispatch. ALSO CORRECTED, all from the handler table at 0x00B8DE94: the pop-to-savemap opcodes are 0x0B/0x0D/0x0F, not 0x08 (0x08 is PSHL, a PUSH of a local), so half the variable-write record was reading the wrong opcode; MAPJUMPO takes two arguments, not four; and opcodes 0x25-0x28 do not mark a ladder -- 0x00525900 writes a movement mode onto the entity that RUNS them, which is the character doing the climbing. In glwater3 and glwater2 the ladder objects carry none of them and only the six party members do, so with the decode corrected the mod would have started announcing Squall as a Ladder. ITEM-vs-NPC, second pass: 'wrote a savemap variable outside init' matched 876 entities across 400 fields -- Raijin, Fuujin, Cid, most of Balamb. A collectible GATES ITSELF: init reads a variable to learn whether it has already been taken and the interaction method writes that same variable, after which it hides; ADDITEM is the other, now-exact path; and a collectible is never talked to. 89 entities match. Timber Maniacs, the Weapons Monthlies, 'hon', 'book' and the itemkun drops all survive. NEW INFRASTRUCTURE: tests/jsm_scan_harness runs the REAL ScanJSMScripts on the build host over the real field files and diffs 866 fields against tests/jsm_scan_golden.txt -- nothing on this side of the build could execute the scanner at all before, because field_archive.cpp is a Win32 translation unit whose archive reader wants the game's 294 MB field.fs. tests/winshim gives it a windows.h, FF8OPC_ARCHIVE_TEST_SEAM gives it its files, and fieldsim/extract_fields.py regenerates them. jsm_decode_test checks the encoding against 59 real SET3 sequences plus the walkmesh geometry each one has to produce, and asserts the OLD reading resolves none of them; 7 mutations applied, 7 killed. One housekeeping item from the same pass: the curated-name lookup in the item relabel is a plain function rather than a lambda, because DedupeCatalog's neighbourhood carries __try and a lambda in an SEH function is the exact shape of MSVC C2712 -- a captureless one is very probably fine, but 'very probably' costs a build cycle and Aaron is the only person who can run one. lint_seh now flags a lambda in any function containing __try; verified by injecting one into IsDrawPointLivePresent, where it fires.

## v0.58.0

(#119 THE FILE LAYOUT WAS WRONG IN THREE PLACES AT ONCE). Aaron reported more phantoms lately and NPCs read out as Items. Both trace to field_scripts_init (FF8_EN.exe 0x0052BC00), which builds a field's script objects in four loops and settles three orderings this codebase has been guessing at since v0.07.73 -- disagreeing with it on all three. (1) The .jsm group-word array is ordered LINES, DOORS, Backgrounds, Others, not Door-first: on the 79 fields carrying both, the first min(nD,nL) groups had Door and Line swapped, so 30 real trigger Lines carrying a MAPJUMP (to_fhtown23, jumpline0, winedoor, ...) were typed JSM_ENT_DOOR and never scanned as exits. (2) The runtime object table at 0x01D9D020 is ordered Others, Lines, Backgrounds, Doors, and REQ/REQSW/REQEW index it directly with their inline param (0x0051CD8D) -- the scanner was using that as a group index, so on nearly every field the REQ-target set was shifted and the director gate kept and dropped arbitrary entities. (3) The .sym bare-name list is ordered Others, Lines, Backgrounds (doors omitted), each block in code order; the scanner assumed Lines, Backgrounds, Others. A v0.20.26 heuristic papered over this by guessing each name's category from its method names, and on ecenter1, ecmway1 and ecoway1 -- three of the biggest Esthar fields -- the guess failed and it fell back to the broken path: on ecoway1 ALL 35 names were on the wrong entity, rotated by nBackgrounds. Across the disc, 150 of 849 fields carry wrong entity names today, 41 of them completely wrong. All three are now read out of the group words by JSMOrderMap (field_archive_jsm_order.inl); the heuristic is deleted. NPC-vs-Item: the relabel asked 'does ANY script entity share this walkmesh triangle and grant an item?', a workaround adopted because names were unreliable -- true, but from this ordering bug, and the workaround swaps identities whenever two entities stand on one triangle. A person standing where a magazine lies was announced as Item, and the magazine, having been claimed, never surfaced. It now joins on the runtime slot, which is an identity: Others slot i is JSM group nLines+nDoors+nBg+i. Also a separate phantom source: the v0.20.45 post-battle trigger-line backup was a function-local static keyed only on field id and never invalidated, so a previous visit's lines could be restored into a later visit whose scripts run no SETLINE. It is dropped on a real field change now; returning from a battle, the one case it exists for, still keeps it. catalog_harness RUNS again -- it has been compile-only since v0.20.48, dying on fixture 7 because the draw-point gate reads three hardcoded engine addresses that g++'s no-op __try cannot survive; the pages are mapped, all 35 fixtures execute (two new: the sparkle gate, and NPC-vs-Item identity), and catalog_golden.txt is re-baselined. I verified the new code is byte-identical to v0.57.1 on all 33 original fixtures BEFORE re-baselining, so none of the drift is from this change. New tests/run_gates.sh runs linters, the 80 KB size gate and every harness. jsm_order_test checks the order map against the two independent halves of the real .sym for 16 fields; 9 mutations applied, 9 killed.

## v0.57.1

**v0.57.1 (#110 — THE CONTACT POINT WAS NOT IN HIS CATALOG, AND AARON WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE TIMING).** He completed the run and boarded at contact point 2, but never reached point 1, and reported: *"The instructions said something about having to cross at a certain time, but that is not correct — for all three contact points if you get to the right point and just wait it will trigger."* Both halves of that are the log's story exactly. **WHY POINT 1 WAS UNREACHABLE — ONE LINE OF LOG.** v0.57.0 correctly told him to cross `eccway21`'s trigger line and correctly named where it leads. The catalog had already thrown that entry away: `[refresh] camera-transition line0 filtered: not a boundary of player's zone [v0.20.29]`. So the thing he was told to walk to did not appear in his catalog, the GPS could not be pointed at it, and he spent **eight minutes bouncing between `ecmway1`, `ecopen3`, `eccway12` and `eccway21`** hunting for an exit that was not on any list — through the whole 15:00–12:00 window — before the point lapsed. **AND THE CONTROL IS IN THE SAME LOG.** In `eccway41` the same kind of line SURVIVED that filter, was catalogued (as "Camera transition"), and he selected it, `[GPS] Started: Camera transition dir=west dist=1936 steps=7`, walked onto it, and boarded at contact point 2 on the first attempt. **Identical mechanism; the only difference was whether it was in the list.** The v0.20.29 zone filter is right in general — it stops the catalog offering camera lines you cannot walk to — and wrong about the objective of a timed minigame. A contact-point line is now **exempt from it while the run is live, and named "Contact point 1/2/3"** instead of "Camera transition", which told the player nothing. `field_catalog.inl` asks the new `EpContactLineAt()`, matching on field plus line midpoint. **The midpoints are cross-validated: the values extracted offline from each entity's own LINE opcode and the values the BAT's own `[LINE-PAIR]` capture reported agree to within ONE UNIT on all six** — `(3679,1248)` vs `(3679,1248)`, `(-5032,-4205)` vs `(-5033,-4205)`, `(-1713,-6966)` vs `(-1714,-6966)` — so the 64-unit match tolerance is slack rather than fudge. **AARON IS RIGHT ABOUT THE TIMING FOR TWO POINTS OUT OF THREE, AND THE SCRIPTS SAY WHICH TWO.** A line's miss-branch — where crossing outside the window puts you — is a neighbouring field, and for the CP1 and CP3 lines that neighbour is the **stand-and-wait site for the same contact point**: `eccway11`/`eccway21` miss to `eciway11`, `eccway41`/`ecmall1` miss to `ecoway3`, and both of those poll and board you by themselves. So for points 1 and 3 the honest instruction is **go now, whatever the clock says** — cross in the window and you board on the spot, cross early and you land where it happens on its own. v0.57.0 told him to time every crossing; that was wrong for two points out of three and needlessly hard. **CP2 is the genuine exception**: its two lines are the single doorway between `eccway12` and `eccway41` and each misses to the *other*, neither of which polls, so crossing early there only walks you back and forth. It is now the one place the mod asks anyone to wait for a window — and it says an early crossing is recoverable rather than fatal. New `EpMissIsAuto()` decides this from the site table rather than from prose. **A STOPPED CLOCK IS NOT AN EXPIRED ONE.** The BAT opened with `t=0 point=3 open=0` in `ecmview1` — before `ecmview1 :: Timelimit::default` had run its `SETTIMER 1201` — and v0.57.0 announced contact point **3**, the last one, as the target, because a clock that has not started and one that has run out read identically. Zero now means "not started" until a non-zero value has been seen once. **"/" IS ANSWERED FIRST.** The probe caught a slash immediately after a contact-point transition getting nothing back: the transition branch can be throttled by the 1.5 s floor and then `return`, swallowing the question. An explicit request is now handled before any of the transition branches. **Verified: five linters OK; size gate OK (largest non-exempt 81,711); every probe and harness compiles and passes as before; `catalog_harness` compiles the changed `field_catalog.inl` and caught the exemption's missing dependency on the first try — an MSVC-only break otherwise (`'EstharSite' does not name a type`) — and the model is now included there for that coverage. 8 mutations applied across the model and the wiring, 8 killed.** **⚠ HONEST GAP: the catalog exemption itself is compile-covered but not behaviour-covered**, because `catalog_harness` still cannot RUN on the host (the pre-existing v0.20.48 draw-point segfault). It logs its own decision on one line, which is what the BAT should check. **BAT: this run is one-shot, so aim at contact point 1 and expect it to be easy.** (1) When the run starts you should hear the greeting ONCE, then silence. Press `/` — it should name **contact point 1** (not 3) and give a clock that counts down from about 19:50. (2) Walk the named exits. On reaching a field that holds the trigger, `/` should say *"Head for Contact point 1 in the catalog and cross it — you can go now."* (3) **Cycle the catalog: there should be an entry literally called "Contact point 1".** Select it, let the GPS walk you onto it, and you should board — either immediately, or by landing in Esthar - City 21 and being taken aboard when the clock reaches 15:00. **If no such catalog entry exists, that is the whole bug and the log line `line0 is Esthar contact point 1 -- KEPT despite the zone filter` will be missing; send the log.** (4) If you miss point 1, point 3 behaves the same way (its marker is "Contact point 3" and crossing early lands you where it happens by itself). Point 2 is the only one that needs its window, and the mod will say so.

## v0.57.0

**v0.57.0 (#110 — THE PANDORA RUN: THE MOD SAID "WAIT" AT A DOOR YOU HAVE TO WALK THROUGH).** Aaron reached the Esthar minigame. The mod told him he was standing on contact point 1 with the window open; nothing happened. *"If you are in the right place it happens automatically."* He is right, and v0.55.0 had him in the wrong kind of place. **THE MECHANISM IS A WALK-THROUGH LINE.** Boarding is a MAPJUMP to field 417/418/419 (ecenc1/2/3).
