An exhaustive scan of all 892 fields finds **exactly eight in the whole game**, and six of them are `Linejump1::touch` or `Linejump2::touch` — the engine's `touch` event, which fires when the player **walks through a trigger line**. On every one of those entities `talk`, `push`, `across`, `touchOff` and `touchOn` are two-instruction stubs, so crossing the line is the only way to fire anything. **Waiting is the one action that cannot work there**, and waiting is what the mod told him to do. The other two sites are the opposite — `eciway11 :: JumpTimer::defalut` and `ecoway3 :: TimerJump::defalut` are polling loops that fire by themselves the moment the window opens — and those are what the route now aims at. **AND THE TWO KINDS COMPOSE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.** Every line's miss-branch — what happens if you cross it outside the window — is an ordinary map transition, and in five of six cases it lands you on a trigger for the *same* contact point. Both CP1 lines miss to **eciway11**; both CP3 lines miss to **ecoway3**. So "get to eciway11 and wait" is correct whether the clock is ready or not: cross early and you arrive at the site that fires on its own, cross during the window and you board on the way. That is the only shape of instruction a blind player can act on without watching a timer, and it is now what the mod gives. Aaron was **one exit** from it and was told to stand still. **THE CLOCK WAS READ FROM THE WRONG PLACE, AND THAT IS WHAT BROKE EVERYTHING ELSE.** v0.55.0 preferred `var[1024]`, falling back to the engine dword. var[1024] is the **timer HUD mirror `info::default` re-establishes every frame**, so reads land mid-update and return 0. In the BAT the clock alternated between the true value and zero on consecutive ticks, which flipped the target contact point 3→1→3 and fired the "point has passed" and "window open" announcements over and over: **six interrupting utterances in a single second, ~420 log lines a second, for the whole run.** That is also Aaron's *"I think it was also breaking auto-drive somehow"* — nothing else the mod said could be heard through it. There is one truth and it is one address: GETTIMER (opcode 0x0A4, handler `0x00521710`) is `mov eax,[0x01CFE92C]`, and all eight boarding gates compare against that. So does the mod now, **with no fallback** — an unreadable clock means say nothing, not guess. **A FLOOR UNDER THE SPEECH, INDEPENDENTLY.** Fixing the clock removes the cause, which is not the same as making it impossible, so nothing this module says may follow anything else by less than 1.5 s; `/` bypasses it, because being asked a question is not flapping. The first version of that floor covered only *interrupting* speech and the probe caught it letting a flapping field queue 600 non-interrupting lines in ten seconds — which is not politer, it is the same unusability with a delay. The floor is unconditional now. **THE WINDOWS ARE PER-SITE AND THREE OF THEM DIFFER FROM THE DISPLAY LADDER.** The briefing and the `Disp` ladder say 15:00–12:00, 10:00–5:00, 3:00–0:00 — but the gates are `t <= 900` at eciway11 and `t <= 903` at the two CP1 lines, and **ecmall1 alone uses `LT`, one second narrower than every other CP3 gate**. Each site now carries its own bound; the planning windows are the intersection, so "the window is open" is true wherever the player is standing. **WHAT THE PLAYER HEARS.** Which exit, by the name the CATALOG uses for it ("Take the exit to Esthar - City 21"), so it can be cycled to and walked to — not the internal field name v0.55.0 spoke, which meant nothing. On arrival: at a stand-and-wait site, *"Stay exactly where you are — it takes you aboard on its own"*; at a line, *"Contact point 1 is open. Walk through the exit to Esthar - City 21 now — crossing it is what takes you aboard"*, and when it is early, *"a crossing, not a place to wait… going early only puts you there, and that side opens by itself in 4 minutes."* A contact point already spent says so (`var[678]` bit 0 for CP1, bit 1 for CP2) instead of promising a boarding that cannot happen. **THE ROUTE TABLE IS REGENERATED FROM THE REAL CITY GRAPH.** v0.55.0 BFS'd over the `.inf` pedestrian gateways alone, and Esthar's connectivity is mostly script MAPJUMPs — which is why it sent Aaron to eccway21 and then had nothing to say. The graph is now the union of both, minus `efbig1` (the timeout jump, in every field) and the three boarding fields: **47 city fields, every one of which reaches every contact point**, and `offline/gen_esthar_tables.py` reproduces the shipped table exactly. **A DECODE BUG THAT CAUSED THE WRONG STORY.** `.jsm` entry offsets carry a 0x8000 flag the engine masks off itself (`0x0052BF98` / `0x0052C0A4`, `and eax,0x7fff`). Read unmasked, eccway21's `entries[210..217]` come out as 36247.. against a 6756-dword code array, **seven methods collapse into their predecessor**, and the CP1 trigger reads as `Edea::afkantei2` instead of `Linejump1::touch`. Every masked value lands on opcode 0x005, the SCRIPT marker. That single missing mask is how v0.55.0 came to describe a walk-through line as a lifter and to invent a menu for it. **THREE OTHER CORRECTIONS TO WHAT v0.55.0 BELIEVED.** `var[678]` bit 2 is **not** "CP3 used" — ecenc3 sets it only on the timer-expired exit and **no gate anywhere reads it**, so CP3 can be retried. `var[1029]`, which gates the two automatic sites, is a per-field-load scratch byte: the engine zeroes `var[1024..1279]` in the field-script loader (`0x0052C426`, the only such write in the image), so it cannot be left dirty by talking to someone in a previous field. And no menu is involved in any boarding path at all — the "Inner Skyway / Get off / Keep going" chooser belongs to `Director::defalut` and is hidden outright while the run is live. **Verified: five linters OK (lint_stub caught a `Say` collision with menu_sim.cpp — renamed); size gate OK; 37 of 38 probes and harnesses pass, catalog_harness still excepted; disc3_models_compile now decodes all eight gates out of the shipped .jsm and checks the model against each one's window, used-bit, kind and miss-branch; 12 mutations applied across the model and the wiring and all 12 killed.** **BAT: the run is one-shot, so this is the shape of it.** (1) At the start you should hear *"Lunatic Pandora run"* ONCE and then nothing until you move or press `/`. **If you hear a stream of chatter, stop and send the log — that is the old fault and everything after it is unreliable.** (2) Press `/`. Expect a clock that counts down sensibly, "Contact point 1, the centre of the city", and **"Take the exit to Esthar - City NN"**. Follow those exits; each new field should give you one line and then be quiet. (3) The destination is **Esthar - City 21 (eciway11)**. When you get there it should say *"Wait right here… it takes you aboard on its own."* **Then genuinely do nothing.** If the window is still shut it opens at 15:00 on the clock and boards you; if it is already open it should board you within a second or two. (4) If you cross into City 21 while the window is open you may board on the way in — that is expected and is the same success. (5) `[ESTHAR]` log lines carry `t=`, `point=`, `open=`, `hops=`, `next=` and `site=AUTO|LINE` on every field change, which is enough to reconstruct the whole run if it goes wrong. (6) **Contact point 1 is the only one worth aiming at on a first attempt** — CP2 has no stand-and-wait site (its trigger is the doorway between City 3 and City 13, walked through in either direction) and CP3 is the last chance at 3:00.

## v0.56.0

**v0.56.0 (#118 — AUTO-DRIVE ON ESTHAR: ONE STALE BYTE, FIVE DEAD DOORS, AND A CIRCLE THE LOG DRAWS EXACTLY).** Aaron reached disc 3 and drove to Lunar Gate, Sorceress Memorial and Tears' Point. None arrived. Three failures, two causes, and both are in the shipped data rather than in the terrain. **CAUSE ONE, AND IT EXPLAINS TWO OF THE THREE: THE MOD THOUGHT HE WAS PILOTING A SHIP.** At 20:40:41 the world-map entry debounce logged `Snapshot baseline locomotion=3 (was 0, suppressed 102937ms of byte noise)`. **Locomotion 3 is VEH_GARDEN — the Ship.** He was on foot in Esthar and had been all session. That byte is an ANIMATION-state byte; DEVNOTES has said since v0.18.3.255 that it is "never authoritative for vehicle detection", and v0.20.56 added a CORROBORATION GATE requiring any non-foot claim to be seconded by the engine's in-motion vehicle id or by that vehicle's own savemap mirror being where the player is. **The gate was right and was simply not on the path that fired**: the entry-debounce snapshot has its own branch that returns before reaching it, and that branch assigned `s_lastVehicle = vehicle` outright. One noisy read, believed for the rest of the session. **The two consequences are the two failures.** POSITION: `GetWorldMapPosition_Active` repointed at the Balamb Garden mirror 70 km away at (20360,-3850), so the Tears' Point drive planned from Fisherman's Horizon — `dist=72125 units (72 km)` for a target 25 km off, `Fine path: 142 cells from fine(147,92)`. STEERING: `isOnFoot` in world_map_drive.inl comes from the same byte, and the entire camera-write executor lives behind `} else if (isOnFoot) {`. Every drive after 20:40:41 took the VEHICLE branch while he was on foot — no camera write, no closed-loop trim, four-way probe arrows against a camera nothing was steering. The world map's arrows are screen-relative and the camera follows the character, so that is a feedback loop, and **the 554 position samples in the log orbit (87900,6950) at radius ~1400 with the heading advancing a steady −32° per sample: one revolution every nine seconds for thirty-five seconds, until he cancelled.** Not a wedge against terrain — a circle. The `[CAMW]` trim lines stop at 20:39:49 and never return, which is that branch never being entered again. **THE OLD GUARD COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT EITHER, AND THAT IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF.** `GetWorldMapPosition_Active` already had a foot-motion override and it fired correctly at 20:40:58. Its rule was `footAlive = (now - lastFootMove) < 2000` — sound evidence when present, and **absent exactly when it is needed: the player stands still to press the drive key.** At 20:41:54 he had cancelled at :50 and pressed the catalog key at :51 and :53; four seconds without moving, window closed, override silent. **A two-second window on "did the player move" is a timer, not a discriminator.** NEW `src/world_map_locomotion.inl` replaces it with one latched verdict updated from evidence: foot DWORDs moved this tick → FOOT (definitive — the engine's integrator only runs them while the player IS the foot character); byte claims a vehicle AND is corroborated → VEHICLE; **neither → keep the last verdict**, because standing still is not information and treating it as information is the entire bug. The corroboration test is the v0.20.56 gate moved here whole, so the snapshot path, the commit path and the position source cannot drift apart. **CAUSE TWO: FIVE ESTHAR MARKERS THAT COULD NEVER HAVE OPENED ANYTHING.** The Lunar Gate drive was the one that worked — 31 km, `Entered final approach zone (dist=982)`, standing within 10 units of the catalog marker — and then `[TRIGWALK] tick seg=410 -- no entry program covers this square`. **Segment 410 has no entry program at all.** Checked against the shipped polygons, **all five Esthar markers stand on ZERO foot-walkable entry triangles; the five new aims each stand on exactly one.** The old coordinates were never measured — their digits give them away (…521/…021, …865/…135) — and three are not even in a segment that has a door. `WORLDMAP_ENTRY_POLYGONS.md` listed all five under "no foot-walkable entry polygon anywhere near them, which is correct — they are not walked into"; **that conclusion was wrong**, every one has a real patch, 3.7–12.1 km from its marker, which is further than that scan looked. Bound by the v0.21.7 authority — a patch sits in a SEGMENT, a segment has one PROGRAM, the program names its destinations: **Sorceress Memorial** (seg 441, prog 29, dest 30, 248 walkable entry tris of 248) and **Tears' Point** (seg 506, prog 32, dest 31, four bars around a hollow centre — the aim is the SOUTH bar, because the game's own arrival record sits 272 u due south of it) have their markers in the same segment as their patch, so those two bindings are facts of the same class as Deling City's. **Esthar City** is argued and strongly: segs 406/407/438/439 are a contiguous 2×2 block holding eight door patches in mirror pairs about the seam between them — one structure across four squares, which is why it needs four programs, and what a city with four gates looks like. **Lunatic Pandora Lab and Lunar Gate** are the pair that is not pinned by any single-segment fact, and four independent arguments agree; the one worth the ink is the FIELD NAMES — destination 28's fields are `edlabo*` and `edmoor*` (laboratory, and the mooring Lunatic Pandora sits in), destination 29's are `escont`/`escouse`/`esform`/**`esfreez`**, and the Lunar Gate is where you are sealed into a cryogenic capsule before launch. **If that pair is swapped one BAT says so and the fix is two lines** — the arrival line prints `fieldName`, and the geometry is right either way. All five programs are gated `story >= 1750` and Aaron is at 2000, so all five are live now. **THE ANNOUNCED DISTANCE NOW MEASURES TO THE DOOR.** The drive already retargeted to the entry aim, but the catalog readout and the drive's opening line measured to the marker — harmless while every aim sat within 800 units, and at 12 km it means the catalog says "Esthar City, 7 kilometres" and the drive then says "19 kilometres". For someone navigating entirely by those numbers that is two different answers to the same question, so both now measure to where the drive is actually going. The marker is unchanged and is still what the catalog is built from, what BFS filters on, and what arrival capture compares against. **THE OFFLINE GRID IS THE SHIPPED GRID, PROVEN SIX WAYS.** `offline/wmx.py` reproduces world_map_segments.inl's rasterisation step for step — same segment/block walk, same vertex frame, same first-non-ocean-wins gate, same steepness, same Dollet patch, same road overlay and override — and reproduces **every one of the six statistics the mod's own startup log prints: land 8311, forest 828, mountain 1960 (1372 steep-blocked), ocean 38053, walkable 9727, clearance max 11, wall-hugging 4580.** NEW `tests/world_map_route_test.cpp` plans over that grid with world_map_planner.inl's edge rule verbatim (4-neighbour, torus wrap, WM_CLIMB_STEP guard with the road exemption) and asserts eleven previously-working legs across Galbadia, Balamb and Centra still plan — Deling→Tomb, G-Garden→Dollet, Dollet→Timber, Timber→Deling, Balamb Town→Fire Cavern, Chocobo Forest 7→Edea's House and back, and the rest — plus all five Esthar retargets from both of Aaron's actual positions. **It also asserts the five DEAD markers are still walkable**, because the Esthar failure was an entry fault and not a routing one, and an edit that "fixes" it by making them unwalkable has misunderstood it. **THREE THINGS THE PROBES CAUGHT THAT REVIEW DID NOT.** (1) `LocoCorroborated` calls `IsFootLocomotion`, which was defined in world_catalog.inl — included AFTER world_map_locomotion.inl. **An MSVC-only build break**, invisible to every existing host probe, found because `catalog_story_test` compiles the real include order; `IsFootLocomotion` now lives in world_map_geometry.inl beside `IsCanonicalLocomotion`. ## v0.55.0

**v0.55.0 (#110 / #111 / #112 — THE THREE DISC-3 BLOCKERS, BUILT OFFLINE FROM THE SCRIPTS, AND THE FOUR THINGS THE PROBES ONLY CAUGHT AFTER THEY WERE MADE TO BITE).** Aaron has no save at any of these yet — *"I can test when I reach the scene, which will take a couple of hours play time on my end"* — so every claim below comes out of `FF8_EN.exe` and the shipped `.jsm`/`.msd` data, and every constant is pinned by a probe fixture EXTRACTED from those files rather than typed. **#110 ESTHAR, THE LUNATIC PANDORA RUN.** Odine's briefing (`emlabo2`, msgs 7-14) gives three contact points and a 20-minute clock; a sighted player then gets three PICTURES of the city and nothing else, which is why this is unplayable blind. `ecmview1 :: Timelimit::default` arms `SETTIMER 1201`, the engine holds it as a dword at `0x01CFE92C`, and all 21 minigame fields mirror it into **var[1024]** every frame. `eccway11 :: Disp::default` dwords 5405-5468 — byte-identical in all 21 — is the ladder that picks the target: **720 / 900 / 300 / 600 / 180**, which is the briefing's 15:00-12:00, 10:00-5:00, 3:00-0:00 in seconds, and the probe checks the two against each other. The mod now speaks the clock, which contact point is live, whether its window is open, **and which exit to take from where you are standing** — a 114-row next-hop table built by BFS over the pedestrian graph extracted from `field.fs`. It interrupts on a window opening and on a point lapsing, ticks the last five minutes, and answers `/` anywhere. Gated on **var[672] == 19**, so the same fields stay an ordinary city the rest of the game. **#111 THE SPACE RESCUE.** `ssspace3 :: rinoa::default` dwords 225-243 take the verdict exactly once, at the end of the approach: four tests of **var[1040] / var[1044] against 180**. So "centred" is the game's own win box, not a tolerance the mod picked, and everything after dword 243 — `var[1035]=1`, `var[256]=2564`, `MAPJUMPO 877` — is the game's own win path. The mod calls the direction once a second, rings the bgbtl tone the moment the box is entered or lost, and **F9 holds both variables at zero every tick** so the game declares its own win; nothing is forged and no transition is synthesised. **#112 THE PROPAGATORS.** All eight `alien0N::defalut` scripts read the same way: kill one, `var[445] |= 4` and `var[447]` remembers it; kill a NON-partner next and `var[446] &= ~var[447]` — **the first one gets up again**. The mod names the colour in front of you, the room its pair is in, and after every kill which one you are now allowed to kill; `/` repeats both. The game's own mercy is `var[437] > 24`. **MOVEMENT SUPPRESSION IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS BUILD**: `dic::defalut` mode 0 is a patrol with the touch-and-battle branch unreachable, but it covers only four of the eight rooms and has to be rewritten every frame, and a per-frame write into a script's own state in a scene nobody has ever run the mod in should follow a BAT rather than precede one. The reason is written into the file so it does not get lost. **FOUR DEFECTS THE PROBES FOUND ONLY AFTER BEING MUTATION-TESTED, WHICH IS THE REAL STORY OF THIS BUILD.** (1) `namespace Propagator` shadowed `struct Propagator`, so `const Propagator*` inside it named a namespace — a hard MSVC error that `lint_braces` cannot see and that no host probe had ever parsed, because nothing compiled the wiring layer at all. **NEW `tests/disc3_wiring_compile.cpp` compiles AND RUNS all three wiring files on the host, mmapping real pages at the game's own `0x01CFxxxx` addresses so the code reads and writes through the same `D3ReadU8`/`D3WriteI32` paths at the same addresses it uses in the game.** (2) **The space brief would have said "? and ? move you left and right."** `GardenBattle::CopyKeyName` has four slots and they are the Garden battle's four ACTION buttons; the D-pad bits are not in it, so it writes the literal `"?"` and never leaves the buffer empty — which is what the brief was written against. **The probe's stub was wrong in exactly the way that hid it**, the same shape as `button_map_rescue.inl`'s C2653: a stub is a statement about an interface, not evidence that the interface exists. The stub is now the real function's contract, the space module does not call it (every direction in this mod is the arrow keys), and the probe fails if ANY utterance anywhere contains a `?`. (3) `SrMaskForX(4000) == SR_MASK_RIGHT` was **the constant on both sides of its own test** — swapping SR_MASK_LEFT and SR_MASK_RIGHT left it passing. The mapping is now DERIVED by walking `director1::default`'s own nested `BTN_HELD` tree (dwords 1147-1321, extracted) down to the direction code each leaf writes to var[1024], which `rinoa::keyl/r/u/d` gate on as 1/2/3/4. **0x8000 = LEFT, 0x2000 = RIGHT, 0x1000 = UP, 0x4000 = DOWN, out of the game's own dispatch**, and both swaps now fail. Same for the Propagator table: `PG_PENDING_MASK 0x04 -> 0x08` survived BOTH probes, so the own-bit, partner-bit, pending mask, resurrection and mercy threshold are now read out of **two extracted windows from each of the eight scripts** and the pairing is checked to CLOSE as an involution covering 0xFF. (4) **The derived field ids were being trusted in the wrong direction.** Aaron has never stood in Esthar, the Ragnarok or space with the mod running, so those ids are derived, and a wrong derived RANGE does not fail silently — it fires somewhere else, and the failure mode is Propagator kill-counts announced in the middle of an unrelated scene for the rest of the game. **Esthar and the Propagators are now NAME-ONLY** (neither is reflex-timed; `pCurrentFieldName`'s 2-5 second lag costs nothing) and log the observed id, so one BAT settles the derivation either way. **Space keeps id-OR-name** because the steering and the skip cannot wait out that lag, and it is additionally fenced by a clamp check on both variables. The probe tests all four cases including an rg-range id under a foreign name **while var[445..447] churn underneath it**. **TWO DEAD GATES BROUGHT BACK, BOTH FOUND BY RUNNING THE WHOLE SUITE RATHER THAN THE FILES I TOUCHED.** `tests/garden_aboard_test.cpp` stopped compiling at v0.53.0 when `struct GardenDock` moved into `world_garden_inlets.inl`; it now includes it (13 checks, all pass). `tests/chase_harness.cpp` — the offline A* harness built for #113 — had stopped LINKING because `EdgeCrossesScreenBound` is forward-declared in `field_nav_pathfinding.inl` and was defined only in `field_navigation.cpp`, which no host probe can compile. Copying it into the harness would have created a second copy of the A* barrier rule that can drift from the shipped one, so **`Orient2D` / `SegmentsCross` / `EdgeCrossesScreenBound` move into NEW `src/field_nav_geometry.inl`** which both include, and the harness tests the code the game runs (CHASEGUARD: PASS). **`field_navigation.cpp` 81,827 -> 46,279 bytes** across the two extractions (`field_nav_state.inl` 34,022 for the 80 KB guard, then the geometry file), which is what made room for the three new modules in the first place. **⚠ ONE GATE IS STILL DOWN AND IS NOT FIXED HERE: `tests/catalog_harness.cpp` segfaults on the host** at `IsDrawPointLivePresent` (field_catalog.inl:2197), which reads the sparkle triple at `0x01CDC620`/`0x01CDBFEA`/`0x01CE0750`. In the mod those reads sit inside `__try` and fail OPEN; under g++ `__try` is `if (1)`, so it dies on the seventh of 33 fixtures and has done since v0.20.48 (#117). Mapping the pages makes it run all 33 — **and the dump then differs from `catalog_golden.txt` in ways that are NOT all explained by the draw-point gate** (a stray `idx=-200 Interaction 1` appears in most fixtures from `naming_paths` onward). That is either a real catalog regression hidden behind a dead gate or a stale golden, it wants its own build to settle, and regenerating the golden would silently bless whichever it is. **Verified: lint_braces / lint_freeze / lint_seh / lint_stub / lint_xtu all OK; size gate OK (largest non-exempt 81,711); 34 of 35 probes and harnesses compile and pass, catalog_harness excepted above; disc3_models_compile 0 bad and disc3_wiring_compile 0 bad, with 33 mutations applied across the model constants and the wiring logic and ALL 33 killed.** **BAT (three separate scenes, in story order, and each is worth its own log):** (1) **Esthar** — when the run starts expect "Lunatic Pandora run." then, on `/`, the clock, the contact point, open/closed, and a field to head for; grep `[ESTHAR]` for the per-field `hops=` / `next=` lines and for any `OUTSIDE the derived range` line, which is the id derivation reporting itself. Walking the route it names is the actual test. (2) **Space** — expect "Reaching Rinoa" and a direction once a second; the useful check is whether the words track the screen, so `[SPACE] x= y= -> ""` against what you hear is the whole thing. Then try **F9** and confirm the game itself completes the rescue. (3) **The Ragnarok** — expect the colour and its pair's room on entering each of the eight, and a status line after every kill; grep `[PROPAGATOR]` for `pair table consistent` on the first field and for the `dead=0x.. pendBit=0x..` line after each fight. **The monsters will still charge you — that part is not in this build on purpose.** If they make the rooms impassable, the log will show which fields and the `dic` mode pin is four lines on top of a scene that has then actually been walked.

## v0.54.0

#109: **The White SeeD Ship, measured — and the 773 units that made two
correct-looking markers fail.**

The v0.53.1 inlet sweep found it on its ninth leg. Crossing from inlet 7 to
inlet 8, the world map handed off:

```
[GARDEN] moving to dock site 8, approach (-20160,49600)
[GROUNDH] pos(-17911,46995)
WorldMap: Exited world map
[GARDEN] stopped: Docked at White SeeD Ship.
[DRIVE] Manual world-map exit -- lastPos=(-17974,47006)
[fieldload] id=853 name='sefront1'
```

Field 853 `se\sefront1` is the White SeeD Ship's deck. **The boarding point is
`(-17974, 47006)`** — the hull's position on the frame the transition fired, so
it is inside the zone by construction rather than by inference.

### And it explains both failures

wmsetus record 17, `(-17350, 46550)`, is **773 units** from it. Close enough
that the record really was the ship's marker — the only sea-level ocean record
in the whole location-marker table, exactly as v0.51.0 argued — and far enough
to miss.

**The reason 773 was fatal is the shape of the approach, not the size of the
error.** Park and dock were the *same* coordinate, so the hull arrived on the
mark, the bearing to the dock became noise, and the nose-in's lateral sweep —
±384, ±768, ±1152, which would otherwise have covered 773 — went in no
particular direction. Two BATs of the hull sitting on a mark, pressing at
itself.

The approach is now a **separate point 1,100 units due east**, which is the
heading the hull was travelling when it worked. It drives west *through* the
boarding point instead of stopping on it, and site 0 gets a full seven-phase
press rather than the two-phase search stop.

### What is kept

The 41-inlet sweep stays behind it as sites 1–41. It is what found the ship,
and it costs nothing until the known point misses. If it ever runs, the log
says so and something above it is wrong.

### The marker also repairs the entry capture

v0.53.1 refused to record the coordinate it had just found:

```
[DRIVE] Manual field entry at (-17974,47006) -- nearest location
        White SeeD Ship is 19182u away (> 3000), not capturing
```

because the marker was still the first sweep inlet. With the marker on the
boarding point, a future capture lands inside its own window.

### Checked before shipping

Against the real grid: 42 of 42 sites reachable and plannable; the
approach→boarding-point line is Garden water end to end; and 12 `gexec3` routes
from three starts arrive at the approach with **zero replans**.

The probes pin the 773 and refuse `park == dock`, so neither failure can come
back quietly — both mutations were re-introduced and both fail.

## v0.53.1

#109: **A stray brace, and the reason nothing caught it.**

v0.52.0 added four lines to `world_map_segments.inl` and left a `}` behind that
closes nothing:

```c
    WmDumpWorldmapSlots();
    }                          <- closes nothing
```

MSVC reported it as `error C2059: syntax error: 'for'` sixty lines later, then
twenty more errors after that. The brace is gone.

### The reason it got out is the part worth fixing

**No host probe compiles `world_map_segments.inl`.** The garden harness
compiles the garden files, `catalog_story_test` compiles `world_catalog.inl`,
and every other file in the world-map set is built only by MSVC. For those
files the first syntax check in the loop was the BAT — the most expensive place
in the loop to put one.

`tests/lint_braces.py` is the cheap check that catches the whole class: strip
comments and string literals, then count braces and parentheses per file. A
complete translation unit or textual include must come out at zero, and 232 of
232 source files do.

One declared exception, checked as a **pair**: `world_map_drive.inl` opens a
function that `world_map_drive_exec.inl` closes, a split made for the 80 KB
guard. The pair must still balance together, so a stray brace in either half is
still caught.

Re-introducing the exact v0.52.0 brace makes the lint fail — which is how I know
it would have caught this one rather than merely that it runs.

## v0.53.0

#109: **The coordinate is not in the shipped data, so the Garden searches for
it the way the game asks a sighted player to.**

Aaron got Edea's letter — the dialog log has her saying *"they may have
stationed their ship by an inlet somewhere on the Centra continent"* and
handing it over — and drove again. `dist to press point 11`. The F11
screenshot is the same empty inlet.

### wmsetus record 17 is not the ship

v0.51.0 shipped it on the strength of being the only sea-level ocean record in
the location-marker table, sitting in a bay that matched every walkthrough's
description. Two BATs killed it, the second with the prerequisite provably met.

### And it is not findable statically

Worth writing down so nobody spends another day on it:

- **No entry polygon.** The flag `sub_545EA0` tests — byte `0x0E` bit 3 — is not
  set on any polygon within twelve kilometres of that bay. Boarding is not a
  terrain trigger.
- **Not in the trigger table.** None of the 38 programs in wmsetus section 7
  targets a field id in 775–784, the `se\` set.
- **No savemap record.** The WORLDMAP struct's four unnamed position slots are
  empty in all 41 saves and in all three disc-3 saves.
- **Not a constant anywhere.** Neither `wmsetus.obj`, `wmset.obj` nor
  `FF8_EN.exe` contains the coordinate of **Mobile Galbadia Garden** either —
  and that one is *known*, pinned by a BAT. Scripted world-map event zones are
  simply not stored where static analysis can reach them.

### So do what the game tells the player to do

Edea gives no coordinate. The guides say *"sail around, around and around until
you find the ship"*, *"look around all the jagged rocks"*, *"make 360 turns and
check every corner"*. **That instruction is useless to a blind player, and
automating it is the accessibility fix.**

Choosing the White SeeD Ship now runs a **sweep** of every enclosed water
pocket in Centra. A water cell qualifies when land blocks at least 14 of 16
rays cast 2,560 units out — which is what "an inlet" means as a shape. Pockets
under six cells are dropped as noise, each pocket contributes its single most
enclosed cell, and only cells the Garden can actually reach survive, from one
flood under the planner's own rules. That leaves **forty-one**, ordered by
distance from Edea's House because every account starts there: *"start out at
the orphanage and go north"*.

The sweep reuses machinery that already exists — the nose-in's *"another place
the hull can touch? go there rather than reporting failure"* path — pointed at
a list instead of at a guess. Each stop is two phases rather than seven,
because the question at a search stop is only *is it here?*, and it announces
*"Inlet 7 of 41."* as it goes.

**It ends the moment a field loads**, and the mod's entry capture then records
the real coordinate — so this stops being a search at all on the second visit.

### What the harness checks

Against the real grid built from the real `wmx.obj`: all 41 inlets reachable
*and* plannable from the Garden's position in the current save;
`Garden_DockSite` walks the list and ends; Trabia Garden's own dock row still
resolves behind the new branch; and a sweep stop is fewer phases than a dock
attempt.

### Headroom

`world_garden.inl` came back to 79,866 bytes by moving four helpers into the
new `world_garden_inlets.inl`. `world_map_segments.inl` is still only 456 bytes
under the gate.

## v0.52.0

#109: **The navigation was right, the bay was empty, and the mod spent ninety
seconds searching the shore of open water.**

The v0.51.0 coordinate holds up. The Garden drove 28 km from Edea's House to
`(-17350, 46550)` in 28 seconds with **zero replans**, nosed in through all
seven phases, and then:

```
[GARDEN] patrol trace (-17353,46554) hd=3582 dist to White SeeD Ship 5
[GARDEN] patrol trace (-17354,46547) hd=4047 dist to White SeeD Ship 5
   ... ninety seconds of this ...
[GARDEN] patrol of White SeeD Ship exhausted at (-17355,46549)
[GARDEN] stopped: Balamb Garden could not dock at White SeeD Ship.
```

Five units from the mark. **The ship is not there** — and the F11 screenshot
proves it: Balamb Garden floating in a narrow cliff-walled inlet, the *"little
bay surrounded by mountainous terrain"* the walkthroughs describe, with no ship
in the frame.

### The prerequisite is Edea

rpgclassics, on disc 3: *"Travel to Edea's house and get her hint on where the
ship of the White SeeDs is — **you will not find it unless you talk to her
first**."* The story word reads 1350 and the ship has not been placed. No
amount of driving fixes that.

Three things change, none of them a guess.

### (1) A shoreline patrol needs a shoreline

The patrol hugs whatever blocks the bow. On open water nothing does, so it
aimed at a dock point it was already sitting on and turned on the spot — the
trace is ninety seconds of the heading walking 0..4095 while the position moves
ten units. That is not a search, it is a wait with the engine running.

A dock point on water now gets the nose-in and nothing after it. The failure
goes from about two and a half minutes to about one.

### (2) The failure says what is actually wrong

*"Balamb Garden could not dock"* reads as a navigation failure, and navigation
is the one thing that worked. When the press point is afloat the hull has
already been everywhere it can be, so the message now says the spot is right
and the thing is not there — and, for the White SeeD Ship where the player can
act on it, names the prerequisite:

> *"Balamb Garden is right on the spot for White SeeD Ship and nothing is
> there. The ship does not appear until Edea tells you where it is. Go to
> Edea's House and talk to her first, then come back."*

### (3) All eight WORLDMAP slots are dumped

The struct is eight 12-byte position records at savemap `+0x125C` and only four
have ever been identified — char, ragnarok, bgu, car. The other four are empty
across all 41 saves and, re-checked for this, in the three disc-3 saves too.

Which one the ship is decides the whole design. If it is an **object with a
live position**, one of these goes live the moment it appears and the
destination should read it the way Mobile Balamb Garden reads `bgu_pos` — which
would also survive the ship moving. If they all stay zero, the gate is a story
value and the destination should be hidden until it passes.

Eight log lines on every world-map entry settle it, and they cost nothing to be
wrong about. New file `world_map_wmslots.inl`: `world_map_segments.inl` was 643
bytes under the 80 KB gate and this did not fit.

### Still tight

`world_garden.inl` is 599 bytes under the gate and `world_map_segments.inl` is
456. The next change to either needs a split first.

## v0.51.0

#109: **The White SeeD Ship was the Centra Ruins moved by a round number — and
it is not a place you walk to.**

*"Auto-drive failed to get there."* The log:

```
[NAVMESH]  White SeeD Ship  (4887,51285) tri#90376 terr=7 not reachable
[GARDEN]   parked (arrived) at (2899,53093) walk=2687 to White SeeD Ship
[GARDEN]   stopped: ... White SeeD Ship is 27 hundred units north-east.
           Leave the Garden and press backslash to walk the rest.
```

There is nothing there.

### The coordinate was never measured

`(4887, 51285)` is the Centra Ruins marker `(6887, 55285)` minus exactly
`(2000, 4000)`. A nudge, not a measurement. `WORLDMAP_CATALOG_STORY_WINDOWS.md`
had already flagged it — *"the coordinate came from the original research
document and has never been driven to"* — and the coordinate audit measured it
as 4.5 km from any wmsetus record. It is 4,205 units, and it put the ship
inland on terrain 7, on a foot landmass the player cannot reach.

### The real one is wmsetus.obj section 8, record 17

That section is the location-marker table this catalog was built from: 12-byte
records of `int32 X, int32 Y, int16 Z` at file offset 5580.

**Record 17 is `(-17350, 46550)`, Z = 0** — the only record in the whole table
that sits at sea level on deep ocean (terrain 33). A ship floats at zero.

No polygon within 2,600 units carries the foot entry flag (byte `0x0E` bit 3),
and byte `0x0F` reads `0x30`: the Garden mask set, foot clear. It cannot be
walked to at all.

The walkthroughs agree with the data on both counts. Position: *"a small,
U-shaped island north and slightly east of Edea's House"*, *"in a little bay
surrounded by mountainous terrain"* — record 17 is 22,908 north and 12,075 east
of Edea's House, in exactly that bay. Method: *"run into it to board the White
SeeD ship."*

### So it is a drive-in

Like Fisherman's Horizon and Mobile Galbadia Garden: park **is** the marker,
walk 0, and arrival hands over to the nose-in that already exists — which
presses straight at the target with the wall guard off, because there grinding
into the thing is the objective.

### Verified offline before shipping, by two independent models

The **real C++ grid and planner**, built in `tests/garden_harness.cpp` from the
real `wmx.obj`, reach it from four starts — including the exact Garden position
in the current save and both starts from the failed BAT. Sixteen `gexec3`
executor routes (four starts × four headings) arrive with **zero replans**,
260–287 units out, inside `GD_ARRIVE_DIST`. The two models agree on the
waypoint counts to within one.

### The probes read the coordinate out of the game file

`tests/catalog_story_test.cpp` carries wmsetus records 14–21 verbatim and pins
the table's base offset and 12-byte stride on four anchors the mod already
ships and Aaron has driven to — Winhill, Centra Ruins, Edea's House, Shumi
Village — *before* reading record 17. Get the stride wrong and the anchors fail
first. It also asserts the berth is a drive-in on the marker with no walk, and
that Fisherman's Horizon still stands off its own marker, so "park == marker"
stays a property of this berth rather than of drive-ins in general.

#108: **The silence beat.** And #105: the skip that still rang the bell.

The v0.49.0 BAT was clean. The refine picker read `id=0 "Laguna"`,

### (1) A dialogue window that reached the player as nothing at all

In `bghoke_2`, Squall says *"Rinoa... Call my name."* and the reply window holds
`(......)`:

```
[RAMESW] win[1] REJECTED garbled: "(......)"
```

Eight characters, zero letters, so `IsGarbledText`'s `letterPct < 30` rule
fired — the right rule for a stale tutorial buffer, the wrong one for a
deliberate pause. The short form was no better off: `...` is three characters,
under the `len < 8` floor, so it went to the screen reader unchanged, and a
screen reader reads punctuation-only text as silence at default settings.
Either way a dialogue window arrived with no announcement and no reason to know
a confirm press was waiting.

Every dots-only message now speaks as **"Ellipsis."** and is exempt from the
garbled filter.

**The fixture is the population, not a sample.** Every message in the 883 field
`.msd` files was decoded through the sysfnt glyph table (`0x10` is the `...`
glyph, `0x18`/`0x19` the parentheses). All forty-nine dots-only messages — five
distinct forms — are listed in `tests/dialog_ellipsis_compile.cpp` with their
counts:

| form | occurrences |
|---|---|
| `...` | 40 |
| `(......)` | 6 |
| `(.........)` | 1 |
| `(............)` | 1 |
| `..................` | 1 |

A line carrying any letter or digit is untouched, so *"Well..."* and
*"...I don't know."* keep their own words, and the canonical garbage sample
still fails the filter.

22:50:14  "Blocked."

A wind-up tone instructing the player to do something that cannot matter,

## v0.48.0

#105: **A recovery names its own attack, and a block is not announced into the
next one.**

v0.47.0 held. In the 2026-08-21 log every cue resolved, there was no `hit with
no cue outstanding` and no expiry, and Aaron won the fight on round 3. Two
defects sat underneath it, and both came from the same cause: **the two attack
scripts overlap, and v0.47.0 paired recoveries to cues by age.**

**(1) The round Laguna lost.**

```
21:41:38  ATTACK (quick) ip=531   attack cue QUICK
21:41:39  recovery ip=545          <- the FIRST attack's full stop
21:41:40  ATTACK (quick) ip=531   attack cue QUICK   <- the next wind-up rings
21:41:40  "Blocked."               <- the FIRST attack's outcome, one beat late
21:41:41  recovery ip=545
21:41:41  hit 890 ms after the cue / "Hit. Laguna down."
```

The block was real. The problem is when it was said. *"Blocked."* is heard as
*you can let go now*, and it arrived one second after the next wind-up had
already been cued — so the guard came down into a live attack, and the next
line in the log is Laguna going down. A block whose cue has been superseded is
now **held silent** and logged instead: there is nothing safe to say about it
while the player still has to keep holding, and the newer cue speaks for both.

**(2) Both outcomes charged to the wrong cue at once.**

```
21:42:00  ATTACK ip=531           attack cue
21:42:03  ATTACK (quick) ip=605   attack cue QUICK
21:42:04  recovery ip=619   ->  hit 3969 ms after the cue    <- charged to :00
21:42:16  recovery ip=545   ->  "Blocked."                   <- charged to :03
```

`ip=619` is `dragon::kougeki`'s recovery and belongs to the `:03` cue; `ip=545`
is `dragon::default`'s and belongs to the `:00` one. Oldest-first swapped them.
The outcomes happened to read plausibly, but `3969 ms` is the tell — nothing in
this fight takes four seconds unless something else was measured.

**The script already says which is which.** Both attack routines have the same
shape — `ANIME(47,1)`, block check, damage REQ, `ANIME(98,48)` — and the two
animations sit exactly **fourteen dwords apart in both of them**:
`dragon::default` 671 and 685, `dragon::kougeki` 745 and 759, runtime 531/545
and 605/619. A recovery now matches the cue whose instruction pointer is that
far in front of it. The gap is a property of the script rather than of the load
address, so it holds wherever the field loads. A recovery whose gap names no
cue falls back to oldest-first **and says so in the log**, because a signature
change must not look like working code.

The health drop follows the recovery to the same cue rather than to the oldest,
since the damage REQ runs immediately after the block check.

**The cue queue moved into the pure model.** It is the part that has now been
wrong three releases running, so `tests/dragon_fight_compile.cpp` replays both
of the log sequences above through the real code, and the fourteen is read out
of the `dragon::default` script fixture rather than copied off a log — bump the
constant by one and eight assertions fail.

**Two items from v0.45.0 closed by this run.** The Magic menu diagnostic reads
`char=0 modelId=8 -> "Laguna"`, `char=2 modelId=9 -> "Kiros"` and
`char=5 modelId=10 -> "Ward"`, and the battle magic list indexes Kiros at
charIdx 2 and Ward at charIdx 5 — the dream party, not the stale formation. The
Laguna Switch screen ran clean end to end.

## v0.47.0

#105: **The wind-up is interruptible, so a deadline cannot judge it.**

The v0.46.0 fixes held — the retry announced itself as *"Round 2. Both back to
full"* and kept cueing all the way through both rounds. The log exposed the last
defect underneath them: **"Blocked." one second before "Hit."**

```
21:13:11  ip=531 ch=2 (47,1) speed=32   ATTACK (quick)   the attack starts
21:13:12  ip=638 ch=5 (42,1)            dragon::damage — Laguna hit it,
21:13:13  ip=717 ch=5 (85,43)             preempting the wind-up
21:13:14  "Blocked."                    FALSE — the 2600 ms deadline fired
21:13:15  ip=545 ch=2 (98,48)           the real end of the attack
21:13:15  **hit with no cue outstanding**
21:13:15  "Hit. Laguna, 2 hits left."
```

A quick attack that should have resolved in 828 ms took nearly four seconds,
because the player hit the dragon during it and `dragon::damage` — a priority-5
script — suspended the wind-up. The fixed deadline then announced a block that
never happened, consumed the cue, and left the real hit with nothing to pair
with. It happened three times in this run, always in the same shape: an attack
cue, a *"Dragon, N hits left"* in the middle of it, then the false block.

**The attack has its own full stop.** Both attack scripts end the same way —
block check, damage REQ, then `ANIME(98, 48)` on the same channel 2
(`dragon::default` dword 685, `dragon::kougeki` dword 759, and nothing else in
the field uses that pair). It starts at the instant the check has been made, so
it is exact and, unlike a timer, it cannot be wrong about an attack that was
interrupted.

So the outcome is decided by the recovery and never by a deadline, plus **one
bounded beat** for the damage script to run: `laguna::damage` is REQ'd at
priority 6, not called inline, so the health drop lands just after the recovery
starts — inside the same second in the log. A cue whose recovery never arrives
expires **silently** after fifteen seconds, because by then nothing true can be
said about it.

The probe locates the recovery in the same routine *after* the attack rather
than trusting the pair, so a wrong animation or speed fails it, and the backstop
has to clear twice the longest wind-up.

The all-channels animation trace is also **narrowed to channel 2**. It cost two
hundred log lines a fight and it earned every one of them — it found the attack's
two call sites, the speed byte behind the quick attack, and now the recovery —
but both questions are answered, so the noise goes and the gate stays.

Everything else in the run was clean: both rounds cued, both speeds cued, the
grace covered the attack that was in flight at the restart, the skip and the key
names behaved, and no channel logged an exception. (`FFNx=FAIL` in the battle
banner and `MH_ERROR_ALREADY_INITIALIZED` in the mod log are both long-standing
and unrelated.)

All twenty-three gates.

#105: **The Game Controls box could hang the fight, and did.**

Aaron: *"Dragon battle glitched though, after I lost the first time I no longer
heard any sound cues."*

The log diagnoses itself. Laguna goes down at `20:51:48`, the retry re-opens the
Game Controls box at `20:51:58`, two keys get named at `:58` and `20:52:00` —

The box pins `var[1028]` and `return`s before the ring drain, so while it is up
the fight runs on with nothing able to hurt Laguna and not one cue announced.
It was waiting for Enter, which a player who has just died has no reason to

Three changes, and only one of them is the timeout:

* **The box opens once per visit.** A restart says *"Round 2. Both back to full.
  Hold A to block, tap W to attack."* and takes no key at all.
* **F9 closes it too.** A player who has decided to skip the fight has by

### The missing quick attack was never a missing signature

v0.45.0's per-animation log settles it. The hook catches the attack at **two**
instruction pointers, `531` and `605` — seventy-four dwords apart, which is
exactly the gap between `dragon::default`'s `ANIME` (offline dword 671) and
`dragon::kougeki`'s (745). Both scripts attack, and the hook sees both:

```
20:51:44  anime ip=531 ch=2 (47,1) speed=16  ATTACK
20:51:48  anime ip=531 ch=2 (47,1) speed=32  ATTACK (quick)
20:51:48  attack cue QUICK
20:51:48  hit 828 ms after the cue
```

So the quick attack cues, the slow one cues, and the 828 / 1610 ms pair is the
same animation at the two speeds `[ctx+0x208]` carries. **Every cue that went
missing was one the briefing had swallowed** — either dropped at close, or never
drained because the box was still up. Both are fixed above; there was no third
attack to find.

The probe now pins both constants: a briefing with no timeout fails it, and a
grace shorter than the longest measured wind-up fails it.

## v0.45.0

#104 / #105 / #106: **The second cursor is a third byte, every animation is
logged, and a dream battle was reading the wrong character's spells.**

---

### The Switch screen: `+0x43` is a mode, and the cursor is `+0x31`

v0.44.0 fixed the wrong half of this. `+0x43` is not a flag with two states, it
is a **mode with three**:

```
1  browsing         +0x32 focus, +0x34 grid, +0x35 slot
2  CHOOSING A SLOT  the cursor is +0x31, and the browse trio freezes
3  the +0x2e != 0 variant, +0x33 / +0x36 / +0x37
```

State 3's `0x40` branch (`0x004E8E96`) checks `+0x2e` — **which the creator
writes as zero** — so this screen always takes the state-6 path. State 6
(`0x004E9342`) sets `+0x43 = 2` and hands to state 7, whose entire body walks
`+0x31` up and down the slot mask through `0x004ABCA0` / `0x004ABCD0`, writing it
back at `0x004E9378` and `0x004E9399`. v0.44.0 watched for mode 3, which this
screen never produces, so it stayed silent for the second time running.

The swap at `0x004E94E8` names both ends in six instructions and is the proof:

```
8A 46 32     mov al, [esi+0x32]       the FROZEN focus
8A 46 31     mov al, [esi+0x31]       the DESTINATION slot
8A 56 34     mov dl, [esi+0x34]       the FROZEN grid cursor
8A 54 32 3B  mov dl, [edx+esi+0x3B]   the character in hand
8D 4C 30 38  lea ecx, [eax+esi+0x38]  &slots[destination]
```

So the reader now announces the **destination** while a pick is in hand — the
slot under the second cursor, who is in it, and who would come back the other
way, because this is a swap and not a placement. The probe decodes the state-6
mode write, the state-7 cursor, the `E8 rel32` that proves the walk really is
the mask walker, and all five instructions of the swap.

---

### The dragon logs every animation it starts

Aaron: *"The audio cue only seems to show up with some attacks… I think one
attack, the one we flag now, is a longer rearing-up attack, while the one we are
missing is a quick attack."*

The log has a hit with nothing in front of it, and there is no honest way to tell
a missed hook from a signature the model does not know without seeing what the
dragon actually started. So the hook now records **every** first-execution
animation on this field — channel, both arguments, the instruction pointer, and
`[ctx+0x208]` — and Update logs each one, marking the ones it cues on.

`[ctx+0x208]` is the byte opcode `0xE7` writes: its handler (`0x005264A0`) is
four instructions, pop one word and store it there. `dragon::default` writes
**32** before a third of its attacks and **16** after every one, so *the quick
attack is the same `ANIME(47,1)` at double speed* — which is exactly the
**828 ms / 1610 ms** pair the cue-to-hit measurements fall into. If the missing
attack is that one, the log now says `ATTACK (quick)` next to it; if it is
something else, the log names its channel and arguments.

Two things fixed along the way:

* **The tone is no longer gated on the health bytes.** v0.44.0 consumed the cue
  and then dropped it silently when `ready` was false. A cue the player does not
  get is worse than one that arrives a beat early.
* **Each cue carries its own deadline.** `dragon::default` and the REQ'd
  `dragon::kougeki` both swing, so attacks overlap, and one pending slot lost the
  first outcome every time a second cue arrived. A hit that arrives with nothing
  outstanding now says so in the log.

---

### #106 — a dream battle was building another character's magic list

Aaron: *"I rearranged Ward's magic but the rearrangement wasn't properly
reflected in the battle menu, resulting in my casting spells which I did not
intend."*

`GetBattleCharName` has known since **v0.17.8.17.2** that
`SAVEMAP_PARTY_FORMATION` is stale in a dream battle — its own comment records
the array reading `[05 00 01]` (Selphie/Squall/Zell) while the live actors were
Ward, Laguna and Kiros — and works around it with the actor-kind byte at
compStats `+0x1C3`. But `BuildMagicList`, `BuildGFList` and
`BuildCharCommandList` all index the savemap character array **through that same
stale byte**, so in a dream they can build another character's list. The cursor
position the player hears then has nothing to do with the spell that gets cast,
which is exactly what Aaron describes.

The bridge between the two is the character record's **model byte at `+0x08`**.
The menu side already trusts it — `menu_tts_junction.inl` logs `roster[0]=5
modelId=9` and names that character Kiros — so during a dream the savemap array
holds the dream members with their models set to 8, 9, 10. Given the actor kind,
the character is the record whose model matches.

**Normal battles are untouched.** Actor kinds there are 0–7, so the override
never fires and the formation byte is used exactly as before; in a dream where
the formation already agrees, the search returns the same index. It differs only
where the two disagree, which is the bug.

The party-name half of Aaron's report (*"when exchanging magic it showed Squall,
Irvine, Selphie"*) is **not** fixed here, because it cannot yet be located: the
Magic reader's own name resolver is already dream-aware and the junction reader
demonstrably resolves the same characters correctly. It now logs
`char=N modelId=M -> "name"` once per pair, so the next dream log says whether
the model bytes were wrong at that moment or the names came from a path that
never calls it.

All twenty-three gates.

## v0.44.0

#104 / #105: **The second cursor, and the dragon gets a controls screen.**

The first BAT of both screens. Three reports, and the first one turned out to be
a misreading of the module rather than a missing announcement.

---

### The Switch screen has two cursors, and v0.43.0 read the wrong one

Aaron: *"The second cursor on the Switch screen did not announce as it should."*

State 4 — `0x004E8F88`, the instant a pick is lifted — is four instructions, and
they are the whole story:

```
8A 4E 32        mov cl, [esi+0x32]        the live focus
8A 56 34        mov dl, [esi+0x34]        the live grid cursor
8A 46 35        mov al, [esi+0x35]        the live slot cursor
C6 46 43 03     mov byte [esi+0x43], 3
88 4E 33        mov [esi+0x33], cl        COPIED into the second trio
88 56 36        mov [esi+0x36], dl
88 46 37        mov [esi+0x37], al
66 C7 46 10 05  state = 5
```

and state 5 (`0x004E8FA4`) then reads the focus from **`+0x33`**, moves
**`+0x36`** with the same row*4+column arithmetic and **`+0x37`** through the
slot mask, writing them back at `0x004E9066` and `0x004E9099`. The first trio
never moves again until the pick is put down. The draw agrees: `0x004EA284`
tests `+0x43 == 3` and takes the second cursor from those same three bytes.

So the **first** trio is *what is in your hand* and the **second** is *where you
are* — and v0.43.0 had it exactly backwards. It named the pick correctly on the
lift (the two are equal for that one frame) and then went silent for the entire
second half of every placement, which is what the BAT heard.

Both halves are fixed and both are now tested: a pick carried down the slot
column, and a pick carried around the grid (which is how two party members are
swapped with each other). Mutating either offset, or reverting the live-cursor
choice, fails the probe 2–3 ways.

---

### The dragon fight: the keys, a Game Controls screen, and F9

Aaron: *"it did not announce the keys to hit. We also should implement a game
controls screen and skip functionality to this mini-game just like we did the
punch mini-game."*

**The keys.** The names come from the Garden battle's own learner, reading the
same button word (`0x01CE48B0`) this fight reads — masks `0x80` and `0x10` are
two of the four it already learns, so there was nothing to build. The briefing
now says the player's actual keys instead of "the block key".

**Game Controls.** Opens when **both bars read 120** — what `dic::defalut`
writes to start the fight and `laguna::damage` writes again on a retry — names
each key as it is pressed, and waits for Enter. Enter must be seen **up** first,
which is the lesson the Garden battle's retry briefing paid for in v0.20.121:
its box was being dismissed by the keypress that opened it.

**F9.** Pins the guard and sets the dragon to **one hit** from defeat, so the
game's own win path — the `var[1032] == 0` branch inside `dragon::damage` — ends
the scene on the next swing. Nothing is forged and no jump is invented; the
scene ends the way it always does, one hit sooner.

Both the briefing and the skip hold the fight with **`var[1028]`** — the guard
flag `laguna::bougyo` writes every frame the block key is down. That is the only
byte this module writes. In particular **no health is written**, which is the
mistake the Garden battle's first skip made in v0.20.120: zero HP is a lethal
value however briefly it is held.

---

### Three bugs the log caught

The 2026-08-21 field log is worth reading; it caught all three without a
screenshot.

1. **The cue rang 47 seconds before the fight** — `attack cue (laguna=0
   dragon=0)` during the cutscene. Gated now on the fight being real.
2. **`laguna=216 dragon=0`** sat in the health bytes before the scene wrote
   120/120, v0.43.0 took the 216 as a starting point, and then reported the drop
   to 120 as **"Hit. Laguna, 3 hits left."** 216 is not a health value; a byte
   the fight has not set up yet is not a health byte.
3. **The blocked/hit deadline was a guess, and the log measured the truth.**
   Cue to hit is **828 ms or 1610 ms** — two clusters, the short and the long
   wind-up — against a 2000 ms deadline, so a long wind-up could be announced as
   blocked and then land. It is 2600 ms now, and the probe fails if that ever
   drops back under the measurement.

That measurement also settles a question v0.43.0 left open: the warning here is
long enough for speech, unlike the Garden battle's 133 ms. The tone stays
anyway — the useful signal is "hold it now", and a rising pair says that in
180 ms without talking over the fight.

All twenty-three gates.

#104 / #105: **The Laguna junction-party screen, and the dragon fight.**

Two blockers in the Laguna sequence that opens shortly after disc 3.

### #104 — the junction screen is not the Switch Member UI

Aaron: *"A specialized Switch screen appears where you select the party members
whose junctions you want swapped to Laguna, Kiros, and Ward. Laguna is preset to
Squall and can't be changed. This Switch screen currently reads nothing out."*

It reads nothing because it is **a different menu module**, and the chain from
the field script to it is short enough to walk end to end:

```
bghoke_2 (B-Garden Infirmary), dwords 262-273:
    0x08C(8) 0x08C(9) 0x08D(10)   flag Laguna, Kiros, Ward as present
    PSHN_L 3 / OP_0x109           <- opens the screen
    PSHN_L 946 / 0 / MAPJUMPO     then jump to tvglen1, the dream

0x0051EFB0  (opcode 0x109)   [0x01CE4760] = 5
                             [0x01CE4762] = 0x16      <- the menu id
                             [0x01CE490B] = gameObj[0x68] & 7
0x00470DA6  copies both into [0x01D2BB98] / [0x00B87798]
0x004B3161  lea ecx,[eax-1] / cmp ecx,0x1C / mov dl,[ecx+0x4B32E8]
            / jmp [edx*4+0x4B32B0]      menu id 0x16 -> 0x004B3190
0x004B3190  mov [0x01D75599], al        <- THE SLOT MASK
            push 0x0D                   <- the screen id
0x004BDB30  screen id -> pair table 0x00B87ED8, pair 13 = creator 0x004E8A30
```

Pair **10** of that table is `0x004CB850`, the Switch Member UI
`menu_tts_switch.inl` already reads. Pair **13** is a different function
entirely, which is exactly why the existing reader was silent here.

The module is found by walking the same ten-slot pool `menu_tts_magic.inl`
walks (`0x01D76BC8`, stride `0x78`, MRU head `0x01D76B48`, update fn at `+0x08`)
for the one whose update function is `0x004E8B50`. **No game-mode gate** — this
screen is opened from a field script and never enters menu mode 6, which is the
other reason nothing in the mod could see it.

Every offset is decoded out of the creator and the state machine:

| field | what |
|---|---|
| `+0x24` | mask of pickable characters (savemap char `+0x94` bit 3) |
| `+0x32` | focus: 0 = the left character grid, 1 = the right slot column |
| `+0x34` | grid cursor, **row*4 + column**, into `+0x3B[8]` (`0xFF` = empty cell) |
| `+0x35` | slot cursor, a **bit index** walked through the slot mask |
| `+0x38..0x3A` | the three assignments (`0xFF` = empty) |
| `+0x43` | 3 = one end of a swap is held |

**`mov byte ptr [esi+0x38], 0` in the creator is "Laguna is preset to Squall"** —
not an inference, a literal in the shipped code.

`[0x01D75599]` — the byte the field script's parameter became — is the **slot
mask**: `0x004B2DB0` is nothing but `mov al,[0x01D75599] / ret`, and both the
state machine and the draw loop use it to decide which slots exist. That is how
a dream with no Ward is expressed, so the reader takes the slot list from the
mask rather than assuming three.

What it says: the board on arrival, then who is under the cursor as it moves —
and on the left grid, **who that person is already lending to**, because the
whole task is dividing eight people between two or three slots and a conflict is
invisible otherwise. Assignments are read out as the slots that changed, not as
"swapped", since a swap moves two at once. `/` reads the whole board back.

---

### #105 — the dragon fight

Field **`tvglen3`** (Trabia Canyon, the movie shoot), and its `.sym` names every
part of it in romaji: `laguna` has **kougeki** (attack), **bougyo** (defend),
**damage** and **taiki** (standby); `dragon` has **kougeki**, **damage** and
**gaoo** (roar); and a referee entity called **hantei** (judgement) owns the
input loop, which is four instructions:

```
PSHN_L 0x80 / BTNTEST(0x6D)  -> REQ laguna::bougyo    a LEVEL  -- hold
PSHN_L 0x10 / BTNTEST(0x6E)  -> REQ laguna::kougeki   an EDGE  -- tap
```

Same two masks as the Garden battle. The health is `var[1031]` for Laguna (120,
minus 40 a hit — **three hits**) and `var[1032]` for the dragon (120, minus 12 —
**ten**), and `OP_0x13B(gauge, value)` is what draws the two bars.

**The cue.** `dragon::default` is the entire fight in thirty dwords: roll a
random, wait, then `ANIME(47, 1)` on channel 2, and **read the block flag after
it**. Opcode `0x30`'s handler (`0x00526810`) returns 1 on its first execution —
bit 1 clear, so the dispatcher does not advance the instruction pointer — and 3
only once the animation has finished. So the player's window *is* the animation,
and it opens the instant that opcode first runs. `ANIME(47,1)` on channel 2
appears twice in the whole field and both are this attack.

So the module hooks **opcode 0x30**, installed only while `tvglen3` is loaded.
It cannot dedupe on the instruction pointer the way v0.42.0's password counter
does: `dragon::default` loops straight back to the *same* instruction for the
next attack, so two attacks in a row share a pointer. It uses the engine's own
answer instead — the `1 << [ctx+0x174]` bit in `[ctx+0x175]` that the dispatcher
sets for a starting instruction and that `0x00526810` itself tests to decide
whether to start the animation or poll one already running.

The cue is the Garden battle's **tone**, for the same reason that one is: the
block has to be a key already held when the check happens, so the useful signal
is "hold it now", which a rising two-note pair delivers in 180 ms and a sentence
does not. Health is reported in **hits** rather than points, because the bars
carry no numbers and hits are what is being decided. `/` reads both sides and
whether the block key is currently down.

It does not touch the fight: no input assist, no veto, nothing written. The
Garden battle needed an assist because its warning was 133 ms; here it is a whole
animation and the block is a plain hold. If the BAT says otherwise, the assist
belongs in a version with a measurement behind it.

---

New: `src/laguna_switch_model.inl`, `src/menu_tts_laguna_switch.inl`,
`src/dragon_fight_model.inl`, `src/field_minigame_dragon.inl`,
`tests/laguna_switch_compile.cpp`, `tests/dragon_fight_compile.cpp`.
Both probes decode their claims out of the shipped bytes — the module pool and
the offsets out of FF8_EN.exe, the fight out of `tvglen3.jsm`'s own dwords —
rather than restating the model. Mutations fail them 1 to 7 ways.
All twenty-three gates.

## v0.42.0

#103: **The password counter was counting frames — and SET TARGET answers in a
picture.**

Two things from the 2026-08-20 BAT of v0.41.0. The terminal itself was right:
the boot summary, "Running simulation" and its report, "Uploading… please wait"
and "Coordinate data uploaded." all read, and each label read once.

**The password counter counted the wrong thing.** v0.41.0 advanced the position
once per ASK/AASK *opcode firing*, on the assumption that an opcode fires once
per question. The log settles it: forty `[REPEAT]` lines in three seconds,
cycling "Letter 1 of 4" through "Letter 4 of 4" over and over while not one
letter had been entered, and the run-position line firing on every single one.
What was being counted was **frames**.

A blocking field opcode re-runs from the same instruction every frame, and the
engine's own dispatcher says so in four instructions (`0x0052A621`):

```
mov  cx, [esi + 0x176]        ; IP = dword index of THIS instruction
call [0x00B8DE94 + op*4]      ; the handler
test al, 2
je   +0x19                    ; <- skip the increment
inc  word ptr [esi + 0x176]   ; only advance when the handler says so
```

and AASK's waiting path (`0x00529755`, out of `execute_opcode_table[0x6F] =
0x005296C0`) is `mov eax, 5 / ret`. **5 & 2 == 0**, so while the dialog is up
the IP does not move and the same instruction fires again next frame.

So the discriminator is the **instruction pointer**, not the count of firings.
Same `(context, IP)` as last time is the same question still waiting for an
answer — say nothing, count nothing. A different IP means the script advanced.
Position is then *where that IP sits in the order the sites were first seen*,
which makes a retry come out right for free: a wrong password jumps back to the
first AASK, whose IP is already site 1, so it says "Letter 1 of 4" again rather
than "Letter 5 of 4". **Nothing about the four call sites is written down** —
the script's own addresses are the table.

`tests/repeat_prompt_compile.cpp` decodes all three fragments out of FF8_EN.exe
rather than trusting the paragraph above — both `[esi+disp32]` displacements are
decoded from the instruction bytes, and the `B8 imm32` in AASK's epilogue is read
and its bit 1 checked. Its fake VM contexts take the IP at the **literal** offset
`0x176`, because a fixture that wrote it through `REPEAT_PROMPT_IP_OFFSET` would
agree with the constant under test by construction. Mutations: counting firings
fails it **40** ways, a wrong offset **8**, ignoring the context **1**.

**And SET TARGET refuses in a picture.** Aaron: *"No announcement of the error
that appears when you try to set target."* `settarget::targetmenu` cursor 0 plus
confirm is `REQ(seigyo, 344)`, and script 344 — `seigyo::settargetselect` — is
forty-six dwords whose entire visible effect is `REQ(caution, 101)` / `WAIT 90`
/ `REQ(caution, 102)`: raise the CAUTION layer for ninety frames, take it down.
There is no window and no message — none of `gmmoni1.msd`'s thirty-five strings
is that text, because it is baked into the background graphic. So the player
picks the one item the scene is named after, the thing the party came here to
do, and the game answers silently. It now reads:

> Caution. Authorization required. This control panel is only available to the
> System Administrator or Commander Okamoto. Enter the password now, or you can
> not use this system.

Transcribed from the F11 capture, the same standing as the boot screen and the
simulation report: a layer with no branches behind it cannot say anything else.
Keyed on the **rising edge** of confirm with the submenu already open, because
`targetmenu` clears `var[1029]` *after* its blocking REQ rather than before it
(the main menu does the opposite) — confirm therefore stays 1 for the whole
eight seconds the layer is up, and a level test would fire on every frame of it.
The same edge is also how the mod learns the submenu opened at all, since it
opens with its cursor already at 0 and a player who confirms straight away moves
no cursor for the screen tracker to see.

Changed: `src/field_repeat_prompt.inl`, `src/field_dialog_scan.inl`,
`src/field_dialog_opcodes.inl`, `src/field_dialog_lifecycle.inl`,
`src/field_missile_terminal.inl`, `tests/repeat_prompt_compile.cpp`.
All twenty-one gates.

## v0.41.0

#102: **The Missile Base password — and the one path where it said nothing at
all.**

The password is not a keyboard. It is **four ordinary AASK choice dialogs in a
row**, all on one message (`gmtika4.msd` #23):

```
{3F}Please enter / your password.{3E} / A / B / C / D / E / F
```

`AASK(win 0, msg 23, firstLine 2, lastLine 7, default 2, cancel 2, 20, 20)` — so
the six choices are lines 2-7 and the value returned is the 0-based choice index.
The script (dwords 2189-2320) checks **4, 3, 4, 0** over A-F: **E, D, E, A**, the
password the Wounded Soldier gives once in message 19 before it starts.

AASK is already hooked, so the prompt and the six letters read. Two things were
missing.

**Position.** Four identical prompts with nothing to say which letter is being
entered. `src/field_repeat_prompt.inl` counts consecutive opcode-driven openings
of the same prompt and prefixes "Letter 1 of 4." … "Letter 4 of 4.". The count
comes from the script — four AASK calls — not from a guess, and a wrong password
restarts the run at one rather than counting on to "Letter 5 of 4".

**And on one path the mod said nothing whatsoever.** The four AASKs reuse the
same window without closing it, so the scanner sees the same prompt each time
with the cursor reset to the default — line 2, **"A"**. Its dedup is
`prompt == lastChoicePrompt && curChoice == lastSpokenChoice`, so **choosing A
for any letter makes the next prompt byte-for-byte the state it just spoke, and
it says nothing** — no prompt, no letter, no cue that a new entry has begun. The
password ends in **A**, so the last letter of the only password in the game hits
that path every time. The position line is now spoken on that branch too, which
is why the counter is a prefix owned by its own file rather than a tweak inside
the dedup.

**Scope.** It fires only for a `(field, prompt substring)` pair in a table — one
entry, `gmtika4` + "password" — and only when an ASK/AASK **opcode** fired, not
on the poll rescan, which would re-count the same dialog every frame. Every
other choice dialog in the game is untouched, and the probe checks that: the
same prompt on another field, an unrelated prompt on the same field, and no
field name at all all yield no prefix.

`tests/repeat_prompt_compile.cpp` drives four openings and the restart, and pins
that taking the prefix consumes it so it can never attach to a second utterance.
Three mutations — never resetting at the end, not consuming the prefix, dropping
the field scope — fail it one, two and three ways.

New: `src/field_repeat_prompt.inl`, `tests/repeat_prompt_compile.cpp`. The
`field_dialog.cpp` include chain is now ordered by dependency, with a note
saying so. All twenty-one gates.

BAT: this rides along with the terminal. At the control panel, the password
prompt should read "Letter 1 of 4" through "Letter 4 of 4" — and **A should
still speak**, which is the case that was silent.

## v0.40.1

#101: **The three silent screens — and the labels were being said twice.**

Aaron BAT'd the whole control panel. Everything the terminal *does* read
correctly (four main labels, the submenu, the percentage climbing 4 → 100 and
"maximum" at −150, both outcomes, the yes/no). Three screens said nothing:
the boot self-check, the simulation, and the upload progress bars.

**All three are background layers with baked-in text — there is no window to
read.** But all three are also *fixed*, and the scripts prove it:

```
script 336 (simulation)  153 dwords, 0 branches, 0 variable reads
script 359 (upload)       96 dwords, 0 branches, 0 variable reads
```

Not one conditional and not one variable between them, so neither screen can
vary with anything the player did. Aaron's own capture confirms it from the
other side: he ran the simulation with the error ratio at **100%** and the
report still read **"Error Ratio 65~80%"**. It is a canned demo, not a
calculation — which is what makes a fixed transcription honest here rather than
a guess, and the only reason these strings are allowed to be literals.

* **Boot screen** — spoken on entering the terminal: the ID/BIOS/memory/network/
  safety-unit check and "Welcome to HTMS".
* **Upload** — `control::uploader`'s Yes branch is `WINCLOSE / REQ(seigyo, 359) /
  if (var[484] & 1) var[484] |= 2 / var[1029] = 0`, and **that REQ blocks for the
  whole animation**, so `var[1029]` stays 1 for its entire duration — twenty-five
  seconds in the BAT. It is the one persistent signal either animation offers,
  and it now says "Uploading coordinate data to three units. Please wait."
* **Simulation** — here `var[1029]` is cleared *before* the REQ, so it is only a
  start signal. "Running simulation. Please wait." rides on that; the report is
  anchored instead to the game's own **"End simulation"** prompt, which is the
  one thing on that screen that is a real window and therefore the one moment
  the report is certainly on display. The same confirm both starts the run and
  dismisses it, so the end prompt being absent is what separates the two.

**And the menu labels are no longer spoken here.** v0.40.0 said them on the
theory that a readout depending on another subsystem catching the window works
by luck. The log settled it — `[AMES] win[1] Speaking: "SET TARGET"`,
`"CONFIRM EQUIPMENT"`, `"SIMULATION"`, `"EXIT"`, `"DATA UPLOAD"` on every cursor
move — so the second copy was redundant, and since AMES speaks with interrupt
while this file queues, the copy was being discarded anyway. The cursors are
still tracked, because they are what identifies the screen; only the speech is
gone, along with the `SnapshotWindowsAsSpoken` call it needed.

BAT: the terminal again. Boot summary on arrival, "Running simulation" then the
report, "Uploading… please wait" then "Coordinate data uploaded.", and each
label exactly once.

## v0.40.0

#101: **The Galbadia Missile Base terminal — five screens, and three of them
have no text at all.**

Aaron: *"there is a scene where the player must interact with a computer
terminal and set the error ratio to maximum."*

The terminal is field `gmmoni1`, and it is built entirely out of field entities
and background layers — no menu module is involved, which is why nothing in the
mod could see it. Every screen is a loop over **field variables** at
`0x01CFE9B8 + index`:

| screen (the script's own name) | cursor | address | values |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Director::default` — main menu | `var[1024]` | `0x01CFEDB8` | 0 Set target · 1 Confirm equipment · 2 Simulation · 3 Exit |
| `settarget::targetmenu` | `var[1025]` | `0x01CFEDB9` | 0 Set target · 1 Set error ratio · 2 Data upload · 3 Exit |
| `control::errorratioset` | `var[482]` **signed word** | `0x01CFEB9A` | 0 … −156, step 6 |
| `control::uploader` — the yes/no | `var[1028]` | `0x01CFEDBC` | 0 No · 1 Yes |
| `control::equipment` | `var[1028]` | `0x01CFEDBC` | 0–3 items · 4 exit |

**Cursor value equals message id on both menus** — each block ends in
`MES(win 1, msg n, 16, 160)` where n is the cursor — so the readout is a table
lookup and not an interpretation. `tests/missile_terminal_compile.cpp` proves it
the only way worth proving: it holds the **encoded bytes of messages 0–5 out of
`gmmoni1.msd`**, decodes them with the real decoder, and requires
`MAIN_LABELS[i]` to equal message *i* and `SUB_LABELS[i]` to equal message
`{0,4,5,3}[i]`. Reading that .msd with its first dword as a count instead of an
offset — the mistake that turns "SET TARGET" into "CONFIRM EQUIPMENT" — fails it.

**Three things have no text, which is what made the terminal unusable:**

* **the ratio bar** is a sprite position, 27 of them, with no number anywhere;
* **the upload yes/no** is two sprites lit by `upbyesno`, no window;
* **the outcome of confirming is silent.** `control::errorratioset` does
  `if (var[482] <= -150) var[484] |= 1;` and **otherwise nothing at all** — a
  refused ratio looks exactly like an accepted one. `control::uploader` does
  `if (var[484] & 1) var[484] |= 2;`, so choosing Yes before the ratio is set
  also does nothing, silently. And SET TARGET's EXIT refuses to leave until both
  bits are set.

So the mod reads the bar as a percentage (throttled to one readout per 250 ms,
because holding the button walks 27 positions — **except** the step that crosses
into acceptable, which is never throttled), says "maximum" the moment
`var[482] <= -150`, names the yes/no by **what confirming does** rather than by
a sprite it cannot see, and reports the outcome on leaving each screen by
comparing `var[484]` against what it was on entry — so a bit set on an earlier
visit is not claimed twice.

`/` reads back the screen, the value, and both progress flags. It is bound only
while `gmmoni1` is loaded, so it collides with nothing.

**Which screen owns `var[1028]`** is the one ambiguity: the uploader and the
equipment screen share it. A value of 2 or more settles it outright (the
uploader has two options); below that the path decides, since the uploader is
reached from SET TARGET item 2 and the equipment screen from main-menu item 1.

**One decoder change, and it is not cosmetic.** `0xAE`/`0xAF` are an emphasis
pair — `{AE}Save Point{AF}`, `{AE}CONFIRM EQUIPMENT{AF}` — blank in the Deling
grid because they draw no glyph. They were being counted as two *lost* bytes on
every such string, and `dropped` is exactly the signal a caller like the shop
reader uses to decide it is holding a fragment. They are now consumed silently,
the way colour and icon codes already are.

The reader is polled from the **top** of `PollWindows`, before the window scan,
and marks what it says as already-spoken — so the labels read deterministically
instead of depending on the scan happening to catch the window, and are never
said twice.

New: `src/missile_terminal_model.inl`, `src/field_missile_terminal.inl`,
`tests/missile_terminal_compile.cpp`. All twenty gates.

BAT: the Missile Base terminal. Walk the four main items, go into Set target,
set the error ratio to maximum (listen for the percentage climbing and for
"maximum"), upload the data, and try Exit before doing either so the refusals
read. `/` at any point should say where you are.

Worth reporting on the same trip: the **password** screen in `gmtika4` is four
ordinary AASK choice dialogs on "Please enter your password. A B C D E F"
(the answer is E, D, E, A), and AASK is already hooked — so it may already read.
If it does, the only thing missing is knowing which of the four letters you are
on.

## v0.39.0

#100: **"Move right" — and the audio description will stop talking over the
